### WF-0074 — push-only suite failures are invisible until they block a runtime PR, and a docs-only merge re-launders main's public-safety signal — **NEW; filed 2026-08-12 by NA-0717 (D-1353; text as amended at A1 §7, ruled R267/R271)**

Mechanism (source, 5b43eefe): the gate's first check reads main HEAD's public-safety check-run (public_safety_gate.py:1161-1176); the gate is invoked on a PR only when classify marks it runtime_critical or workflow_security (public-ci.yml:477); on push, the full-suite wait runs only for non-docs pushes (:505-506), so a docs-only push's public-safety check-run completes green unconditionally (:592-597) whatever the push-only suites' state. Measured cost, one week (NA-0717): `macos-qsc-full-serial` failed FIVE times over 7 days (a0b18d66→5b43eefe) before any lane noticed — notification was INEFFECTIVE here (default notification behavior unmeasured); 16 of 21 first-parent pushes were docs-only; docs PR #1724 re-greened a red main and admitted #1726. When main is red for a reason no profile covers, all three admission paths refuse every runtime-critical PR — until any docs merge re-greens the signal. NA-0717 used this door deliberately, on record, ONCE, for the cure (R269: PR-A). Design options for a future Director-scoped lane (named, not chosen): a PR-visible smoke subset of the serial suites · push-failure notification · profile-coverage policy · admission-path review · should docs merges relaunder main's health signal. Status: **PARTIALLY REMEDIED by D-1364 (NA-0728) and D-1365 (NA-0729), and OPEN on options 3-5.** Option 1 — the PR-visible smoke subset — is **TAKEN and landed**, and it cost one cargo line rather than a new job: the already-required `macos-qsc-qshield-build` was measured to run `cargo test -p qsc --locked` on every PR while omitting `--lib`, which is precisely where all five failures died (in an in-`src` `#[cfg(test)]` module no `--test` selector can reach), so the required macOS check had been **structurally blind** to the defect class. The decisive row: on `b845e678`, in the same workflow file, on the same runner pool and commit, `macos-qsc-qshield-build` concluded **success at 15:09:45Z** while `macos-qsc-full-serial` concluded **failure at 15:11:06Z**. Adding `--lib` costs no new macOS job, so the five-slot budget, `FANOUT_WAVES`, `MAX_CEILING` and `COVERAGE` are all untouched. Option 2 — push-failure notification — is **TAKEN and landed in REDUCED form at D-1365 (NA-0729)**, after the read it was held for. R315.2 had ordered an SR-15 read on it (on Director's discretion, **not** on a mechanical trigger — all three measured negative) because it would be the first workflow in this repo that writes automatically to a **public** surface, and because `infra-literal-scan` examines repo files, not runtime-generated issue bodies, so the existing net does not cover it. R315.3 split the lane so the measured, low-risk half was not held hostage to the unread half. **The read returned 2 BLOCKER and 4 MAJOR findings and R318 refused the frozen bytes while ratifying the capability class**, so what landed is the reduced form: the auto-close arm DELETED (replayed against the occasion it opened five issues and closed all five within 1h37m-19h50m, every closing run a docs-only merge that ran zero macOS tests — the alarm erased by the very laundering the second half of this entry's title describes), the branch guard TYPED against `head_repository` because `head_branch == 'main'` also matches a fork's default branch and a passing fork run would have CLOSED a true alarm, and de-duplication re-keyed off the mutable public title onto an immutable body marker plus the `ci-red` label. ⚠ R319 additionally closes the net's hole this entry named: `scripts/ci/sentinel_body_selftest.py` renders the issue body from the workflow's own bytes against adversarial fixtures and runs `infra-literal-scan`'s own needles over the result, watched RED before GREEN, so what the body omits is held by a gate instead of by a comment. ⚠ Options 3, 4 and 5 — profile-coverage policy, admission-path review, and whether a docs merge should relaunder main's health signal — are **untouched, and the second half of this entry's own title still stands**: a docs-only merge still re-greens main's public-safety signal. ⚠ **P2 of that occasion is now measured and the answer changed the remedy class:** the gap was never "no signal" — over a 21h55m window the notification stream carried **250 notifications, all of reason `ci_activity`, 226 "succeeded" against 11 "failed"**, so a failure arrives at **1 in 22**. It is a signal nobody sees, which is why selectivity plus a durable in-repo artifact is the shape, and why a settings toggle alone cannot be the remedy.

### WF-0076 — suites approach their ceilings silently: nothing warns before a timeout kill, so a ceiling expires instead of being re-fitted — **NEW; filed 2026-08-13 by NA-0719 (D-1355; ordered with the R278 ceiling correction)**

Both push-only suite ceilings were fitted honestly to measurements (NA-0664's method, the basis comments in the files) and then aged out in silence: `macos-qsc-full-serial` was killed at 100% of its 180-minute ceiling on two consecutive all-green executions (runs 31643260667 and 31661853338, banked in the NA-0717 lane record — the second was the run proving the NA-0717 fix on main), and `qsc-linux-full-suite` sits at ~91% of its 240 across five consecutive banked main runs. The kill decided the schedule where a measurement should have. Proposed remedy (named, not built): the suite jobs emit measured runtime vs ceiling at completion; a check WARNS at ≥80% and FAILS a ceiling-review obligation at ≥90% — at current figures that would have signaled macOS three weeks before the first kill and names Linux today. Related but distinct from ENG-0120 (the monolith's growth itself) and from the operator-ratified demote-after-three-green-lanes plan, both unaltered. Status: **FOLDED IN BY D-1360 (NA-0724)** — `qsc_shard_check.py --ratchet SECONDS CEILING_MINUTES --ratchet-arm ARM`, called at the end of each shard step on both platforms from the wall-clock the step already prints. **WF-0076's own 80 % / 90 % thresholds are UNALTERED**; only which arm may turn them into an exit code changed. Watched both ways on both arms: 18.5 % quiet rc 0, 81.5 % WARN rc 0, 90.7 % on `push` **WARN naming the suppressed FAIL** rc 0, 90.7 % on `pull_request` **FAIL rc 1**, and omitting `--ratchet-arm` fails closed. ⚠ **Why the push arm only warns:** the repair for suite GROWTH is a ceiling re-fit, i.e. an edit to `.github/workflows/**`, which classifies `workflow_security` — exactly the class every admission path refuses while main is red. **Alarm and freeze must not share a trigger.** ⚠ **NAMED CONSEQUENCE, so no successor mistakes a quiet ratchet for an enforced one: post-merge the macOS ratchet can only ever WARN** (the macOS shards do not run on ordinary PRs), so its FAIL arm is exercised exactly once, on NA-0724's own PR; **the Linux FAIL arm stays live** because the Linux shards run on every PR. The current Linux headroom is 37.8 % and the projected macOS worst shard 54.5 %, both far below the warn line. Status: folded in by D-1360; the alarm is live, its macOS enforcement arm is not. ⚠ **RE-SCOPED by D-1364 (NA-0728, ordered at R314.4) to name the CAUSE rather than the symptom, because a successor inheriting "the enforcement arm is not live" cannot act on it and a successor inheriting the reason can.** Both thresholds re-verified at source at spine main `fbcf2869` and **UNALTERED**: `RATCHET_WARN_PCT = 80.0` and `RATCHET_FAIL_PCT = 90.0` (`scripts/ci/qsc_shard_check.py:123-124`), with `RATCHET_SUPPRESSED_ARM = "push"` (`:125`) and `--ratchet-arm` carrying no default and failing closed when omitted (`:485-490`) — so the bands behave exactly as filed. **The macOS ≥90 % FAIL arm is unreachable because the macOS shard job's `pull_request` arm is gated on `startsWith(github.head_ref, 'na0724-')` (`.github/workflows/macos-qsc-sharded-suite.yml:141-144`, and the aggregate carries the same guard at `:199-202`) and NA-0724 is CLOSED — no future branch matches that prefix, so the guard is dead and the FAIL arm fired exactly once, on that lane's own PR.** Reaching it again requires a decision about that guard, which is the sharding arrangement's business and not WF-0076's. ⚠ **NA-0728 does NOT advance this entry**: its edit set touches `.github/workflows/macos-build.yml`, which invokes `qsc_shard_check.py` nowhere, so no ratchet runs there — said plainly so the lane is not read as fixing more than it did. A ratchet call on the `macos-qsc-qshield-build` job was considered and **not taken**: it would protect that job's own 45-minute ceiling, not the 90-minute shard ceilings this entry is about.

### ENG-0185 — the push-arm public-safety wrapper's single-job poll cannot cover the honest suite ceilings on a hosted runner — **NEW; filed 2026-08-13 by NA-0721 (D-1357; text as written at NA-0717 STOP 011 §3, landed byte-verbatim by the door-2 closeout-records errand)**

The wrapper derives its watchdog coverage from the suite ceilings (`COVERAGE = MAX_CEILING + 60m queue margin`) and refuses when coverage exceeds its own budget minus a 20m gap. With honest ceilings (300/330, fitted to measured 206.5m/229m runs) coverage = 390m, but the job runs on ubuntu-latest where GitHub terminates hosted jobs at 360 EXECUTION minutes regardless of declared timeout-minutes — so no declarable budget can cover 390m: `ERROR: derived watchdog coverage 390m exceeds the safe bound 340m` (main push on f54d3b82, job 94366916007, log banked NA-0717). The guard is CORRECT (it refused rather than hang into ENG-0052); the architecture is the defect: a single polling job cannot outlive the suites it waits for. Remedy ruled to its own gate lane (R282): retire the poll — the push arm keeps fast checks; a workflow_run-completion job posts the public-safety check-run when BOTH suites conclude for the sha. SR-15 mandatory. Status: **ARITHMETIC CURE LANDED by D-1360 (NA-0724); the ARCHITECTURAL remedy remains open.** R289 amended R282 on measurement: sharding the two push suites moves MAX_CEILING under 280 without a redesign. Measured by executing the consumer's own sizing block against the edited tree: shard ceilings 90/90, FANOUT_WAVES 3, `MAX_CEILING 270 <= 280`, `COVERAGE 330 <= 340`, rc 0 — against 330/390/rc 2 at base. The guard was watched REFUSING first (counterfactual ceiling 150 => COVERAGE 510, rc 2) and its refusal boundary measured exactly (94 => 342 red; 93 => 339 green), so **93 is the largest admissible shard ceiling** and a re-fit to 94+ reds main post-merge with no pre-merge detection (the sizing step is push-only). ⚠ **FANOUT_WAVES 3 is the ceiling of the arithmetic path** — 4 x 90 = 360 > 280 — so if a fourth wave is ever needed the arithmetic is spent and **R282's workflow_run redesign becomes NECESSARY rather than deferred**; the measured escalation trigger is `wait_for_required_checks` rc 2 WITH `transient_poll_errors=0` AND a final iteration printing `status=in_progress` (the other two rc-2 causes are API flake and a check that never existed). **R282 is NOT withdrawn.** This entry stays open on the architecture.

⚠⚠ **A THIRD MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, added 2026-08-15 by NA-0734 (D-1370; ordered at R332.2) — and it is FORWARD-FACING, not historical. No WF is minted** (WF-0029 precedent: the finding already exists; only the consequence is new). Main's `public-safety` is a **polling job** that waits on the push-only full suites, and on the `6f6b72e9` push it waited **52m08s** (16:08:35Z → 17:00:43Z) on the macOS shards. ⇒ **Any `runtime_critical` or `workflow_security` PR opened inside that window reaches step 15 — *"Block relevant PRs when latest main public-safety is red unless the PR clears live advisories"* — against an **UNSETTLED** main, and fails for a reason that has nothing to do with itself.** Measured on PR **#1749**: step 15 ran at **16:58:16Z** and read `main sha=6f6b72e9 check=public-safety status=in_progress conclusion=None`; main completed **`success` 2m27s later**. `check_main_public_safety` passes **only** on `completed`+`success`, so **an in-flight main is indistinguishable from a red one at that seam**, and the bounded admission paths correctly refuse a PR that never claimed them. ⚠ **Earlier lanes missed this purely by timing** — #1748 merged 35 minutes before #1749 opened, so main was already settled for every previous promotion. ⚠⚠ **It will RECUR and get worse: Slice 4 is runtime-class PR after runtime-class PR**, so the window stops being an edge case and becomes the normal case. **This is a further argument for R282's redesign — retire the poll; post the check-run from a `workflow_run`-completion job when both suites conclude for the sha — not a new defect.** ⚠ The remedy applied at the time was a **re-run of the `public-safety` job alone**, authorized at R332.1 against a three-condition test that is recorded here so it cannot become a loophole: **(a)** the failure's own log NAMES an external input; **(b)** that input's value has MEASURABLY changed; **(c)** the check RE-READS that input on every execution. **All three, or the answer is no** — and the re-run must then be verified to pass FOR THE RIGHT REASON from the step list, not merely to pass. Last lane: NA-0734 (D-1370). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

⚠⚠ **A LOG LINE FROM THAT SAME STEP THAT READS AS A MISCONFIGURATION AND IS NOT ONE — recorded here, where a reader will meet it (added 2026-08-15 by NA-0734, D-1370; ordered at R332.3).** When step 15 refuses, its log emits `ERROR: branch protection required checks do not include public-safety`. **That claim is FALSE as a standalone statement** — measured live against `branches/main/protection/required_status_checks/contexts`, **`public-safety` IS among main's 15 required contexts.** It fires only because its **sibling fires first**: `ERROR: branch protection required checks are unreadable (HTTP 403); cannot verify required PR checks` — the workflow token cannot read branch protection, so the gate's `required_contexts` list is **empty**, and a membership test against an empty list necessarily fails. ⚠ **A successor reading that line cold would reasonably conclude the gate is misconfigured and go hunting a defect that does not exist.** Same 403 shape NA-0716 investigated and concluded *"was never the wall"*; it is not the wall here either. ⚠ Two further lines in that refusal are also diagnostics rather than findings — `queue proof does not show exactly one READY item` and `target PR changes paths outside active READY scope` — both belong to the red-main-repair admission profile, which the PR never claimed. **Read the refusal's decisive line, not its line count.** Last lane: NA-0734 (D-1370). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

### ENG-0186 — P2 — the red-main-repair MARKER admission arm is INERT under a sharded push suite — **NEW; filed 2026-08-13 by NA-0724 (D-1360; ordered at R295's F2 cure, which RESCINDED the Director's own T8(b) "behavior-preserving" premise)**

`validate_red_main_repair_evidence` requires every profile marker to appear in the job log of the check named by `failure_check` (`public_safety_gate.py:824-827`), and `build_live_red_main_repair_evidence` fetches exactly that one log (`:972-977`, via `github_job_log_text`) — both anchors re-verified at the edit, where the file's diff is 16 insertions / 16 deletions and therefore shifts no line. ### WF-0077 — the `**Class:**` result-class field fell out of the decision record for twenty consecutive decisions, and an undocumented inline form partly replaced it — **NEW; filed 2026-08-14 by NA-0725 (D-1361; deferred at D-1359 DV-3, measured as TWENTY at R297.2, reserved by R297.5 until NA-0724 was proven post-merge, released at R302)**

Measured at spine main `324f076b`: **D-1340 through D-1359 — twenty consecutive decisions, all present, zero gaps — carry no `**Class:**` field**, which is the house form for a result class (the token inline after `**Base:**`, its value backticked; last instances D-1338 and D-1339). The last decision to declare one in that field is **D-1339**, and **D-1360 ends the drift** by declaring `SUITE_ECONOMICS_SHARDING_PASS` (R297.3), so the range is closed and exact rather than open-ended. ⚠ **The drift is in the FIELD, not uniformly in the practice, and that distinction is the finding:** four of the twenty declare a result class in an *undocumented inline form* — **D-1340** `QSL_OUTPUT_IPC_BOUNDARY_CLOSURE_PASS`, **D-1341** `QSLD_GUI_INPUT_DRIVER_PASS` and **D-1342** `QSLD_ERASE_ERROR_ONE_RESIZING_WRITER_PASS`, each written as ``Class `NAME` `` inside the decision's own Date/Lane metadata bullet, plus **D-1344** `QSLD_QSC_PIN_BUMP_QSCV01_REFUSAL_PASS` written as `Class at close:` — so the field did not merely lapse; a second, ungoverned spelling partly replaced it, and the remaining sixteen declare none in any form. Three further inline `class `-shaped hits inside the range (D-1343, D-1344, D-1346) name a **different** lane's class in a retirement note and are correctly not counted. ⚠ **Instrument note, carried because this measurement is easy to get wrong in both directions:** a naive `grep '\*\*Class:\*\*' DECISIONS.md` **over-counts** — it returns **15 hits at `324f076b`**, where R297 recorded **12** at `f8370bce` (D-1360's merge added three: one real declaration plus two inside its own column-0 fence) — and the hit it attributes to `## D-1359` is **not a declaration** but D-1359's own DV-3 prose *code-quoting the token* while describing this very measurement: a needle wider than its claim. The decisive instrument excludes column-0 fenced regions (this record carries whole ruling documents in them, the D-1356/D-1359 precedent) and excludes code-quoted mentions: `**Class:**` occurrences within D-1340..D-1359 = **1**, of which code-quoted = **1**, therefore **zero declaration-shaped fields**, against a **positive control of 10** over D-1330..D-1339 proving the needle can fire. ⚠ Two governing documents cite **eleven** (D-1359 DV-3 over D-1348..D-1358, and R296.5) — each true of the range it named, each honestly scoped to its own act — so **a cited enumeration is not the maximal one; measure it.** **Recommended change: none decided here — but the question is not the one the drift first looks like.** ⚠⚠ Because a second, ungoverned spelling **partly replaced** the field rather than the field simply lapsing, *"revive or retire `**Class:**`"* is the wrong framing: a remedy must decide **which spelling is canonical**, **what becomes of the four decisions written in the other one**, and whether either is enforced by a lint over `DECISIONS.md`. This entry exists so that call is made against a measurement rather than an impression (**R303.1**). ⚠ Note for whoever takes it: **D-1361, this filing's own decision, DOES declare a result class** — `RECORDS_SEAT_PROVISIONING_PASS`, in the `**Class:**` field, ruled at **R303.2** after the lane stopped rather than invent one — so the filing does not extend the lapse it records, and declaring in the field prejudges nothing about which spelling the remedy adopts. ⚠ **Related — and this is the sentence to read first if you are reading both entries: `WF-0029`** (the workspace `user.email` hazard, filed 2026-07-22 by NA-0666 / D-1292) **is not a duplicate of anything this lane filed, and is not closed by it.** The ledger has carried that **FINDING** since 2026-07-22; what was missing was the **STEP**, which NA-0725 landed in `START_HERE.md` §4 Step 1 (*Bootstrap*) rather than as a new entry here. WF-0029's bytes are untouched and it keeps its own status. Status: open — FILING ONLY. Originating/last lane: NA-0725 (D-1361). Last-updated: 2026-08-14.

### WF-0079 — SR-15's escalation threshold turns on "source files", a term the governance spine never defines — **NEW; filed 2026-08-14 by NA-0728 (D-1364; ordered at R315.1)**

`docs/ops/STANDING_RULES.md:79` escalates any directive that "exceeds five source files" to an adversarial second read, and **nothing in the spine defines what a source file is.** Measured at spine main `fbcf2869`: the string's only normative occurrence is SR-15's own text; every other occurrence across the record means **code** (`"the alternative fix touches 236 source files"`, `"the two qsc source files"`, `"a scratch source file"`, `"no source files were changed"`), and NA-0724's own edit-set arithmetic separated **"10 code"** from **"the 6-file governance bundle"**. The gap is not theoretical: **one edit set in this lane admitted three defensible counts — 2 (code/workflow), 4 (code plus spine-process docs), 8 (every file) — straddling the threshold**, so the same directive both did and did not trigger a mandatory read depending on a reading the rule never supplies. R315.1 ruled the narrow reading correct on that evidence, which settles this instance and not the rule. ⚠ **The hazard is that the ambiguity resolves in whichever direction suits the lane doing the counting**, and the lane is the party with the least standing to choose; the only reason it did not resolve that way here is that the lane referred it rather than taking it, which is a discipline and not a mechanism. ### ENG-0188 — the two nightly relay workflows have failed every run for 187 days, and they do NOT share a cause: an untrusted relay CA stops `remote-relay-tests` only, and only since 2026-08-14 — the newest of three sequential causes — while `remote-handshake-tests` fails locally at `peer_identity_key_missing` before any network act — **filed 2026-08-14 by NA-0728 (D-1364; observation measured in-lane, cause supplied by the Director at R315 and CORRECTED at R316 after the operator challenged the mechanism); FIGURE AND CAUSE-STRUCTURE CORRECTED 2026-08-15 by NA-0730 (D-1366; ordered at R325.4); M6 MEASURED LIVE AND ITS HAZARD CORRECTED 2026-08-15 by NA-0731 (D-1367; R328.3)**

- Severity: **P2** (no runtime, protocol or security defect in the shipped client — the trust policy behaving as designed is the *cause* of the relay half only; the defect is that two scheduled instruments have been dark for **187 days at `50bb5703`** and nothing said so)
- Status: open — **partly discharged by NA-0730 (D-1366)**: the relay half's newest cause is remedied (a CA secret is staged and a preflight proves trust *in the job log*), and `remote-relay-tests` is expected to go green. **The handshake half is deliberately NOT repaired** — its cause is unrelated and no CA can fix it; that repair is **ENG-0189**'s own script-only lane. ⚠ The relay fix discharges the NEWEST of three sequential causes only; whether a fourth waits behind it is unknown until a run gets past TLS.

**THE OBSERVATION, measured in this lane at `fbcf2869`.** `remote-handshake-tests` and `remote-relay-tests` have each concluded `failure` on **all 60 of their most recent runs**, zero successes — every one on `main`, and both are red now. ⚠⚠ **THE FIGURE DERIVED FROM THAT SENTENCE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE (NA-0730, R325.4).** The measured sentence — *"all 60 of their most recent runs"* — was accurate. The inference drawn from it — *"120 consecutive failures … spanning 2026-06-24 through 2026-08-14 (51 days)"* — was not: **60 is `gh run list`'s default PAGE SIZE, not the population**, and 51 days is merely how far 60 nightly runs reach back. **A paginated API's default page was read as a duration.** Re-measured at `50bb5703` over a 200-run window per workflow: `remote-relay-tests` **195 consecutive failures at head at `50bb5703`**, last success run `21812862848` on **2026-02-09T04:54:00Z**; `remote-handshake-tests` **197 at `50bb5703`**, last success run `21813215809` on **2026-02-09T05:12:26Z** ⇒ **392 consecutive failures over 187 days at `50bb5703`**, not 120 over 51 — an occasion ~3.7× longer than the one recorded. *(Same family as R324.2 and R304.3: a count is scoped to the QUERY that produced it and is written base-scoped, so **state the window with the count, always**.)* Both are `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only: neither runs on `pull_request`, neither is among main's fifteen required contexts, and neither is in the public-safety watchdog's `--required` set, **so nothing in the program could see them**. Both fail at the same place — the smoke-script step — *after* `Build qsc (locked)` succeeds, which is why a build-side reading of the failure was never available.

⚠⚠ **THE STREAK IS NOT ONE FAILURE REPEATED — IT DECOMPOSES INTO THREE SEQUENTIAL CAUSES, AND THE CA IS ONLY THE NEWEST (NA-0730, measured at `50bb5703` by downloading artifacts run by run).** `remote-relay-tests`: `contacts_store_invalid` — dying **before any network act** — in the oldest non-expired artifact (2026-05-17); then `qsc_error=relay_inbox_push_failed` with `diagnostic_class=dns_timeout` across six identical runs from 2026-08-09 **through 2026-08-14T04:40Z**, the old endpoint having stopped resolving; then `qsc_error=relay_tls_untrusted` from **2026-08-15T03:28Z** onward. **Transition evidence from a second, independent surface:** the repository secrets' `updated_at` — `RELAY_URL` **2026-08-14T23:03:49Z**, `RELAY_TOKEN` **2026-08-14T23:08:56Z** (names and timestamps only; no value was read) — falls **exactly between** the last `dns_timeout` run and the first `relay_tls_untrusted` run, so the CA failure began when the secrets were repointed at the new relay. ⇒ **each earlier cause was SUPERSEDED, not fixed**, and pinning the CA discharges the newest layer only. ⚠ **A coarse instrument was blind to precisely this**: artifact metadata survives expiry, so artifact *size* looked like a cheap complete probe for "did the cause change" — it showed **no change** (4666–4670 B) straight across the transition. **Size discriminates "died at a different point", never "died for a different reason."**

⚠⚠ **AND THE TWO WORKFLOWS DO NOT SHARE A CAUSE — SEE ENG-0189.** `remote-handshake-tests` fails at `hs_init` with `reason=peer_identity_key_missing`, **before any network act**; a needle for every TLS/relay error class over its whole artifact returns **ZERO**. The CA paragraph below is therefore true of `remote-relay-tests` **only**. ⚠ **A green `remote-handshake-tests` would falsify this and is a STOP, not a bonus.**

**THE CAUSE OF THE RELAY HALF, supplied at R315 and corrected at R316, so a successor does not re-derive it.** `relay_http_client()` composes trust roots **ADDITIVELY**: the webpki/Mozilla roots and the OS trust store are **NEVER disabled** — the function deliberately does not call `tls_built_in_root_certs(false)`, and that absence is the webpki-continuity pin — and an operator CA is **ADDED** when configured (`QSC_RELAY_CA_FILE` → `RELAY_CA_FILE` → vault secret). A configured-but-unloadable CA is a hard error; it never silently proceeds. **Neither nightly workflow configures a CA file** — measured: `RELAY_URL` and `RELAY_TOKEN` are the only secrets referenced anywhere under `.github/` — and the endpoint presents a certificate that chains to no public root, so **verification fails correctly** and the suites cannot pass until a CA is pinned. ⇒ **Not a dead destination, not a bad token, and not a client that refuses public roots: no CA is configured for an endpoint that needs one.** ⚠ **The endpoint's address, host, port and hosting arrangement are deliberately NOT recorded here** — operator infrastructure details are never written into repo truth; the class is what a successor needs and the class is what this entry carries. ⚠ **This mechanism sentence was wrong in its first drafting and is recorded as corrected rather than silently replaced**: the earlier text said the client "trusts only pinned CAs", which read a code comment *naming* `tls_built_in_root_certs(false)` as evidence the function *calls* it, when the comment exists precisely to record that it does not (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/transport/mod.rs:2095-2125`). ⚠ **The tree could have refuted it before it was ever written** — `NEXT_ACTIONS.md`'s NA-0663 record already stated the true mechanism, *"UNION with the baked-in webpki roots"* and *"the explicit ADDITIVE CA-file option"* — and it was not consulted. The correction was prompted by the operator challenging the claim, which is the instrument that fired here.

**Remedy sketch (NOT implemented; its own lane).** Supply the trust anchor to both workflows through the existing `RELAY_CA_FILE` path as a repository secret, then prove the fix by watching a run go green that is red at base — a nightly that has failed **195 times in a row at `50bb5703`** is an unusually well-controlled starting point, and **a green with no watched red proves only that something changed**. ⚠ **Two constraints the successor must weigh BEFORE pointing unattended nightly load at the relay**, both named at R315: the relay runs on a small free-tier box, and there is an ENG-0186-adjacent `max_body_bytes` hazard. ⚠ **Sequencing: these two workflows ARE the first half of the nightly endurance window already on the roadmap**, so whoever repairs them is doing that work — plan the lanes as one rather than as two.

**THE CAUSE, grounded in source.** `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs:1432-1444` (at `50bb5703`) records the NA-0633 / ENG-0038 C1 decision: the initiator loads the peer's **pinned identity KEM key** and encapsulates to it so the responder must prove KEM-secret possession, and *"a contact without the full key (legacy/incomplete) fails closed here — no fallback to the unauthenticated path."* The smoke script adds contacts with **`--fp <fingerprint>` only** (`qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh:307-312`) and never transfers the peer's identity KEM key. **Attribution is exact:** `git log -S peer_identity_key_missing` → commit **`eaf39aa4`, 2026-07-11T07:21Z** ("NA-0633 Phase 2 (core fix): C1 responder-authentication"); the cause bisect shows `relay_inbox_push_failed` on 2026-07-05 and `peer_identity_key_missing` from **2026-07-12 onward — the first nightly after that merge** — unchanged through the endpoint migration and unchanged through the secret repoint, for **35 days at `50bb5703`**.

**THE REPAIR, fully specified so the successor lane does not re-derive it — script-only, no product change.** `contacts add` already accepts `--kem-pk <hex>` and `--sig-pk <hex>` (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/cmd/mod.rs:437-445`, documented for exactly this purpose); the values are already printed by `identity rotate` as `identity_kem_pk=` / `identity_sig_pk=` (`lib.rs:267`, `:357`) and are already present in the uploaded artifacts; and the script already carries the extraction idiom (`extract_identity_fp`). ⚠ **The acceptance criterion is INVERTED until this lands** (R325.2): while ENG-0189 is open, a **green** `remote-handshake-tests` falsifies this entry and is a **STOP**, not a bonus — it would mean the attribution above is wrong. Cross-reference: ENG-0188; ENG-0190; NA-0633; D-1366; R325.2; R325.3. Originating/last lane: NA-0730 (D-1366). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

It was written before anyone knew a **fourth cause** sat behind this one, and it set the wrong bar — **this entry's defect is `peer_identity_key_missing`, and that defect is measurably gone.** Post-merge dispatch of `remote-handshake-tests` at `ea5bb95f` (run `31898549150`): `peer_identity_key_missing` appears **0 times in the job log (58898 bytes / 760 lines)** and **0 times in the artifact (8 files, 25022 bytes)**, against **0 and 4** on the pre-fix run. `$out/markers` grew **20 → 50** lines, the artifact **16922 → 25022** bytes, `event=handshake_reject` fell **1 → 0** and `event=error` **1 → 0**, and the **full four-message handshake completes on both sides** (`handshake_complete role=initiator` at `hs_poll_2`, `handshake_complete role=responder peer_confirmed=yes` at `hs_poll_3`). ⚠ **The single most direct evidence is `resp_kem_ct_len=1088` on message A1**: that ciphertext exists **only because the initiator had the peer's identity KEM key to encapsulate to** — the exact absence this entry describes. ⚠ **The suite remains RED for a different, OLDER cause, filed as ENG-0191**, which this lane deliberately did not touch. ### ENG-0190 — the diagnosis defect: both remote smoke workflows hide every `qsc` error inside an uploaded artifact, so the job log carries a symptom and never a cause — **this, not TLS, is why 187 days passed** — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0730 (D-1366; §7 F-2); SHARPENED 2026-08-15 by NA-0731 (D-1367; R328.2) — a second measured instance, and the more extreme one**

- Severity: **P2** (no defect in the shipped client; a diagnosability defect in the instruments — and the one that made a 187-day outage survivable)
- Status: open — **partly mitigated, for trust failures only**, by the preflight NA-0730 adds to both workflows; the general defect is untouched.

**MEASURED at `50bb5703`.** Latest relay run `31861928563`, job `94956721494`, log fetched with `--allow-escape-sequences`, **53529 bytes printed** (the byte count is the only tell against the empty-file trap). Steps 1–4 `success`, step 5 `Run remote relay smoke` **failure**, step 6 upload `success`. The **entire** failure text in the job log is two lines: `counts failed happy-path expectations` and `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` — that is `qsc_remote_relay_smoke.sh:326`, a **symptom** (`deliver_count == 0`). Both smoke scripts redirect every `qsc` invocation into files under `$out` and only `cat` them into per-step **files**, so the cause reaches the uploaded artifact and never the log. ⇒ **A reader of the check mark — or of the entire job log — cannot learn why.** For 187 days nobody could, and the three distinct causes behind that streak (ENG-0188) were indistinguishable from one another at every surface a human actually reads.

⚠ **The general remedy is NOT the preflight.** NA-0730's preflight makes *trust* failures legible and nothing else; a fourth cause would be exactly as opaque as the first three. The remedy this entry asks for is that a failing smoke step **emit the decisive marker lines to stdout** as well as to `$out` — bounded, and subject to the design constraint that `$out` is uploaded **publicly**, so whatever is echoed must be class-only (see WF-0083). Cross-reference: ENG-0188; ENG-0189; WF-0083; D-1366; R325.1. Originating/last lane: NA-0730 (D-1366). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

EXTREME ONE. NOT DISCHARGED.** R325.2 set as its acceptance that the handshake suite's cause would be
*"now VISIBLE in the job log"* once the preflight landed. Measured after #1746 merged:
`peer_identity_key_missing` appears **ZERO** times in that job log, and the smoke step's **entire**
output is `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1` — **worse than the state this entry
documented**, since the relay script at least printed a symptom (`counts failed happy-path
expectations`). ⚠ **R328.2 rules this the Director's own error, not a shortfall in execution**: the
ruling assumed a legibility cure would extend to a failure it never covered. **This entry's own text
was right as written** — it says in terms that the preflight makes trust failures legible *and
nothing else* — so what overreached was the acceptance criterion, not the finding.
⚠⚠ **The property, which is the transferable part: a remedy's scope is set by what it INSTRUMENTS,
not by what a ruling hopes it reaches.** ⇒ **ENG-0190 is SHARPENED, not discharged**, and reporting
three-of-four rather than scoring a pass is the reason the surrounding record is worth trusting.
⚠ The entry keeps **no `Resolution:` line**: the partial-closure rule is the load-bearing half, and
this finding is not merely open — it just got worse. Cross-reference: D-1367; R328.2; ENG-0189.

⚠⚠ **MEASURED 2026-08-15 by NA-0733 (D-1369) — A MEASUREMENT, NOT A REMEDY. STILL NOT DISCHARGED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** NA-0733 was the only lane that would hold both a failing and a passing run of this suite, so its order required it to capture what this entry's successor would otherwise have to re-derive — and forbade it from making the fix. **The two surfaces of the pre-fix run** (`31872524157`, job `94983257654`, head `04affcc9`): the JOB LOG carries `peer_identity_key_missing` **0 times in 58832 bytes / 759 lines** (the byte count is the only tell against the empty-file trap — `gh api …/logs` needs `--allow-escape-sequences`), while the uploaded ARTIFACT carries it **4 times in 16922 bytes across 8 files** — twice in `happy-path/alice.log` and twice in `happy-path/markers`. **The failing step's entire job-log output** is GitHub's own `##[group]Run …` echo of the step body and env (lines 706–719) followed immediately by `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` (line 720), with **nothing between them** across 19.2 s of execution. ⚠ **CHECK, DON'T COUNT** (R328.4): a reader counting lines in that region would report five lines of script output — they are the runner's echo, not the script's, which emitted **zero**. **THE SPECIFIC REDIRECTION, named by file and line** (`scripts/demo/qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh`, numbering as of D-1369): **`:194` — `) >"$tmp" 2>&1`** is the redirection, sending every `qsc` invocation's stdout *and* stderr to a file; `:156` places that file inside `$out`, the artifact root; `:198` `cat`s it into `$out/alice.log` / `$out/bob.log`; and `:200` / `:202` route the very `QSC_MARK/1` lines that carry the reason into `$out/markers`. ⚠ `:343` calls `hs_init` **bare** rather than through `run_required_qsc_step`, so under `set -euo pipefail` (`:2`) the non-zero return kills the script **with no message at all** — the second half of the answer, and the reason the log is not merely uninformative but *empty*. The sibling `scripts/demo/qsc_remote_relay_smoke.sh:166` / `:170` carries the identical construct, so the successor has **two sites, not one**. **THE MINIMAL CHANGE THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE CAUSE VISIBLE, stated as a measurement and NOT MADE:** one line inside `run_qsc_step`, between the marker extraction (`:203`) and `return "$rc"` (`:205`), guarded by `[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]`, echoing to stdout the `QSC_MARK/1` lines it has just extracted. ⚠ **WF-0083's public-upload constraint is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the part worth recording**: those exact bytes are already uploaded publicly in `$out/markers`, so echoing them introduces no disclosure class that does not already exist — the design constraint this entry names as bounding the remedy turns out not to bind at that seam. Measured effect: `peer_identity_key_missing` would have gone from **0 occurrences in a 58832-byte job log to at least one.** ⚠ **A THIRD INSTANCE, measured free and stronger than the two already recorded:** in **both** halves of NA-0733's local A/B — the failing run and the repaired one — the script emitted **0 bytes** to stdout and stderr. **The invisibility is independent of which cause fires**, which is the argument for fixing it once at `run_qsc_step` rather than per-cause. ⚠ **No `Resolution:` line is added and none is earned:** nothing here changes the instruments, and the entry is left exactly as open as it was. | `31898549150` (post-fix, `ea5bb95f`) | `assert_marker_present`, which does `echo "$msg" >&2` | **`alice handshake status is not established`**, then `##[error]` |

⇒ **Failures routed through `assert_marker_present` / `run_required_qsc_step` are ALREADY LEGIBLE; failures routed through a bare `run_qsc_step` are SILENT.** ⚠ **The post-fix run is the first time in over 35 days that this suite's job log named its own cause — and no instrument changed.** The visibility moved because the failure moved. ⚠ **This narrows the remedy precisely:** the one-line change named in `## D-1369` — an `rc != 0`-guarded echo inside `run_qsc_step`, between the marker extraction and `return "$rc"` — covers exactly the silent class and nothing else, and WF-0083's public-upload constraint is satisfied **by construction** because those bytes are already uploaded publicly in `$out/markers`. ⚠ **Still a measurement, not a remedy: no change was made.** ⚠ A reader should also note the corollary for the sibling `qsc_remote_relay_smoke.sh`, whose `:166`/`:170` carry the identical construct — **two sites, and the same non-uniformity applies to each.** Last lane: NA-0734 (D-1370). ### WF-0081 — `relay ca-show` answers "is a CA **stored**", not "will a CA be **used**", and reports `configured=false` while an env-supplied CA is in force — contradicting its own help text — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0730 (D-1366; §7 F-3, DV-7)**

Measured at `50bb5703`: `relay ca-show` reads the **vault secret only** (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/transport/mod.rs:2198-2207`), while `relay_http_client()` resolves env `QSC_RELAY_CA_FILE` → env `RELAY_CA_FILE` → vault `tui.relay.ca_file` (`:2061-2071`). ⚠ **The consequence is a ready-made FALSE RED:** the obvious way to gate "prove the CA is configured" is `relay ca-show`, and against a correct env-configured run it reports `configured=false` and the gate fails a working setup. NA-0730's preflight therefore asserts on `relay server-info`'s reported **outcome** instead, and this entry exists so the next author does not walk into the same instrument. No mechanism change is proposed here: either `ca-show` should report the **effective** source, or its help text should stop promising that it accounts for the env precedence it does not read. Status: open — FILING ONLY. Cross-reference: WF-0082 (the same lane's other instrument trap); ENG-0188. Originating/last lane: NA-0730 (D-1366). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

### WF-0082 — `relay server-info` returns **rc 0** for `outcome=unreachable` and `outcome=cert_not_trusted`, so a step that asserts on `$?` passes green against a dead relay — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0730 (D-1366; §7 F-4, DV-8)**

Measured at `50bb5703`, executed rather than modelled: with a valid PEM and with the CA unset alike, `qsc relay server-info` against a dead endpoint printed `event=relay_server_info outcome=unreachable` and exited **0**. ⚠ **This is a vacuous pass waiting to be written**: asserting on the exit code is the obvious shape, and it would have made NA-0730's own preflight report success against a relay that answered nothing. The behaviour is *defensible* — it is a probe, not an assertion, and its five outcomes (`reachable` / `auth_required` / `cert_not_trusted` / `not_a_qsl_relay` / `unreachable`) map 1:1 onto the causes measured across ENG-0188's streak — but the contract is documented nowhere a consumer will read it. ⚠⚠ **The general property this instance carries, promoted for the B-list: when a tool reports status in its OUTPUT, its EXIT CODE may not carry it — assert on the reported VALUE, never on `$?`.** Remedy options (named, not chosen): document the contract in the subcommand's help · add an `--assert-reachable` flag that *does* map outcome to exit status · leave it and rely on the property being written down. Status: open — FILING ONLY. Cross-reference: WF-0081; ENG-0188; R325.5. Originating/last lane: NA-0730 (D-1366). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

### WF-0083 — relay smoke artifacts published the endpoint URL in plaintext until ~2026-06, and the design property that closed it was never written down — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0730 (D-1366; §7 F-5, DV-10)**

Measured at `50bb5703` by reading historical artifacts: relay artifacts up to ~2026-06 contain the **plaintext endpoint URL**, because `cargo run` echoed `--relay <url>` into files under `$out` — and `$out` is uploaded as a **public** artifact (`path: ./_remote_relay_out`, `./_remote_handshake_out`). ### WF-0085 — the metadata-mitigation defaults were chosen against a rule-based analyst, and the threat has moved to learned traffic classifiers; and nothing in the record measures the CURRENT WIRE BEHAVIOUR — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0731 (D-1367; Director filing text of 2026-08-15, `FILING_metadata_classifier_threat_2026-08-15.md` sha256 `5e1711aa812d9fdd955159b108d7768c03b8cc62a22233852721fafdde986f2e`, 78 lines)**

⚠ **This entry is FILING ONLY. No remedy is chosen and none may be inferred from it.**

**What is NOT being filed: a gap in the catalogue.** The program's metadata work is real and already
mapped, and all of it is present and re-measured at spine main `04affcc9`:
`docs/audit/THREAT_MODEL_PROTOCOL_METADATA.md`, the NA-0134 leakage audit
(`docs/audit/METADATA_LEAKAGE_AUDIT_NA-0134.md`), and the NA-0137 mitigations roadmap
(`docs/audit/METADATA_MITIGATIONS_ROADMAP_NA-0137.md`). ⚠ **A precision correction measured while
filing: the NA-0138 MVP selection is not a separate artifact** — it is §E and §F of the NA-0137
roadmap (`:78-106`), so a successor should not go looking for a document that does not exist.
NA-0137 §A names five leakage drivers — traffic timing/cadence, size/volume patterns, delivered-receipt
timing correlating sender and receiver, file-chunking patterns leaking size class and transfer rhythm,
and error timing/classes. Receipt shaping has shipped with operator controls: `--receipt-mode`
(default **batched**, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/cmd/mod.rs:153`), `receipt_batch_window_ms` (`:161`)
and `receipt_jitter_ms` (`:164`).

**What IS being filed: a challenge to NA-0137 §D's default policy.** Measured at `04affcc9`, §D rules
fixed-interval mode, padding/bucketing, receipt shaping and file-chunk normalization each `Optional`,
and rules cover traffic separately: *"Cover traffic/constant-rate behavior: `Not recommended` for
default mode at this stage due to high operational cost."* Two reasons to think that basis has
weakened. ⚠⚠ **BOTH ARE STATED AS ARGUMENTS, NOT AS FINDINGS. Neither is a measurement taken here,
and nothing below should be read as one** — letting an argument read as a finding is the precise
failure shape `docs/ops/PREDICTION_LEDGER.md`'s ten SR-16 rows (landed by this same lane) record ten
times over.

1. **ARGUMENT — an opt-in metadata defence identifies the user who opts in.** Metadata defences have
   a property encryption does not: they work only in aggregate. If padding and fixed-interval polling
   are off by default, the users who enable them form a distinguishable class, and a defence that
   marks its user can have negative value against an adversary doing classification rather than
   decryption. §D's stance — auditable opt-in controls, minimal default burden — is coherent against
   a per-target analyst and weaker against a population-level classifier. *General knowledge; not
   measured against this program.*
2. **ARGUMENT — "reduced" leakage is not the operative bar for a learned classifier.** Size bucketing
   that defeats a human reading sizes may not defeat a model trained on bucket SEQUENCES; residual
   signal in transition patterns is often sufficient. Measured at `04affcc9`, NA-0137 §C's
   cost/impact table scores Bandwidth, Latency, Battery/CPU and Complexity/Risk — it has **no column
   for whether a mitigation survives a learned classifier**, which was not the pressing question when
   it was written. *The absence of the column is measured; the claim about learned classifiers is
   general knowledge and is not.*

**A consideration that may cut the program's way, and it is UNMEASURED:** QSL's relays are
self-hosted, so the expected observer is usually a network-level adversary rather than a relay
operator, and there is no per-byte provider cost. **The "high operational cost" basis for refusing
constant-rate behaviour may therefore not hold for this architecture** and deserves re-measuring
against the real deployment rather than inheriting. Stated as a consideration, not as a conclusion.

⚠⚠ **THE DECISIVE MISSING ARTIFACT: nothing in the record measures the CURRENT WIRE BEHAVIOUR.**
NA-0134 is an analytic audit; there is no captured baseline of packet sizes, inter-arrival timings or
flow shape from a real two-party session. **A defence cannot be evaluated against an unmeasured
baseline**, and any successor lane that proposes mitigations before capturing one would be
re-deriving NA-0137 rather than advancing it. ⚠ This is a negative claim about the record as it
stands at `04affcc9`; a successor that finds such a capture should amend this entry rather than
assume it never existed.

**What a successor lane owes, in order:** (1) capture and characterise a real two-party session
against a live relay — sizes, timings, flow shape — as the baseline artifact this entry says is
missing; (2) re-ask NA-0137 §D's default-mode question with the classifier threat stated explicitly,
rather than re-deriving the catalogue; (3) decide defaults on that evidence.
**Dependencies already on the roadmap:** the injectable time source (fixed-interval and batching
cannot be tested deterministically without it) and the nightly endurance window (sustained sessions
are the traffic worth characterising). **Sequencing: after Slice 4** — a metadata defence for a
messenger that cannot yet be used is optimising the wrong thing, and the analysis perishes less
quickly than the product opportunity.

**NOT CLAIMED:** that any mitigation is wrong · that NA-0137's catalogue is incomplete · that any
classifier has been demonstrated against QSL traffic — no such measurement exists here and none is
implied · that self-hosting eliminates the observer · that changing a default is cheap.

### ENG-0191 — `remote-handshake-tests` asserts a handshake status that is UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: `hs_status_truth` cannot return `established` before a message is received, and the smoke script asserts it before sending one — **the FOURTH and OLDEST of the four causes behind the 187-day outage** — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0734 (D-1370; measured in-lane at the first post-ENG-0189 run, ratified and ordered filed at R333.2)**

- Severity: **P2** (a stale test assertion, not a shipped defect — but it is the last thing standing between this suite and green, and therefore between issue **#1745** and closure)
- Status: open — **FILING ONLY. The repair is deliberately NOT designed here** (R333.2), because it carries a real design question this filing must not pre-answer: see *THE DESIGN QUESTION* below.

**THE OBSERVATION, measured at `ea5bb95f`.** Run `31898549150` — the first dispatch after ENG-0189's repair merged — fails at step 7 of 9 (`Run remote handshake smoke (happy-path seed=1)`), with step 8 (`drop-reorder`) `skipped` in consequence. The handshake itself does **not** fail: `event=handshake_reject` and `event=error` each appear **0** times, and both peers reach `handshake_complete`. The failing assertion is the script's own, and the job log names it: `alice handshake status is not established`.

**THE TWO PEERS' ACTUAL STATUS VALUES**, from `$out/markers`:

- alice (initiator): `event=handshake_status status=awaiting_peer_confirm … pinned=true peer_confirmed=no send_ready=yes`
- bob (responder): `event=handshake_status status=established_recv_only … pinned=true peer_confirmed=yes send_ready=no send_ready_reason=chainkey_unset`

**THE CAUSE, read from the FUNCTION rather than inferred from the run.** `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs:1302-1310`, `hs_status_truth`, returns `established` **only** when the session's send chain is keyed **and** `st.recv.nr != 0` — that is, only after at least one message has been **received** on the session. Otherwise it returns `established_recv_only` (send chain unkeyed, `reason=chainkey_unset`) or `awaiting_peer_confirm` (`recv.nr == 0`). The script asserts `event=handshake_status status=established` at `scripts/demo/qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh:351` **before it sends any payload** — the send/receive block begins at `:357`. ⇒ **the assertion is UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION at that point in the script**, which is a stronger and different claim than "not observed", and it is available only because the function was read.

⚠⚠ **A PRECISION THAT EXPLAINS WHY 187 DAYS OF ARTIFACTS NEVER POINTED HERE — AND THAT PARTLY MASKS THE DEFECT.** `:351` and `:352` use the **identical** needle `event=handshake_status status=established`, matched as a substring. **`status=established` is a PREFIX of `status=established_recv_only`**, so **bob's assertion at `:352` PASSES** while alice's at `:351` cannot — and the job log therefore names **only alice**. A reader who concluded from that message that the defect is one-sided, or specific to the initiator's identity, would be reading an artefact of substring matching.

**ATTRIBUTION, exact** (`git log -S` over `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/`): `awaiting_peer_confirm` was introduced by **`a5f235b3`, 2026-04-05**, *"NA-0222: fix handshake status and marker honesty"*; `established_recv_only` and `chainkey_unset` by **`c9ce4b4e`, 2026-02-27**, *"na-0168: add send-ready probe markers and diag gating"*.

⚠⚠ **THE TIMELINE IS THE FINDING, AND IT REORDERS THE WHOLE OUTAGE.** The suite's last GREEN run was **2026-02-09**. `established_recv_only` landed **2026-02-27**; `awaiting_peer_confirm` landed **2026-04-05**. **Both post-date the last green.** ⇒ this assertion has been unsatisfiable since **April at the latest**, and the three causes ENG-0188 decomposed (`contacts_store_invalid` → `dns_timeout` → `relay_tls_untrusted`) plus **ENG-0189** all stacked **on top of an already-dead assertion**. **This is cause four of four, and it is the OLDEST.** Every earlier repair was necessary and none was sufficient, which is exactly what R325 warned when it recorded that *whether a fourth cause waits behind the third is unknown until a run gets past TLS*. **A run got past TLS, and one did.**

⚠ **THE DESIGN QUESTION, STATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED (R333.2).** There are at least two shapes a repair could take, and **they do not prove the same thing**: (a) assert a status that is *true at that point* — accepting `awaiting_peer_confirm` / `established_recv_only` as the correct post-handshake states and checking the `peer_confirmed` / `send_ready` fields instead; or (b) **send first and then assert**, so that `recv.nr != 0` and the existing `established` assertion becomes reachable. **(a) tests that the handshake completed; (b) tests that a session can carry traffic.** Choosing between them changes what this smoke test is for, which is why the choice belongs to a lane with a directive and not to a filing. ⚠ A third possibility must not be excluded by the framing above: that the product **should** reach `established` here and does not — nothing in this filing rules that out, and the two readings (stale fixture vs product gap) are both live.

⚠ **What this entry does NOT claim.** It does not claim the product is wrong; the introducing commit's own title — *"fix handshake status and marker **honesty**"* — is evidence the richer states were deliberate. It does not claim the fix is trivial. And it does not claim this is the last cause: that claim has now been wrong four times, and **the only instrument that has ever settled it is a run.** Cross-reference: ENG-0188; ENG-0189; ENG-0190; NA-0222 (`a5f235b3`); NA-0168 (`c9ce4b4e`); D-1369; D-1370; R325; R333.2; issue **#1745**, which stays OPEN and is telling the truth. Originating/last lane: NA-0734 (D-1370). Last-updated: 2026-08-15.

⛳⛳ **THE DATUM, MEASURED, n=2, byte-identical between runs.** Values EXTRACTED and compared for **EQUALITY**, never grepped as a substring:

⛳ **AND THE CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED BY CONTROL, NOT BY INFERENCE.** In the **identical** environment — same relay process, same store, same `qsc` binary, same base, same scenario and seed, with delivery working in both — the committed arrangement was re-run using an instrument **byte-identical to NA-0737's banked harness** (`cmp` rc 0 against `harness_AFTER.sh`):

| arrangement | `established` by EQUALITY | script exit |
|---|---|---|
| committed (`hs2` mid-flow) — NA-0737's own instrument | **0 / 12** | 0 |
| relocated (`hs2` after the round trip) | **3 / 12**, incl. BOTH peers at X4 | 0 |

**The only variable is where `hs2` sits.** NA-0737's 0/12 is reproduced exactly, C3 swap included; the relocation alone produces the state.

⇒ **WHY 0/12 WAS ALWAYS THE ANSWER, mechanically:** `hs2` **REPLACES** the session (`hs_build_session` `:1129` → `qsp_session_store` `:1883`/`:2098`, one blob per peer). Sitting between the two halves, it means **session-1 carried only A→B and session-2 only B→A. ⚠⚠ **THE DIRECTOR'S ELIMINATION IS THEREFORE REFUTED, AND BY ITS OWN EVIDENCE.** The elimination recorded above — *"a second handshake sits mid-flow and **resets** what is being asserted"* — is refuted three ways: **(1) a reset cannot key a chain**, yet at C3/X5 bob reads `send_ready=yes`, which by branch 1 REQUIRES a keyed send chain; **(2) ENG-0143, the elimination's own cited support, says the session is FRESH** — the surviving SCKA fossil is the exception it files as a bug, and it states *"fresh `nr == 0`"* outright; **(3) the grep could not have found it** — there is no reset in any module, the mechanism being an unconditional whole-session OVERWRITE, which no needle for "reset" can match. **The instinct pointed at the right line; the model was wrong, and the wrong model is what closed the option set.**

⚠ **X5 IS ENG-0143's OWED RE-HANDSHAKE ROW, AND IT CONSTRAINS EVERY REPAIR.** From a state where **both** peers read `established`, the re-handshake drives **both** back out of it — alice to `established_recv_only`, bob to `awaiting_peer_confirm`, the role-dual pair NA-0735 and NA-0737 each observed at C3. ⇒ **any repair that asserts `established` AFTER a re-handshake fails.** In the relocated arrangement the assertion must sit **between the round trip and `hs2`**.

## ⚠⚠ A BLOCKER (d) MUST CLEAR, MEASURED IN THIS LANE'S FIRST RUN — AND IT IS NOT A FIXTURE PROBLEM

The first run of the relocated arrangement **FAILED**: alice's `receive` returned **rc 1** with `event=qsp_unpack code=qsp_env_decode_failed`, and bob's message was never reached. The cause was measured to a source line and a store row:

1. **`handshake poll` NEVER ACKS** — `event=relay_ack` measures **0** in `alice.log` and **0** in `bob.log` against **1** in `bob_recv.log`. Across four runs, **every** handshake frame (A1 4279 B, B1 6436 B, A2 3364 B) is still resident in the relay store at run end; only `receive` acks. Complete accounting: 8 routes, 31 residual rows, **0 unexplained**.
2. Those frames therefore survive on a **visibility timeout** alone — `PULL_LEASE_SECS_DEFAULT = 60` (`qsl-server/src/store.rs:7`).
3. hs1's B1 was enqueued on alice's route at 21:00:36; her `receive` ran at **21:01:55 — 79 s later**, past the timeout ⇒ **the stale handshake frame was redelivered at the HEAD of her queue**.
4. `receive` pulled it, could not decode it as a QSP envelope, and **`qsc/src/transport/mod.rs:1249` `return Err(CliError::code(code))` aborted the ENTIRE receive.** Only `qsp_replay_reject` has a quarantine-and-continue arm; **every other code aborts**, the item is never acked, and it is redelivered — permanently at the head. ⇒ **one undecodable frame at the head of a mailbox blocks every message behind it.**

⇒ **This is a HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCK, it is product behaviour and not fixture behaviour, and it is latent on the committed arrangement too** — it fires whenever a peer's `receive` runs more than the visibility timeout after a handshake frame was last pulled. The committed arrangement runs `hs2`'s polls immediately before alice's receive, which re-leases and masks it. ⚠ **It is recorded here and deliberately NOT filed as its own ledger entry** — that is a backlog-prioritisation act belonging to the operator; drafted text and a swept id are carried in NA-0738 STOP 001. Re-running with `PULL_LEASE_SECS=3600` (the server's own ceiling, `store.rs:8`), the identical harness reached X4 on both peers, twice.

⚠ **What this amendment does NOT do.** It does **not** choose an option — five are now live, (a)–(e), and **the choice is the operator's**. It does not repair ENG-0191; `:351`/`:352` are **untouched** in the committed script, re-verified byte-identical (`c885dcf0…0eef`, 482 lines) after all four runs. **ENG-0191 stays OPEN and #1745 stays OPEN.** ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY, carried verbatim and not smoothed:** loopback plain HTTP, **not CI**, no TLS; `qsl-server` rev `37ec8207`; **n=2** for the relocated arrangement and **n=1** for the control; scenario `happy-path` seed 1, **`drop-reorder` NOT run**; the instrument is a HARNESS COPY, **never the committed script**; and the relocated arrangement was reached only with the visibility timeout raised. ### ENG-0192 — `receive --mailbox` takes a RAW ROUTE TOKEN and the remote smoke fixture hands it an IDENTITY LABEL, so the client politely polls a mailbox nobody ever writes to and reports an empty inbox at rc 0 — **the FIFTH cause behind the 187-day outage** — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0736 (D-1371; measured from NA-0735's sealed evidence and from source at `5201c275`; classification ruled at R335 §1 after ENG-0134 and ENG-0142 were both REFUTED)**

- Severity: **P2** — a FIXTURE defect, not a shipped defect, on the same reading ENG-0191 records for itself. The product behaved correctly at every step; one consumer is wrong about what an argument means. ⚠ It is nevertheless the thing standing between this suite and a *proven* round trip, and it sits **behind** ENG-0191 in the failure order, so clearing ENG-0191 alone will not produce a delivered message.
- Status: open — **FILING ONLY.** No repair is designed here and none is proposed: the natural remedy touches either the committed script or the receive path, and the latter is transport-adjacent (ENG-0142 already places a defect inside it), so any proposed edit is a STOP and the repair lane carries its own cold read by construction.

**THE DEFECT.** `scripts/demo/qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh:375` and `:388` invoke
`receive … --mailbox "$proto_bob"` / `--mailbox "$proto_alice"`, where `proto_bob` is the *protocol
identity label* `bob-${run_tag}`. **`--mailbox` is not a label. It is the relay route token, used
verbatim.** `qsc/src/transport/mod.rs:257-263`:

    let mailbox = match mailbox {
        Some(raw) => normalize_route_token(raw.as_str()).map_err(|code| CliError::code(code))?,
        None => relay_self_inbox_route_token().map_err(|code| CliError::code(code))?,
    };

There is no contacts lookup and no identity resolution on the `Some` arm. Meanwhile every sender
addresses by the *contact's* route token — `qsc/src/lib.rs:1565` and `:1592` call
`relay_peer_route_token(to)` (`qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:70-81`), which reads what
`contacts add --route-token` wrote. **The two strings differ, so the pull is addressed to a mailbox
nothing has ever pushed to, the relay answers empty, and `receive` correctly reports `recv_none`.**

**PROVEN BY HASH, NOT BY READING.** The `recv_start` marker publishes
`route_token_hash8(mailbox)` = `hex(sha512(mailbox)[0..4])` (`qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:5-9`) of the
**resolved** value. Computed over the four candidates at the sealed run's `run_tag`, and
independently recomputed by the Director at R335 §0. ⚠ **The concrete route tokens and the run tag
are deliberately NOT reproduced here** — a route token is an addressing capability, this file is
class-only per `AGENTS.md:121`, and the product itself redacts `mailbox=` in its own markers because
they land in publicly-uploaded CI artifacts. The shapes below are the committed script's own
(`:59-62`); the concrete values live in the sealed operator stop cited above and a reader with it can
recompute every digit:

    f4c89d20  <-  bob-<run_tag>                 == bob_recv.log   mailbox_hash  ✅
    f9fa4170  <-  route_token_bob_<run_tag>        (absent from every log)
    a53c4170  <-  alice-<run_tag>               == alice_recv.log mailbox_hash  ✅
    f20f7f9f  <-  route_token_alice_<run_tag>      (absent from every log)

⚠ **Compare all eight digits.** `a53c4170` and `f9fa4170` share the trailing `4170`; a four-digit
comparison crosses the two candidates.

**THE PULL RETURNED ZERO ITEMS — an exhaustive elimination, not an inference.** `recv_none` fires at
`transport/mod.rs:428` only when `total == 0`, and the pull loop breaks at `:517-518` on
`items.is_empty()`. **Every path an item can take emits a marker before it can be dropped:** a dedup
skip emits `recv_dup_skipped` (`:527`), a successful unpack emits `qsp_unpack ok=true` (`:544`), a
failed unpack emits `qsp_unpack ok=false` (`:1199`). The sealed `bob_recv.log` and `alice_recv.log`
carry `recv_ack_mode` — emitted at `:349`, **before** the pull — then `recv_none`, **with nothing
between them**, at rc 0. ⇒ the item loop never executed.

**WHY NOTHING WENT RED.** `route_token_is_valid` (`qsc/src/adversarial/route.rs:21-28`) requires only
a non-empty ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` string of length **22..=128**. Measured: `bob` (3 chars) is
REFUSED with `QSC_ERR_ROUTE_TOKEN_INVALID`; the sealed run's `bob-${run_tag}` label measures
**25 characters** and is ACCEPTED, passing through `normalize_route_token` unchanged. In CI the label
is longer still, `run_tag` being
`${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}-${scenario}-${seed}`. **The guard catches the toy case and
misses every realistic one.** Then
`transport/mod.rs:3056` maps HTTP 204 to `Ok(Vec::new())`, so **"this is not your mailbox" and "your
mailbox is empty" are the same observable at the client.**

**WHY THE HANDSHAKE COMPLETED WHILE DELIVERY DID NOT.** `handshake poll` resolves
`relay_self_inbox_route_token()` and **has no `--mailbox` override at all**
(`qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs:2422-2425`); `relay inbox-set --token` writes exactly the key that
function reads (`qsc/src/main.rs:544` → `tui.relay.inbox_token`, read at
`qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:60-68`). **The one command that can be misaddressed is the one that was.**

⚠ **THE SHAPE OF THE MISTAKE, worth more than the instance.** On a single script line, `--to` and
`--from` take a peer **LABEL** (resolved through contacts) while `--mailbox` takes a raw **ROUTE
TOKEN** (used as-is). `send --to "$proto_bob"` is correct; `receive --mailbox "$proto_bob"` is not.
**Two argument namespaces that look identical, adjacent, with no type distinction and no error.**

**THE CONSUMER CENSUS, which is why this is filed as a fixture defect and not a product defect.**
Measured at `5201c275`: **99 `--mailbox` call sites across 40 test files**, and every site that
reaches a pull passes a route-token-shaped value (`ROUTE_TOKEN_BOB` is literally
`"route_token_bob_abcdefghijklmnopqr"`). `tests/receive_e2e.rs` asserts `event=recv_commit` at
`:257`, `:311`, `:487` and `qsp_unpack ok=true` at `:486`, `:528` **through** `--mailbox`. The single
bare-label site, `tests/unlock_gate.rs:170`, is a locked-vault negative control asserting
`code=vault_locked` — it refuses before addressing anything. ⇒ **`qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh` is
the ONLY consumer in the entire tree that passes an identity label to `--mailbox`.** The contract is
settled and green-tested; one fixture is wrong about it.

### ⚠⚠ WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES **NOT** ESTABLISH — ordered recorded at R335 §5

This suite's history is **four causes, each hiding the next**; this is the fifth. **Nothing entitles
a reader to assume it is the last.** Two threads are open and neither is answered:

- ⚠ **(a) THE USER MESSAGES' FATE IS UNESTABLISHED.** Both sends returned HTTP 200 with

  ⚠ Do not write "the user messages are sitting in the mailbox", and do not write that they are lost.
- ⚠ **(b) WHY IS THE A1 HANDSHAKE FRAME STILL IN BOB'S MAILBOX AT ALL?** The handshake completed on
  both sides — four messages, `handshake_complete` on each — yet the retained item measures **4279 B**,
  matching `event=handshake_send msg=A1 size=4279` exactly (alice's retained item measures **6436 B**,
  matching `msg=B1 size=6436`). Lease-without-ack, dedup-on-redelivery, and
  consumption-leaves-the-item are all candidate explanations. ⚠ **NO MECHANISM IS INVENTED HERE**
  (WF-0080's precedent: record the observation, refuse the invented cause). Open observation.

**Cross-references.** **ENG-0134** and **ENG-0142** — both REFUTED as candidates for this defect at
R335 §1, see the note added to each. **ENG-0191** — fails first, at `:351`, so it must clear before
this defect can even be reached by a run. **ENG-0189** — the same family: a smoke fixture that

**ENG-0193** — why no artifact could show it.

⛳ **THE PROOF — A MESSAGE CROSSED A RELAY END TO END, BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE PAYLOADS ARRIVED BYTE-IDENTICAL** (`cmp` rc 0 each way). | observable | BEFORE (unfixed) | AFTER (repaired) |

### ENG-0193 — the relay boundary is instrumented on the SEND half and MUTE on the RECEIVE half: `relay_push_diagnostic` 28 occurrences, `relay_pull_diagnostic` ZERO tree-wide — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0736 (D-1371; observed at STOP 001 §8 obs 1, re-measured by the Director, ORDERED SPLIT INTO ITS OWN FILING at R335 §3(b))**

- Severity: **P2** — a **diagnosability** defect, not a functional one: nothing misbehaves because of
  it. It is filed at P2 rather than lower on the Director's stated ground that *"a gate tells you
  THAT it broke; instrumentation tells you WHY"*, and that **the 187-day blindness is a direct
  consequence of this asymmetry, not of the missing gate** (R335 §3(b)).
- Status: open — **FILING ONLY.** ⚠ **Instrumenting the pull path is an edit to the receive region
  and remains a STOP**; this entry deliberately proposes no patch.

**MEASURED at `5201c275`, by the lane and independently by the Director:** `relay_push_diagnostic`
appears **28** times in `qsc/src/transport/mod.rs`; `relay_pull_diagnostic` appears **0** times
**tree-wide**. The push marker carries status class, status code, error class, diagnostic class,
timeout phase, response-body presence and length, route-header presence, auth presence, qsc error and
attempt number — e.g. `api=relay_push_v1 status_class=2xx status_code=200 … route_header_present=true
auth_present=true qsc_error=none attempt=1`. **The pull emits none of this.** Its entire observable
surface is `recv_start` (which publishes an 8-hex hash of the mailbox and nothing else), an optional
`recv_ack_mode`, and then either `recv_none` or `recv_commit`.

⚠ **THE CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** ENG-0192 was found by *computing sha512 over four
candidate strings and comparing the leading four bytes against a marker* — because that hash is the
only thing the receive path publishes about where it looked. **A single `relay_pull_diagnostic`
carrying what the push marker already carries would have named the defect on the first failing run in
February.** Instead the mailbox mismatch was invisible for 187 days behind four other causes.

⚠ **AND THE ASYMMETRY IS ITSELF THE ARGUMENT.** The two halves of one boundary, in one file, written

### WF-0086 — `--mailbox` is well covered against an in-process test relay with the correct value type; what nothing covers is a REAL remote relay round trip, and the one consumer that gets the value wrong has never reached its own receive — **NEW; filed 2026-08-15 by NA-0736 (D-1371; STOP 002 §4's replaced text, confirmed at R335 §3(a))**

- ⚠ **THE FIRST FORM OF THIS FILING WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS WRONG.** STOP 001 §6 asserted *"the
  `--mailbox` override has ZERO green coverage anywhere in the tree."* **Measured, that is FALSE:**
  40 test files, **99** call sites, with delivery assertions. The claim had been quantified over *the
  tree* from a sweep of `scripts/demo/` and `.github/workflows/` alone — **an instrument narrower
  than its claim (SR-21)**. The corrected finding below is narrower, better-aimed and stronger.

  **(i)** `.github/workflows/demo-packaging.yml:55` runs `scripts/demo/qsc_demo_local.sh`, whose two
  receives at `:235` and `:241` end in **`|| true`** — the exit status is discarded — against a
  loopback relay, and the script carries **0** golden comparisons, **0** `exit 1`, and **0**
  assertions on `recv_commit` or `qsp_unpack`. ⚠ `demo-packaging.yml` is **55 lines**: that run is
  the **last step in the file**, so nothing downstream compares anything. **The job is green iff the
  script exits 0 within 60 s.**
  **(ii)** `.github/workflows/remote-handshake-tests.yml` runs `qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh`, which
  **does** carry the right assertions — `qsp_unpack ok=true` at `:395` and `:396` — but they sit
  behind `:351`, unsatisfiable by construction since April (**ENG-0191**), and **have not executed in

  **(iii)** `qsc_remote_relay_smoke.sh` (340 lines) never receives at all: the tokens `receive`,
  `unpack` and `handshake` each appear **0** times in it.
- ⚠⚠ **THE DECISIVE ASYMMETRY.** The receive that *is* exercised omits `--mailbox` and therefore takes
  the correct self-inbox resolution; the only consumer that *supplies* `--mailbox` has never reached
  its own receive. **So the override path has never once been observed green against a real relay** —

  server in the same process. Adding a 100th buys nothing: **a fixture that misaddresses a real
  mailbox is not a thing an in-process test is positioned to catch.**

  message is sent and not received, exercising a **REMOTE relay round trip end to end**.
  ⚠ **A gate over this path is BORN RED while ENG-0192 and ENG-0191 are open.** Two questions are the
  **OPERATOR's**, not a seat's, and must be answered before it is written: **(1)** does it ship
  **REQUIRED or ADVISORY** while the defect is open? **(2)** **which addressing does it exercise?** —
  a gate asserting delivery with `--mailbox` omitted would go green today and still not cover the

### ENG-0194 — the substring defect ENG-0191 found in a shell fixture also exists in a UNIT TEST and in the soak harness, where it makes an assertion INERT: **every consumer of `status=established` in this repository matches it as a SUBSTRING, so `hs_status_truth`'s third branch has ZERO distinguishing coverage tree-wide** — **NEW; filed 2026-08-16 by NA-0738 (D-1373; found by the SR-15 adversarial cold read of ENG-0191, §8.2, sha256 `a5b7324e…b1b4`; consumer census re-measured tree-wide at `62752adf` by the filing seat, which found the read's enumeration SHORT BY ONE)**

- Severity: **P2** — a coverage defect, not a shipped defect. Nothing is mis-computed; a state simply has no test that can tell it from its own prefix. It is nevertheless why the unreachability at the heart of **ENG-0191** survived 187 days *inside* the unit suite as well as outside it.
- Status: open — **FILING ONLY. The repair is deliberately NOT made here.** A test edit is outside NA-0738's authorised edit set and would have been a STOP; and the right repair is coupled to whichever ENG-0191 option the operator rules, since option **(e)** changes what these assertions should say.

**THE DEFECT.** `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/send_ready_markers_na0168.rs:334` asserts

    bob_status_after_out.contains("status=established"),

`contains` is a substring match and **`established` is a PREFIX of `established_recv_only`**. The test's own comment, ten lines below at `:343-346`, states that at this exact point the responder *"is still recv-only (send_ready=no)"* — and `:348` then asserts `send_ready=no`. ⇒ **the assertion at `:334` passes on `established_recv_only`, which is the state the test itself says obtains. It is INERT: it cannot fail, and it cannot distinguish the state it names from the one actually present.**

**THE CENSUS — and ⚠ the cold read's own enumeration measured SHORT BY ONE.** The read's §8.2 names **three** consumers of the literal (`:351`, `:352`, `na0168:334`). Measured tree-wide at `62752adf` over every tracked file, there are **FOUR**:

| # | site | match style | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/demo/qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh:351` | `mark_grep` (regex, unanchored) | ENG-0191; fails for alice |
| 2 | `scripts/demo/qsc_remote_handshake_smoke.sh:352` | `mark_grep` (regex, unanchored) | **passes spuriously** on `established_recv_only` |
| 3 | `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/send_ready_markers_na0168.rs:334` | Rust `.contains` | **INERT** (this filing) |
| 4 | `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/scripts/remote_soak.py:573` | Python `not in` | **INERT**, and applied in **both** directions by the `((a, b), (b, a))` loop at `:561`; a soak whose `hs_pair_handshake_ok` stage is satisfied by `established_recv_only` |

⚠ **The read's CONCLUSION survives and is STRENGTHENED by the correction, not weakened:** with four of four matching by substring, **bare `established` has never been asserted anywhere in this repository in a way that could tell it from `established_recv_only`.** ⇒ **`hs_status_truth`'s third branch had ZERO distinguishing coverage tree-wide** — which is exactly why NA-0738 was the first observation of it (see ENG-0191's 2026-08-16 amendment: X3 and X4, `established` on both peers).

⚠ **A PRECISION, so the finding is not read wider than it is.** Site 4 is an **operator-run** soak harness, not a workflow-run one — `remote_soak` appears **0 times** under `.github/workflows/`. Sites 1 and 2 are CI-run. Saying "four inert CI assertions" would be false; the true statement is *four substring consumers, three of them capable of passing on the wrong state, in two CI-run files and one operator-run file*.

⚠ **The three sites that match `status=established_recv_only`** — `desktop_gui_contract_na0215b.rs:539`, `handshake_contract_na0217i.rs:283`, `handshake_mvp.rs:1165` — are **NOT** part of this defect. They pin the recv-only state deliberately and their needle carries the discriminating suffix. They are cited because they are the evidence that the responder's post-handshake state is **intended**, which is what closes ENG-0191's "product gap" reading.

⚠ **A forward consequence any repair lane must carry:** under ENG-0191 option **(e)**, or under any change from substring to equality matching, **`:352` will begin failing for the first time.** A lane that repairs `:351` and leaves `:352` matching by substring has repaired half a defect and will believe it repaired all of it.

⚠ **TWO CARRIED CONSTRAINTS RIDE WITH IT, unchanged in substance:**

1. **Compose-disabled must NOT key off `send_ready`** (R334.3). `send_ready=no` reports the **chain's** state, not the user's capability: the refusal is `chain_unseeded && !boundary_permitted`, and a **USER** send always may originate — only a CONTROL send is refused. ⛳ **NA-0738 supplies the first direct run-derived evidence for this**: at X2 bob reads `send_ready=no chainkey_unset`, and his very next act — a user send — **succeeds** and seeds his chain (`qsp_dh_ratchet dir=send reason=first_send`), taking him to `established`. **A GUI keying compose off `send_ready` would have disabled the control at the exact moment the send was going to work.** This was a READING when carried; it is now a measurement.
2. **The GUI must never accept a caller-supplied mailbox** — binding the MESSAGING slice, not Slice 4. **ENG-0192** is the demonstration of the cost: `--mailbox` is used verbatim as a route token, `route_token_is_valid` accepts any 22–128-char token, and HTTP 204 renders "not your mailbox" and "your mailbox is empty" indistinguishable at rc 0.
