### ENG-0235 — the tiered gate SCANS RAW MARKUP AND HAS NO `<!--` HANDLING, so a comment can satisfy or break a pin — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0756, discharging the NA-0755 close-out's owed filing**

- Severity: **candidate** — no product defect is claimed. It is an INSTRUMENT property, and naming it is what keeps the seals' claims honest.
- Exact surfaces: the source-text pins in `qsl-desktop`'s `src-tauri/tests/design_polish.rs` and the tiered scanners that read `ui/*.js` / `ui/*.html` as flat text.
- Description: every source-text pin in the tree matches against raw file bytes with no comment awareness whatsoever. That cuts BOTH ways and both were observed live. **Green-when-red:** NA-0755 measured a comment that ENUMERATED four retired helper sentences putting all four back into `main.js`, which would have turned their absence seal green while the feature was gone; and a comment explaining a vault-write mechanism spelled the very construct the trios forbid. **Red-when-green:** NA-0756 measured the mirror image — `every_screen_transition_closes_the_invite_modal` sliced a fixed 1400-byte window from `show()`, and ONE added comment line pushed the closing brace outside it, so the seal failed to FIND the body rather than failing to find the call. **FIVE** occurrences of the class are now on the record across two lanes, and **two of them are NA-0756's own** — one in each direction. The second is the sharpest instance yet: the comment written to explain that a retired form is absent SPELLED it, putting it back in the shipped file and making its own sentence self-falsifying, while the seal PASSED because its slice began below the comment. It was caught by a pre-merge checklist control reading the WHOLE file, not by the seal. ⇒ the cure that held is DESCRIBE-NEVER-SPELL plus a whole-file scope plus a BUILT needle, so the test cannot become the planter in turn.
- ⚠ **What makes it hard to see:** the failure is silent in the green-when-red direction. A pin that a comment satisfies reports PASS, and nothing in the output distinguishes it from a pin the code satisfies.
- Remedy: the cure is a POSITIVE PIN on the shipped form rather than a negative pin on a word — assert the attribute (the usage) rather than the token (the mention) — plus, where a negative pin is genuinely needed, strip comments before matching. ⚠ The comment-stripping half must be done carefully: a naive `//` strip corrupts URLs and regex literals, which is why the positive-pin cure is preferred and is what NA-0755 and NA-0756 both actually shipped.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-23 by NA-0756 (`D-1398`; desktop `D-0037`).
- Cross-references: `D-1397`, `D-1398`, `D-0036`, `D-0037`, `ENG-0230`.
- Source: the NA-0755 close-out's OWED list ("the comment-blind-scanner property FILED (id derived; the tiered gate has no `<!--` handling, measured, four occurrences)"), discharged here; `R387` §S1.

### ENG-0236 — a redeemer's TYPED CONTACT NAME reaches its validation gate TWENTY-FIVE LINES AFTER the invite has already burned — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0756 (measured, NOT patched — `qsc` frozen)**

- Severity: **defect** — user-visible and destructive: the user loses a one-time capability and cannot recover it.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/invite/mod.rs` (`invite_redeem_at`, `:1031-1140`), `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:847`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/lib.rs:2568-2573` (`channel_label_ok`).
- Description: `channel_label_ok` admits ONLY non-empty `[A-Za-z0-9_#-]` — **no spaces, no apostrophes, no accented letters**. In `invite_redeem_at` the identifier `alias` occurs exactly THREE times: the parameter at `:1033`, the provision call at `:1107`, and the handshake call at `:1122`. A validation needle across `:1031-1105` returns **rc 1** — the alias is never checked before use. The capability BURNS at `:1081`, the instant `invite_redeem_call` returns, and the gate is at `contacts/mod.rs:847`. ⇒ a caller passing `"Ben Smith"` — the most natural thing a human types into a field labelled *"Their name"* — spends the invite, then fails with `other` / `contacts_alias_invalid`, and the code cannot be redeemed again.
- ⚠ **Why it surfaced only now:** `invite_create`'s `recipient_label` is NOT subject to this predicate — it is a stored note, not a channel label — so Lane A never met it. Redeem is the first caller whose user-typed string becomes a CONTACT ALIAS.
- ⚠ **The desktop's JS mirror is DEFENCE, NOT A REPAIR.** `qsl-desktop` now refuses to arm Connect unless the name matches the engine's exact set, and a seal's control types `"Ben Smith"` and proves the button DISABLED. That protects one front end. The CLI's `invite redeem --alias` has no such gate, and neither does any future caller.
- Remedy: validate `alias` with `channel_label_ok` at the TOP of `invite_redeem_at`, before the redemption record is committed at `:1066` and long before the network call at `:1081`. It is a fail-closed pre-check with no behavioural cost — the call already fails on that input, only later and more expensively. Consider the same for `invite_accept_at`, whose `alias` reaches the identical gate.

### ENG-0237 — `FacadeError::RelayCaFile`'s own doc says the specific code "travels in `detail`"; it is a UNIT variant and it cannot — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0756 (documentation falsified against the pinned bytes)**

- Severity: **candidate** — a documentation defect with a real consequence for screen copy.

- Description: the variant's doc reads *"The CA-file trio — `relay_ca_file_missing` `:2103`, `_unreadable` `:2105`, `_invalid` `:2107`. LOCAL CA configuration; the specific code travels in `detail`."* It cannot: `RelayCaFile` is a **unit** variant carrying no payload, and the DTO conversion maps `_ => None` for every arm except `Other` and `VaultUnavailable`. ⇒ the three distinct CA-file causes collapse to ONE wire code with NO detail, and a screen cannot tell them apart.
- ⚠ **The distinction DOES exist elsewhere in the tree**, which is what makes the doc's claim plausible enough to mislead: `qsl-desktop`'s relay pane maps all three separately (*"No file at that path." / "That file can't be read." / "That file isn't a certificate."*) because it reads the RAW codes before they reach the facade. - Status: open — filed 2026-08-23 by NA-0756 (`D-1398`; desktop `D-0037`). NOT patched: a doc-only fix is still a `.rs` byte.

### ENG-0239 — an IN-PROCESS `invite_finish` cannot store the session where a SUBPROCESS one can, and the typed cause is discarded before it reaches any caller — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0756 (driven both ways, NOT patched — `qsc` frozen)**

- Severity: **defect** — it bounds what the GUI's finish trigger can do, and the diagnosis it would need is destroyed in flight.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs:1929` and `:2156` (the `map_err` that discards the cause), `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/protocol_state/mod.rs:168-181` (`qsp_session_store_key_load`) and `:183-226` (`qsp_session_store_key_get_or_create`).
- Description: driven both ways in `na0756_two_party_invite_roundtrip.rs` against the **same config dir, the same relay and the same vault**, with the process shape as the ONLY variable:
  - `qsc::facade::invite_finish(None, "alice", &base, 1)` in-process → **`Err(Other("handshake_session_store_failed"))`**
  - `qsc invite finish --alias alice --relay <base>` as a subprocess → **exit status 0**
  The handshake reaches its session store and the store fails; everything before it — create, redeem, provision, accept — succeeds in the same run.
- ⚠ **THE TYPED CAUSE IS DISCARDED, AND THAT IS HALF THE DEFECT.** Both call sites map the store's `ErrorCode` through `map_err(|_| "handshake_session_store_failed")`, so the specific arm never reaches the facade. `model/mod.rs:28-32` gives `ErrorCode::LockUpgradeRefused` a distinct name **precisely so it stays diagnosable to a GUI**, and `facade::store_code_from_wire` carries thirteen such codes — every one of them is flattened to a single opaque string on this path. A screen cannot tell a lock refusal from an I/O failure from a missing key.
- ⚠ **A MEASURED CONTRIBUTING MECHANISM, offered as the leading hypothesis and NOT as a finding:** unlocking the vault in-process to satisfy `require_unlocked_here` takes the store-key load OFF its seed-fallback branch. That fallback fires only on `Err("vault_missing" | "vault_locked")` (`:172`, `:219`); an unlocked mock vault returns `Ok(None)` instead, while a subprocess — which never unlocks in-process — takes the fallback. The store EX lock at `:194` is the other candidate. **Which of the two it is has NOT been isolated**, because the opaque string above prevents it.
- ⚠⚠ **WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, AND IT IS THE QUESTION THAT MATTERS.** Whether `qsl-desktop` hits the same wall is **UNKNOWN**. The desktop also unlocks in-process, but against a REAL vault whose store key can genuinely be written, so its arm may take the `Ok(None) → generate → secret_set` path and succeed. Neither harness can settle it: the desktop's has no relay at all (`ENG-0226`) and this one has no real vault. **If it DOES reproduce there, the GUI's finish trigger cannot complete a handshake and NA-0756's headline is bounded** — which is exactly what the operator's acceptance flight will reveal, and why that flight is the gate rather than a formality.
- Remedy: (a) carry the `ErrorCode` through both `map_err` sites so the arm stays diagnosable — that is a one-line-per-site change with no behavioural cost, and it is what would have isolated this in minutes; then (b) fix whichever cause (a) exposes.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-23 by NA-0756 (`D-1398`; desktop `D-0037`). NOT patched: `qsc` product bytes are outside this lane's scope and a measured need is a STOP.
- Cross-references: `D-1398`, `D-0037`, `ENG-0226`, `ENG-0238`.
- Source: NA-0756's facade drive, driven both ways with the process shape isolated as the only variable.
- ⚠⚠ **AMENDED 2026-08-24 by NA-0757 (`D-1399`; `R388`) — EXTENDED, NOT REWRITTEN, because the
  entry above was TRUE AS WRITTEN and its central caveat was correct.** The bullets above record
  the process-shape asymmetry as *"the leading hypothesis"*, explicitly *"NOT isolated"*. It is
  now isolated, and the hypothesis is **RETIRED — a hypothesis correctly retired, not a finding

- **THE CAUSE, MEASURED.** `qsp_sessions` was created by a bare `fs::create_dir_all`
  (`protocol_state/mod.rs:982`) with **no explicit mode**, so its permissions were the CALLING

  `(mode & 0o022) != 0` (`fs_store:402-406`) — and the refusal was flattened into one opaque
  string. ⚠ The refusal is **correct**; the birth mode was the defect.
- **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE UMASK, NOT THE PROCESS SHAPE.** Three arms, only the umask varying,
  everything else identical: **umask 077 → `Ok(true)`, peer ACTIVE**; **umask 022 → dir born
  0755, self-healed to 0700 by `enforce_dir_perms`, `Ok(true)`, peer ACTIVE**; **umask 002 → dir
  born 0775 → `Err(Other("handshake_session_store_failed"))`**. The in-process facade finish
  completes a real handshake perfectly; NA-0756's in-process arm failed because **the build box's
  own umask is 0002**. ⚠ And a directory pre-poisoned at 0775 fails the **SUBPROCESS** arm too,
  reproducing the field's marker sequence exactly — which is why a *desktop-born* vault breaks
  the CLI. The two entry points differ (`:981` when the dir already exists, `:985` when it is
  fresh) and are indistinguishable at the marker.
- **THE FIELD PROOF CHAIN — operator-flown 2026-08-24 on two notebooks against the live relay,
  quoted VERBATIM from `FIELD_EVIDENCE_ENG0239_20260824.md` (sha256
  `4bd53116fb18d038e3577656e0f0f25a5c77b819234e96230edff1b145dddef7`, 78 lines / 5717 bytes, 444;
  compiled by the Director from the operator's own pastes, transcription fidelity attested).**
  `R389` B3 supersedes attribution-only citation for this evidence: **field evidence that lives
  only in a chat does not survive** (`R331.1`).

  **(a) THE FAILURE — the redeeming machine, CLI subprocess, vault unlocked via file flag:**

  ```
  QSC_MARK/1 event=invite_scan_summary scanned=1 pulls=1 truncated=false selected=invite_resp classes=invite_resp
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_pending peer=Matthew present=true role=initiator key=handshake.pending.self.Matthew state=present
  QSC_MARK/1 event=sig_status ok=true alg=ML-DSA-65 reason=b1_verify
  QSC_MARK/1 event=identity_ok peer=Matthew fp=b1f9f457f11f8adb955ef2bc93b7cd9aab78754c01b7757d8a413a49b6567e3a
  QSC_MARK/1 event=error code=handshake_session_store_failed
  ```

  **(b) THE CAUSE, MEASURED ON BOTH MACHINES.** On the redeemer:
  `stat -c '%a %n' <app-data>/qsc/qsp_sessions` → **`775`**. On the accepting machine the same
  path returned **No such file or directory** — because **`invite_accept` stores a pending in the
  VAULT and never runs the session store at all**, which is the asymmetry this lane predicted

  `drwxrwxr-x` — **process umask 002, observed not inferred** — while the qsc-managed entries read
  `drwx------` because qsc's own code enforces itself.

  **(c) THE INTERVENTION — `chmod 700` on that directory as the SINGLE variable, then the
  IDENTICAL previously-failing command:**

  ```
  QSC_MARK/1 event=invite_scan_summary scanned=1 pulls=1 truncated=false selected=invite_resp classes=invite_resp
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_pending peer=Matthew present=true role=initiator key=handshake.pending.self.Matthew state=present
  QSC_MARK/1 event=sig_status ok=true alg=ML-DSA-65 reason=b1_verify
  QSC_MARK/1 event=identity_ok peer=Matthew fp=b1f9f457f11f8adb955ef2bc93b7cd9aab78754c01b7757d8a413a49b6567e3a
  QSC_MARK/1 event=session_store ok=true format=v3 enc=aead
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_suite_admission result=compatibility_accept mode=legacy_compat reason=ACCEPT_QSC_HS_LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY
  QSC_MARK/1 event=sig_status ok=true alg=ML-DSA-65 reason=a2_sign
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_send msg=A2 size=3364
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_complete peer=Matthew role=initiator peer_confirmed=no
  QSC_MARK/1 event=producer_ack caller=finish sent=1 acked=1
  invite_finish=ok
  ```

  **(d) THE ACCEPTING PARTY COMPLETES — its `qsp_sessions` pre-created `mkdir -m 700`, then the
  handshake poll:**

  ```
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_pending peer=ALIZA present=true role=responder key=handshake.pending.self.ALIZA state=present
  QSC_MARK/1 event=sig_status ok=true alg=ML-DSA-65 reason=a2_verify
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_recv msg=A2 ok=true
  QSC_MARK/1 event=session_store ok=true format=v3 enc=aead
  QSC_MARK/1 event=producer_ack caller=poll sent=1 acked=1
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_complete peer=ALIZA role=responder peer_confirmed=yes
  QSC_MARK/1 event=session_load ok=true format=v3
  QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_status status=established_recv_only peer=ALIZA pinned=true peer_confirmed=yes send_ready=no send_ready_reason=chainkey_unset
  ```

  ⛳⛳ **`session_store ok=true` IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND `handshake_complete peer_confirmed=yes` —
  THE FIRST FULLY ESTABLISHED TWO-PARTY PAIR IN THE PRODUCT'S HISTORY.** `established_recv_only`
  with `send_ready_reason=chainkey_unset` is the documented correct state for a peer that has
  received but never originated a user send; user messaging does not exist yet.

  **(e) PROVENANCE.** Every field command carried `QSC_CONFIG_DIR`, so each run took the
  **`EnvOverride`** arm of `enforce_safe_parents` — the same arm as this lane's probes, which
  closes the cold read's `F-20` and removes the last gap between lab and field.
  ⚠ **A FORENSIC MISS IS RECORDED, NOT SMOOTHED:** the `chmod` destroyed the owner/group/content
  detail the read's `F-11` asked to capture first. The mode and the directory listing are what
  survive. Recorded as a Director row, not repeated.

- ⚠⚠ **THE PROPERTY THIS PROGRAM KEEPS, minted by the SR-15 cold read: A FLATTENED ERROR IS
  COMPATIBLE WITH EVERY CODE IT FLATTENS.** The field capture was the *flattened* string, and
  seven distinct `ErrorCode`s reach that flattening — so the field evidence discriminated
  **none** of them. A lab reproduction proves a cause **sufficient**; only the INTERVENTION
  EXPERIMENT (change one variable, observe the outcome flip) proved the **instance**. Until the
  `chmod` completed the handshake, `unsafe_path_symlink` and `identity_secret_unavailable` were
  live alternatives producing a byte-identical capture. **Neither is cured by a chmod on the
  leaf, so the completion excludes both.**
- **RETRY SAFETY held throughout.** `invite_finish` pulls via the never-acking
  `relay_inbox_pull`, so the reply redelivered on every scan and nothing was lost pre-repair; the
  relay's RETENTION window was the only clock. `ENG-0142` is the adjacent-but-separate wedge
  filing — cross-referenced, **not edited and not closed**.
- **THE DESKTOP CONSEQUENCE, now settled.** As shipped, the app's completion triggers could not
  succeed on any machine whose umask left a write bit — and the desktop's own umask is measured
  002. PR #37 was held on exactly this.
- ⚠ **WHAT THIS AMENDMENT DOES NOT CLAIM.** The heal-policy axis — whether an INHERITED exposed
  directory should be repaired, refused, or repaired-with-disclosure — is **deferred whole** to
  the storage-integrity-check design (`R388` A1(c)). This lane changes **no repair/refuse policy

- **BOUNDARY BETWEEN THE TWO HALVES OF THE RECORD.** The Lane B FLIGHT RECORD — all seven steps,

- ⚠⚠ **`A1(a)` SHIPPED AS TWO EDITS OF UNEQUAL EFFECT, and the record says so rather than

  a just-created directory one line after creation, which the old inline sequence never did. The
  **`DirBuilder` mode-explicit creation closes the creation WINDOW** (the cold read's `F-8`): a

### ENG-0240 — every directory in `qsc` is born at the AMBIENT UMASK, and the safety of the store depends on a call only the BINARY makes — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0757 (`R388` A5)**

- Severity: **defect (systemic, latent)** — one instance of it was ENG-0239, and the instrument that would catch the next one does not exist.
- Description: there is **no `DirBuilder` anywhere in `src/`** (measured, zero occurrences). Every directory is created by a bare `fs::create_dir_all` at whatever umask the calling process happens to carry, and a correct `0700` is achieved only *afterwards* — by `enforce_dir_perms` (`fs_store:417`) or by an explicit `set_permissions` (`vault/mod.rs:659`, the only production instance). The safety of the whole config dir therefore rests on **`main.rs:59` `set_umask_077`**, which is a property of the **binary**, not of the library — and **no in-process consumer makes that call**, `qsl-desktop` included.
- ⚠ **PRECISION, per the SR-15 cold read (F-18).** `protocol_state:982` was the **only bare creation INSIDE the config dir**, and this lane cures it at the primitive. **Two more exist OUTSIDE it and are NOT fixed here**: `lib.rs:2805` (`write_doctor_export` — creates the export directory and writes the report with neither `enforce_dir_perms` nor `enforce_file_perms`) and `output/mod.rs:363` (`log_marker` — creates the `QSC_LOG_PATH` parent, ignores the error, appends the marker log with no perms enforcement). Both write to **user-supplied** paths, which is why they are lower-stakes rather than harmless.
- ⚠⚠ **THE DEEPER SYSTEMIC PROPERTY IS REPAIR-WITHOUT-DISCLOSURE, AND IT IS ALREADY SHIPPED.** `enforce_dir_perms` unconditionally chmods a security-relevant directory back to `0700` and continues, inside `write_atomic` (`:183`), `ensure_dir_secure` (`:121`) and `lock_store_exclusive` (`:333`); `vault/mod.rs:648-661` does the same to the directory **holding the vault file**; and the desktop's `create_private_dir` (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:313-317`) does it to `<data>/qsc` **on every app start**. Nothing anywhere records that a directory was found exposed. That is a coherent product-wide policy question, not a bug — and it is a named input to the operator-blessed **storage-integrity-check** design.
- Remedy: (a) mode-explicit creation everywhere a private directory is born — this lane delivers it inside `ensure_dir_secure`, so its **17 pre-existing call sites (15 of them production) across 8 files** inherit it; (b) route the two outside-config-dir sites through the same primitive or state why they should not be; (c) decide the disclosure policy in the storage-integrity design rather than per-site.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-24 by NA-0757 (`D-1399`; `R388` A5). Partially mitigated: the config-dir class is cured at birth by this lane's primitive fix.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0239`, `ENG-0241`, `ENG-0242`, `D-1399`, `R388`.
- Source: NA-0757's cause isolation, with the precision correction and the reframing supplied by the SR-15 cold read (F-7, F-18).

### ENG-0241 — the G2 anti-rollback record is UNAUTHENTICATED JSON inside the session directory, and one unlink disables the guard — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0757 (`R388` A5, from SR-15 F-6)**

- Severity: **defect (security, bounded)** — needs a local writer in the directory's group or in `other`; it is not remotely reachable.
- Description: `qsp_scka_mono_path` (`protocol_state:558-560`) resolves to **the same directory** as `qsp_session_blob_path` (`:135-137`), and `qsp_scka_mono_load` (`:562-573`) parses it with `serde_json::from_slice` — **plain JSON, no MAC, no AEAD**. The NA-0624 G2 rollback guard (`:927-941`) reads `Ok(Some(rec)) => rollback_check(..)` fail-closed at `:929-930`, but **`Ok(None) => {}` at `:935` — the guard is SKIPPED when the record is absent.**
- ⚠ Consequences for an attacker who can write that directory: **`rm <peer>.scka.json` silently bypasses the guard with one unlink**, after which an older *genuine* session blob — copyable from the same readable directory — replays without objection (AEAD stops forgery; it does not stop replay, and replay is exactly what G2 exists to stop); lowering the recorded counters passes `qsp_scka_rollback_check` (`:575-610`) vacuously for the same effect; raising them or injecting tombstones yields `session_rollback_detected` or suppressed advertisement ids — a targeted denial of service against one contact.
- ⚠⚠ **WHY THIS IS FILED NOW AND NOT BEFORE.** `UnsafeParentPerms` is currently the **only** thing that stops the client resuming out of a directory in that state. Any future change that repairs an inherited exposed directory and continues would resume trusting an unauthenticated guard read from a directory that was, by construction, writable by whoever exposed it. **That makes this a hard input to the heal-policy decision**, which `R388` A1(c) defers whole.
- Remedy: authenticate the G2 record (MAC it with a vault-held key, or move it inside the AEAD-protected blob), and decide whether `Ok(None)` may legitimately mean "no history" once the record is authenticated.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-24 by NA-0757 (`D-1399`; `R388` A5). NOT patched: it is a crypto design act, outside this lane's pre-commitment.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0239`, `ENG-0240`, `D-1399`, `R388`; NA-0624 G2.
- Source: SR-15 cold read F-6.

### ENG-0242 — a facade doc-comment points at a `store_code_from_wire` arm that does not exist, and the arm above it would shadow one anyway — **NEW; FILED OPEN by NA-0757 (`R388` A5, from SR-15 F-14)**

- Severity: **defect (documentation-vs-bytes, latent trap)** — harmless today, and it is a trap laid directly in the path of the obvious next change.
- Description: `facade/mod.rs:286-291`'s doc comment asserts that *"the SAME string as an `ErrorCode::as_str()` wire name from a typed verb is `Store(IdentitySecretUnavailable)` — see `store_code_from_wire`"*. **`store_code_from_wire` (`:319-336`) has no `identity_secret_unavailable` arm** — its thirteen arms are the other codes plus the `vault_write_failed` alias — and `map_code`'s **explicit** arm at `:292-294` maps that string to `FacadeError::VaultUnavailable` **before** the fall-through could ever reach `store_code_from_wire`.
- ⚠⚠ **WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY THIS LANE DID NOT TRIP IT.** The obvious reading of ENG-0239's remedy is *"replace the flattened string with the store code's wire name"*. Had that shipped, `identity_secret_unavailable` — which is what **every** lock failure, every `config_dir()` failure and every `secret_set` failure on the store path collapses into (`protocol_state:189-197`) — would have started arriving at the GUI as **"vault unavailable"**: a specific, confident, WRONG diagnosis pointing the user at a vault that is fine. **Opaque → wrong is a regression, not a diagnostic improvement.** `R388` A1(b) therefore ruled *structured augmentation* instead: the code travels as a `store_code` FIELD on the marker and **no new string enters the facade's wire vocabulary**, so this trap stays disarmed. It is filed so that it is on the record before anyone reaches for the obvious change again.
- Remedy: either give `store_code_from_wire` the arm its caller's documentation claims and teach `map_code` the provenance split it asserts, or correct the comment to describe what the bytes do. The first is a design act (it would create a new error surface, which `D630` §5c decided against); the second is a documentation fix.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-24 by NA-0757 (`D-1399`; `R388` A5). NOT patched: **zero facade bytes** in this lane.

### ENG-0243 — na0742's ack-fault proxy answers a `WouldBlock` read with SILENCE, and its accepted socket may inherit the listener's `O_NONBLOCK` on macOS — **NEW; FILED AND REPAIRED by NA-0759 (from the `0b9d6967` macOS main-push red)**

- Severity: **defect (test fixture; a measured 1-in-12 race on a check `public-safety` gates)** — no product byte is implicated
- **The failure.** macOS `macos-qsc-shard-1` at protocol main `0b9d6967` (run 32783304684, job 97609967915): `t5p_the_poll_tolerates_a_redelivered_already_processed_frame` fails its antecedent `proxy.faulted() > 0` (`:1044`), with `event=handshake_recv code=relay_inbox_pull_failed ok=false`. Green on Linux at the same sha (513.96 s) and green on macOS at the previous main `f98af5cc` (660.53 s). The test file is byte-identical across the merge (`5b136eee…`) and its shard assignment is unchanged (macOS shard 1 at both shas; 35 targets both runs).
- ⚠⚠ **NOT the NA-0757 repair, and the refutation is STRUCTURAL rather than probabilistic.** `relay_inbox_pull` returns `Err` and `perform_handshake_poll_with_tokens` returns at `handshake/mod.rs:1727`, **201 and 440 lines above** the two edited `qsp_session_store` sites (`:1928`, `:2167`). The edits are unreached on the failing path. na0742 asserts on no `event=error` marker — `count_marker` is used three times and only on `recv_frame_skipped` and `producer_ack` — so the augmentation could not perturb it either. `D-1399`'s repair is exonerated.
- **The defect.** `start_ack_fault_proxy` sets the **listener** non-blocking (`:741`) and never clears the flag on the accepted socket (`:753`); `read_head` mapped **every** read error — `WouldBlock` included — to `None` (`:727`); and the caller answers `None` by `continue`, writing **no response at all** (`:762-764`). A dropped connection reaches the client as a bare transport error, which `transport/mod.rs:2229-2240` collapses to `relay_inbox_pull_failed` for every non-TLS send failure. `set_read_timeout` (`:759`) is **inert on a non-blocking socket**, so the 20 s grace the fixture believes it has does not exist in that state.
- **The house pattern already existed, three files away.** `tests/common/mod.rs:898-925` (`read_until_header_end`) tolerates `Interrupted | WouldBlock | TimedOut` and bounds the retry with a deadline. Of the five `set_nonblocking(true)` listener fixtures in the tree, na0742's was the only one that is **serial** (no thread per connection) **and** answers a failed read with **silence**. The repair is conformance, not invention.
- **Evidence, both arms, banked.** A Linux probe measured that `accept()` does **not** inherit `O_NONBLOCK` (listener `true` / accepted `false`), and a mechanism probe in which only the accepted socket's blocking mode varies: blocking ⇒ the client receives a 56-byte HTTP response; non-blocking ⇒ the client receives **0 bytes**, reproducing both observed symptoms exactly.
- ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY.** That macOS's `accept()` inherits the flag is **NOT measured** — no macOS host was available to the seat. Two other routes to the identical marker remain live and are indistinguishable in the banked log: any non-TLS send error, and any unmapped HTTP status (including the **502 this proxy itself emits** on upstream failure, `:838-842`). The repair narrows all three; it is not claimed to have discriminated among them.
- **Frequency, with the denominator corrected.** t5p has executed on a macOS main push **12 times** (11 green, 1 red) since `403432ce` (2026-08-17). A raw run list reads **24** green because **13 of 24** green runs skipped the shards on a docs-only classification — a run list counts RUNS, not EXECUTIONS.
- Remedy, **APPLIED in this lane**: clear the inherited flag after `accept()`; `read_head` adopts the house pattern (`Interrupted | WouldBlock | TimedOut` tolerated, deadline-bounded); and the file-scoped pull diagnostic below so the next opaque pull failure names its own reason.
- Status: **REPAIRED by NA-0759 (`D-1400`)** — fixture-only; **zero product bytes**. Classified `MACOS_FIXTURE_RACE_NOT_A_PRODUCT_REGRESSION` by the Director at the STOP-001 ruling.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0193`, `ENG-0196`, `ENG-0244`, `D-1379`, `D-1399`, `D-1400`, `NA-0742`, `NA-0757`.

### ENG-0245 — the published `LICENSE` is not the canonical FSF AGPL-3.0 text in three repositories, absent in a fourth, and the package metadata contradicts the claim in five manifests — **NEW; FILED AND CLOSED by NA-0760 (the NA-0758 audit's `LI-01`/`LI-02`/`LI-03`/`LI-04` rows, carried to a ledger entry for the first time)**

- Severity: **defect (published legal surface; the organisation's blessed front page states something its own repositories contradict)** — introduced at the initial public cut and never touched since.
- Description: NA-0758's public-docs audit measured the sentence *"Source is `AGPL-3.0-only`; see `LICENSE` in each repository"* FALSE four ways. `LI-01` — `qsl-protocol`, `qsl-desktop`, `qsl-server` shipped a byte-identical non-canonical `LICENSE` (sha256 `459cd3e088dbf32ab04873bd301295a08068dc4a7ea8e2610038d3923c2a2086`, 33,699 B / 651 l) differing in **four operative passages** (§2 `intact.`/`in force.`; §6 omitting `machine-readable`; `expected`/`common` use; §8 `License`/`section`) and missing the appendix's **closing 132 words**, the §13 network-source pointer among them. `LI-02` — `qsl-attachments` canonical but for one line-wrap at 636-637 (`cmp` → byte 33,213). `LI-03` — the `.github` repository, which publishes that very sentence, had **no `LICENSE` and no `NOTICE`**. `LI-04` — `qsc` declared `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, `quantumshield_refimpl` declared `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`, and `apps/qshield-cli`, `tools/actors/refimpl_actor_rs`, `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/fuzz` declared nothing.
- ⚠⚠ **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS.** The four operative deltas are not cosmetic: §8's `License`-for-`section` changes what a termination reaches, and the missing 132 words are the part of the appendix that tells a network-service operator how the §13 source obligation is met. A project whose entire posture is *"the proofs and the gaps both attached"* was publishing a licence text it had silently altered.
- Remedy (TAKEN): all five repositories now carry the canonical FSF bytes, sha256 `0d96a4ff68ad6d4b6f1f30f713b18d5184912ba8dd389f86aa7710db079abcb0` (34,523 B / 661 l), fetched live and **equal to the pin the audit recorded independently**; every workspace manifest declares `license = "AGPL-3.0-only"`; and the property is now **enforced by CI** rather than asserted once — `tests/na0760_workspace_license_agpl_only.rs` fails if any workspace crate answers `cargo metadata` with anything else, **red-arm proven** by a scratch-worktree control before its green was accepted.
- ⚠ **NOT fully closed in one dimension, stated rather than absorbed:** `qsl-server`'s root manifest still carries no `license` field. `LI-04` names it, but the governing order scoped that repository to *"LICENSE → canonical bytes. Nothing else."* That remainder is a later lane's. The root `Cargo.toml` of this repo is a virtual workspace with no `[package]` and is therefore not curable as a crate — reported, not skipped.
- Status: **closed** — filed and remedied 2026-08-25 by NA-0760 (`D-1401`), except the `qsl-server` root-manifest field named above.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0244`, `D-1401`, `NA-0758` census rows `LI-01`/`LI-02`/`LI-03`/`LI-04`/`LI-06`, `PR-06`, `OR-33`.
- Source: the NA-0758 public-docs audit, banked as `STOP_NA0758_003_20260825T033343Z.md` (sha256 `7c677cb1459afdb2bd791e209af6e025e65be571c7f35a24fa96393e22d5fefe`) — whose own handoff named this as *"the arm the Director must run"*, since a seat could not settle the licensing intent. He settled it: AGPL-3.0-only across the board.

### ENG-0246 — ⚠ P2 — the `public-safety` step-15 gate ASSERTS DEFINITE NEGATIVES ABOUT INPUTS IT COULD NOT READ, AND CONVERTS "not yet finished" INTO "is red" — **NEW; filed 2026-08-25 by NA-0761 (`D-1402`), drafted at NA-0760 STOP 002 §4.3 and ordered filed by the records-consolidation order and the NA-0758 + NA-0760 close-out. FILING ONLY — the cure is NOT performed here.**

- Severity: **defect (CI admission control; a required gate blocks correct PRs by publishing statements its own inputs do not support)** — long-standing; measured again on PR **#1793**, 2026-08-25.
- Description: On #1793 the required `public-safety` job settled at **14/15 green with one red, and the red was not the PR's content**. Step 9, the changed-content safety scan, **SUCCEEDED**; steps 10-14 skipped; **step 15 alone failed** — *"Block relevant PRs when latest main public-safety is red unless the PR clears live advisories"* (`.github/workflows/public-ci.yml:476`). The trigger was that main's own `public-safety` was **`in_progress`**, so the gate could not classify it as green, fell through to its bounded admission path, and that path failed for several independent reasons. **Two of the eleven ERROR/NOTE lines it printed are false statements derived from unreadable or untested inputs**, and they are this filing.
- ⚠⚠ **(a) THE GATE ANSWERS A QUESTION IT JUST FAILED TO READ.** The log emits, on consecutive lines: `NOTE: GitHub API 403 … "Resource not accessible by integration"` → `ERROR: branch protection required checks are unreadable (HTTP 403); cannot verify required PR checks` → `ERROR: branch protection required checks do not include public-safety`. **It does include it** — `public-safety` is one of main's fifteen required contexts, measured directly. **Mechanism, read from the source rather than inferred:** `scripts/ci/public_safety_gate.py:796-801` appends the unreadable-403 error and then **falls through** to `if "public-safety" not in required_contexts:` — a membership test against a list that is **empty precisely because the read failed**. An instrument that cannot see its input must say so and stop, not answer.
- ⚠⚠ **(b) THE SENTENCE ASSERTS A CONCLUSION ITS OWN GUARD NEVER TESTED.** The log emits `ERROR: latest main is red for a reason other than advisories; advisory-remediation PRs stay blocked`. **Main was not red**: it carried **0 failures** and its `public-safety` was simply unfinished; the gate's own preceding line says *"is **not completed/failure**"* — i.e. *"I could not classify this"* — and the next line converts that into *"is red"*. **Mechanism at source:** `public_safety_gate.py:1339-1343` guards on `main_advisories_status != "completed" or main_advisories_conclusion != "failure"` — a test of the **`advisories`** check — and then prints a sentence whose subject is **`latest main`**. A healthy green `advisories` satisfies that guard, so the sentence fires while asserting a redness nothing measured.
- ⇒ **"not yet finished" and "failed" are different states, and this gate collapses them.** The consequence is structural rather than cosmetic: **every PR whose `public-safety` runs in the window between a merge and that merge's full-suite settle is blocked by a main with nothing wrong with it.** On this repository that window is **~85 minutes** — #1792 merged 17:19:03Z and main's `public-safety` concluded 18:44:48Z, because it waits on the macOS shards. #1793's check ran inside that wake.
- ⚠⚠ **WHAT IS ALREADY IN REPO TRUTH, MEASURED AT THE FILING RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY — this entry is NOT the first sighting of either statement.** `ENG-0189`'s entry already carries **both**, added 2026-08-15 by NA-0734 (`D-1370`): the R332.3 paragraph records that the branch-protection line *"is FALSE as a standalone statement"* and explains the empty-list mechanism; the R332.2 paragraph records that *"an in-flight main is indistinguishable from a red one at that seam"*, measured on PR **#1749** at `status=in_progress conclusion=None`. That paragraph deliberately **minted no id** on the WF-0029 precedent (*the finding already exists; only the consequence is new*). ⚠ **The tension is named rather than hidden: this filing mints an id for a finding whose predecessor declined to, on the Director's explicit order at two governing documents.** If he prefers the WF-0029 shape, this entry folds into `ENG-0200` as a dated paragraph and the id retires — a one-line ruling, and the seat did not make it for him.
- ⛳ **WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS PART.** The predecessors describe an *unsettled* main and a *diagnostic nuisance*. On #1793 the main was **not red at all and not even ambiguous** — 0 failures throughout, concluding `success` at 18:44:48Z — and the PR was a docs-and-manifests change claiming **no** repair profile. So this is `ENG-0200`'s family (*a red main has no admission path for its own fix*) **with the premise removed: here there is no red main to have an admission path for.** The gate manufactures the blocking condition out of its own unreadiness.
- Remedy (**NOT TAKEN — this is a filing**): make both sites fail closed on unreadability instead of answering — refuse with the 403 as the stated reason rather than falling through to a membership test against an empty list; and separate `unknown`/`in_progress` from `failure` in the admission logic so an unfinished main is a **wait**, not a **red**. ⚠ **Location correction, measured:** the order's parenthetical places the cure in `.github/**`; only the step's *name* lives there (`public-ci.yml:476`). **The logic is `scripts/ci/public_safety_gate.py`** — an ordinary tracked file, not operator-owned and not settings-denied — at `:796-801`, `:814-815` and `:1339-1343`. The companion redesign already on record (retire the poll; post the check-run from a `workflow_run`-completion job when both suites conclude for the sha) subsumes (b) and is R282's.
- Status: **open — FILING ONLY.** No gate byte was changed by NA-0761, whose enumeration is docs/records only.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0200` (the family), `ENG-0189` (both prior sightings, R332.2 and R332.3), `ENG-0186` (a second inert admission arm in the same file), `ENG-0244` (the vacuous macOS rollup, confirmed a third time on the same PR), `NA-0716` (the original 403 investigation, which concluded the 403 *"was never the wall"*), `R282` (the redesign), `D-1401`, `D-1402`.
- Source: `STOP_NA0760_002_20260825T194500Z.md` §4.2-§4.4 (sha256 `d066df2f61ccfaf0f2bbc2b3d392e4512feab4da70d725c35dcab51d32160818`, 702 l / 53636 B, 444, sha-VERIFIED against its own bytes BEFORE being read), whose §15 row 252 records that the seat's **first** reading of this step quoted 2 of the 11 ERROR lines because an `awk` anchored on the step's display name returned **empty** — *an empty extraction reads exactly like "nothing to report"*. Every line quoted above is from the second, whole-block read.

### ENG-0247 — ⚠ P2 — the infra literal scanner AND ITS OWN SELFTEST ARE BLIND TO BINARY FILES, so a committed artifact carrying a build path passes both and the gate reports coverage it does not have — **NEW; FILED by NA-0765 (`D-1406`), owed from NA-0764 and ordered filed by the NA-0765 brief's sec 6(d). FILING ONLY — the cure is NOT performed here.**

- Severity: **defect (a gate whose green is narrower than its claim)** — measured live at NA-0764's step 3, 2026-08-27.
- Description: `scripts/ci/infra_literal_scan.py` reads candidate files as TEXT. A `.pyc` committed by accident at NA-0764 carried an **embedded absolute build path**, and the scanner reported the tree **clean**. The selftest that is supposed to prove the scanner can go red is written in the same text idiom, so it is blind in exactly the same way: **neither the instrument nor its own control could have seen the artifact.**
- ⚠⚠ **(a) THE GREEN WAS TRUE OF WHAT THE SCANNER READ AND FALSE OF THE TREE.** This is the instrument-narrower-than-the-claim family: the job's name and its summary line both say the tree is clean of infra literals; what was actually established is that the tree's **decodable text** is clean. A reader has no way to tell those apart from the output.
- ⚠ **(b) THE ENTRY POINT WAS A SECOND DEFECT, AND IT IS ALREADY CURED.** The `.pyc` reached the index through `git add -A`. NA-0764 cured that half at the source — staging by explicit path, plus a `.gitignore` entry — and this lane staged by explicit path for the same reason. The scanner's blindness is what survives, and it survives independently of how a binary arrives.
- Remedy (**NOT TAKEN — this is a filing**): decide the binary policy explicitly rather than by omission. Either REFUSE to scan a file whose bytes do not decode and fail closed naming it, or scan binaries with a byte-oriented needle. Whichever is chosen, **the selftest must plant its fixture in the same shape it now cannot see**, or the cure inherits the defect. ⚠ The remedy touches CI-adjacent scanning and is its own lane; the NA-0765 brief's sec 8 forbids repairing it here in as many words.
- ⚠⚠ **THE EXPOSURE ITSELF IS AN ACCEPTED RISK, AND THE RULING IS RECORDED VERBATIM SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED.** The operator's ruling on the path exposure the `.pyc` carried, in his own words: **"1, accept."** — recorded here beside the MEASURED string class rather than beside a description of it. **THE MEASURED CLASS IS `host_build`**, established by running the scanner's own classifier: an absolute build path carrying the build host's name returns `['host_build']`, the host name alone returns `['host_build']`, and — the negative control that makes the answer mean something — the ACCOUNT name alone returns `[]`, so the class keys on the HOST and not on the account or on the path prefix. ⇒ the accepted risk is precisely a `host_build` disclosure, not a generic "path leak", and a successor deciding whether that acceptance still covers a new sighting can compare classes rather than prose.
- ⚠ **ACCEPTING THE EXPOSURE IS NOT ACCEPTING THE BLINDNESS.** The ruling above disposes of the ONE artifact. It says nothing about a gate that cannot see the next one, which is what this entry files.
- Status: **open — FILING ONLY.** No scanner byte was changed by NA-0765, whose desktop diff is UI plus two command-registration lines and whose protocol diff is records only.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0244` (a named rollup reporting success having executed zero tests — the same family: a gate whose green covers less than its name), `ENG-0246` (a gate asserting conclusions its own inputs did not support), `ENG-0200` (the family).
- Source: `STOP_NA0765_001_20260827T045720Z.md` (sha256 `007d0086ea498575b9a11dfa75b440b642a5ebf7e3b3b991b8866565db81ca56`, 793 l / 59986 B, 444, sha-VERIFIED against its own bytes BEFORE being read) and the NA-0764 step-3 measurement it carries; ordered filed by `BRIEF_laneC_repairs_20260827.md` sec 6(d) (sha256 `0e3c5ac5f48d5e77687aed0c4b189b6a21990be42ea6a19c5362ff3ce94b59b8`) and authorized a home by `RULING_NA0765_build_20260827.md` R-3 (sha256 `7d652957b1d90a9f7ce47404e7fdda8c8e37b74e66b9056fa8fe714333bca217`).

### ENG-0248 — ⚠ P2 — the HONEST block/unblock pair exists in the engine and is ABSENT FROM THE FACADE, so the desktop can only reach a one-way DESTRUCTIVE block — and a blessed screen's copy is false against it — **NEW; FILED by NA-0765 (`D-1406`) as the successor lane's subject, on the R-1 = Option A ruling. FILING ONLY — no facade byte is changed here.**

- Severity: **gap (a blessed UI control cannot be built truthfully at the shipped pin)** — measured 2026-08-27 at qsl-protocol `b3ae24b430e516d9b43bb654905c7992beb59ce7`, and **independently confirmed by the Director from his own chair at the same base**.
- Description: `MOCKUP_laneC_repairs_v2_20260827.html` draws a blocked contact with an **Unblock** control captioned *"Blocked contacts can't reach you. Unblocking restores the connection you already had."* That sentence cannot be made true with what the desktop can reach.
- ⛳ **(a) THE RIGHT VERBS EXIST.** `contacts_block` (`qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:1541`) and `contacts_unblock` (`:1551`) are `pub`, symmetric and non-destructive: both delegate to `contacts_set_blocked(label, bool)` (`:480`), which flips `rec.blocked` and touches **nothing else**.
- ⚠⚠ **(b) NEITHER IS IN THE FACADE, WHICH IS THE DESKTOP'S ONLY DOOR.** Measured: **0 hits each** in `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/facade/mod.rs`, with `contact_set_display_name` returning **1** on the same needle as the positive control — so the absence is a measurement rather than a failed search. `contacts_set_blocked` itself is `pub(super)`.
- ⚠⚠ **(c) THE ONE REACHABLE VERB IS THE WRONG ONE, IN THREE SEPARATE WAYS.** `facade::contact_request_block` (`:680`) belongs to the contact-REQUEST family that **`D-1405` itself names as *"NOT this flow ... dead surface, zero UI call sites"***; it is **one-way** — no request-family unblock exists anywhere in the facade or the engine; and it is **destructive**, writing `primary.state = "REVOKED"` (`contacts/mod.rs:1694-1696`) alongside the block. The only unblock path, `contacts_set_blocked(label, false)`, clears `blocked` and does **not** restore that device state. ⇒ **a user who blocked and then unblocked would not get back the connection the screen promised.**
- ⇒ **THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MADE THIS A FILING RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND.** NA-0765 refused to ship the control at all — no half-block, no one-way destructive stand-in — because a control whose blessed copy is measurably untrue is worse than an absent one. The absence is asserted structurally in the desktop so a later lane cannot add one silently.
- Remedy (**NOT TAKEN — this is a filing**): expose the honest pair as two thin facade wrappers over the verbs that already exist, then wire the blessed screen in the desktop. ⚠ **It is a LANE, not a rider**: it costs protocol product bytes, a qsc pin bump with the `ORDER_NA0764_P1` two-stage merge choreography, `goal-lint`'s CORE-path demand (a `qsc/src/**` byte hard-requires TRACEABILITY.md + DECISIONS.md + a `tests/` file in the SAME PR), and it takes the product-source count to seven, **which triggers SR-15**.
- Status: **open — FILING ONLY.** Zero protocol product bytes were changed by NA-0765.

### ENG-0249 — ⚠ P2 — the infra literal scanner IDENTIFIES THE REPOSITORY IT IS SCANNING BY FOLDER NAME, so it can fail red on a clean tree or pass a foreign one, with nothing in its output naming the cause — **NEW; FILED by NA-0766 (`D-1407`), owed from NA-0765 and ordered filed by the invite-flow brief's sec 6(b) and the NA-0764/NA-0765 close-out's sec 6. FILING ONLY — the cure is `.github`-adjacent and is its own lane.**

- Severity: **a REQUIRED gate whose verdict depends on a property of the CHECKOUT rather than of the TREE** — measured 2026-08-27 across two lanes and two seats.
- Description: `scripts/ci/infra_literal_scan.py::_repo_name()` reads `remote.origin.url` and, when there is no `origin`, **falls back to the checkout's DIRECTORY NAME**. Its Tier-1 allowlist is keyed on `digest("<repo>:<path>")`, so a wrong repo name makes **every allowlist key miss at once**.
- ⚠⚠ **(a) IT FAILS CLOSED IN ONE DIRECTION, ON A TREE WITH NOTHING WRONG WITH IT.** A seat that deliberately has no `origin` — which is the standing cure for the stale-mirror trap, since a seat's `origin` is the LOCAL MIRROR and not GitHub — resolves to its directory name, and a REQUIRED gate reads **red on an untouched tree**. Proven both arms at NA-0765: adding `origin` = the real GitHub URL made `_repo_name()` resolve to `qsl-protocol` and `--mode tree` exit **0, clean, 659,848 lines**.
- ⚠⚠ **(b) IT FAILS OPEN IN THE OTHER, WHICH IS THE WORSE HALF.** A checkout of repo A sitting in a directory named `qsl-protocol` silently **inherits qsl-protocol's allowlist**, so waivers granted to one repository are honoured for another. Nothing in the output distinguishes this from a genuine pass.
- ⚠ **(c) THE FAILURE NAMES NO CAUSE.** Nothing the scanner prints mentions the repo identity it derived, which is why the red at NA-0765 was first suspected to be in the tree and cost a diagnosis before it was traced to the seat. ⇒ *when a local gate disagrees with CI, suspect the SEAT before the tree, and check what the gate derives from the remote.*
- ⛳ **REPRODUCED TWICE, BY TWO ROUTES, IN TWO LANES.** At NA-0765 as a live red on a clean tree; at NA-0766 as a **pre-empted** defect — that lane's seats were cut with `origin` AND a named `github` remote **both pointing at the real GitHub URL**, which kills the stale-mirror trap and the folder-name trap in one act. That workaround is a seat convention, not a fix: it protects seats that remember to apply it and nothing else.
- Recommended change (**NOT implemented** — filing only, at operator instruction): derive the repository identity from an explicit argument or a checked-in marker, and **REFUSE rather than guess** when it cannot be determined; at minimum, PRINT the derived repo name so a wrong one is visible in the log.
- Related: `ENG-0247` (the same scanner, blind to binary files — filed by NA-0765); `ENG-0244` (a named rollup reporting success having executed zero tests). Both are instances of the same family: **a gate whose output does not describe what it actually checked.**

### ENG-0250 — ⚠ P1 — THE INVITER'S SESSION IS NEVER BUILT: the act that builds it is a HANDSHAKE POLL over the inviter's own inbox, and NO SHIPPED DESKTOP TRIGGER PERFORMS ONE — **NEW; FILED by NA-0767 (`D-1408`), measured on loopback at protocol `94e50aa7` / desktop `11f695df`. FILING ONLY — no repair is proposed and none is authorised by this lane.**

- Severity: **P1 — the product's central promise ("two people connect with no terminal") completes on ONE side only.** The redeemer reaches a session; the inviter never does, and no amount of waiting changes it.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` (the two `qsp_session_store` sites, `:1928` and `:2167`); `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/invite/mod.rs::invite_accept_at` (`:1295`); desktop `ui/main.js::SCAN_CLASSES` (`:3363`) and `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`'s `generate_handler!` registry (`:333`).
- ⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, FROM THE ENGINE'S OWN EMISSION SITES.** The handshake is THREE messages — A1 (`HsInit`), B1 (`HsResp`), A2 (`HsConfirm`) — and the two sides build their sessions at DIFFERENT messages:
  - the INITIATOR (the redeemer) builds and stores at **B1**: `handshake/mod.rs:1928` `qsp_session_store`, then pushes A2 and emits `handshake_complete role=initiator peer_confirmed=no`. `invite_finish` feeds that branch, so the redeemer completes inside her own shipped scan class.
  - the RESPONDER (the inviter) builds and stores at **A2, and NOWHERE ELSE**: `handshake/mod.rs:2167` `qsp_session_store`, emitting `handshake_complete role=responder peer_confirmed=yes`. Her A1 branch (`:2429`) stores only a PENDING record — `pending_session: Some(st.snapshot_bytes())` via `hs_pending_store` — and pushes B1. The source says so in its own words at `:2185`: *"the responder branch's last effect IS the durable commit … with NO push following."*
  - ⇒ the inviter's session requires an act that CONSUMES AN A2 FROM HER OWN INBOX. The only such act in the codebase is `handshake::perform_handshake_poll_with_tokens` reached via `handshake poll`.
- ⚠⚠ **AND NO SHIPPED DESKTOP TRIGGER PERFORMS IT, measured from bytes with both controls.** `SCAN_CLASSES = [finishScanClass, autoConnectClass]` (`ui/main.js:3363`). The registry at `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:333` holds **43** commands and **ZERO** match `handshake` or `poll` (positive control on the same needle set: `invite`=7, `contact`=6); `git grep -E 'handshake_poll|handshake::poll|facade::handshake' -- 'src-tauri/**'` returns **zero**. For the INVITER role the two shipped classes do this and only this: `autoConnectClass` calls `invite_accept` (the ACCEPT — which processes A1 and pushes B1, building NO session), and `finishScanClass` calls `invite_finish` (the REDEEMER's verb), which cannot consume an A2 — see `ENG-0251`.
- ⛳ **MEASURED END TO END ON LOOPBACK, BOTH PEERS, SIX CHECKPOINTS, n=2 complete flows.** Every status compared BY EQUALITY on the extracted value. The inviter reads `status=no_session peer_confirmed=no send_ready=no send_ready_reason=no_session pinned=true` at X2, X3 and X4 — **which is the operator's field line reproduced exactly** — while the redeemer reads `awaiting_peer_confirm / send_ready=yes` from X3 onward. Store accounting `routes/rows/unexplained` was complete at every checkpoint, `unexplained=0` throughout.
- ⛳ **THE MISSING ACT IS NAMED AND PROVEN SUFFICIENT — WITH A BOUND.** A single `handshake poll` on the inviter, run OUTSIDE the tick's lease window, completes her: `handshake_recv msg=A2 ok=true` → `session_store ok=true` → `handshake_complete role=responder peer_confirmed=yes`. ⚠ **But completing it does NOT make her able to send:** she reads `status=established_recv_only send_ready=no send_ready_reason=chainkey_unset`. So "add the missing trigger" yields a RECEIVE-ONLY inviter, not a connected one. That bound is measured, not inferred, and it is why this entry does not recommend a repair.
- ⚠⚠ **AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS DEFEATED BY `ENG-0251`** — appending a handshake-poll class to `SCAN_CLASSES` places it AFTER `finishScanClass`, which leases the very A2 the new class would need, in the same beat. The two entries must be read together.
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED.** This is a measurement lane; the design is the operator's to rule on.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-27 by NA-0767 (`D-1408`).
- Cross-references: `ENG-0251` (the lease that starves the poll); `ENG-0198` (`handshake poll` returns rc 0 while completing nothing — this lane measured a NEW cause of that shape); `ENG-0226` (no fixture relay, which is why this could not be driven through the GUI); `D-1404` (NA-0763's R1, whose recorded bound this lane corrects).
- Source: NA-0767 STOP 001, measured from the engine's own emission sites and from two complete loopback flows.
- ⚖ **RULED 2026-08-27** (`RULING_NA0767_20260827.md`, sha256 `a1bfa391d9bba36f28ea86e1109bb3756198331f50548c882c8ab0f3cfb75d1c`): filed as its own entry, distinct from `ENG-0251`, on `R338`'s identity test. Design direction ruled **A, with no interim step** — one fetch per beat dispatched by frame type. The origin is a deviation from the banked design of record, named by the Director as his own (SR-16 rows 356/357). The design of record is amended by `AMENDMENT_1_delivery_ladder_20260827.md`, sha256 `440b101929601704babbe356c5730746a5af2404ce51081e97544dd5f3952feb`, banked 444 — **cited, not transcribed; the banked file is the text.** ⚠ NOT CLOSED. The repair is the successor lane's, with its own design pass and bless.
- ⚠⚠ **TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS NOW BIND THIS ENTRY'S REPAIR — CROSS-REFERENCE ADDED 2026-08-28 BY NA-0769 (`D-1410`), NOT A DUPLICATE, AND THIS ENTRY IS NOT CLOSED, NOT RE-GRADED AND NOT EDITED ABOVE.** Whatever repair eventually builds the inviter's session must satisfy both: **(1) `ENG-0252`** — the act that consumes an A2 is the handshake poll, and the poll destroys the addressed pending record on an unauthenticated context mismatch at `handshake/mod.rs:2066`, which is the **responder** branch, i.e. **the inviter's own record on the very path this entry's repair must run**; **(2) `ENG-0253`** — any beat that *scans* this mailbox must carry an `AckMode` arm, because retiring `invite_finish` removes the only site in the invite flow that branches the pull shape on ack mode. ⚠ Neither is a defect this program introduced, and neither is repaired by NA-0769, which files only.
- Status: CLOSED 2026-09-03 by NA-0778 (`D-1421`, the Invitations lane's records act; ruled at `RULING_NA0778_001` R4 on `STOP_NA0778_001` sec 8.1), on NA-0768's landed repair (protocol PR #1808, merge `63ece4fe`, merged_at 2026-08-30T17:17:41Z; desktop PR #47 `ac03da05`) and the operator-attested fourth flight X0-X4 HIT recorded at NA-0768's block in `NEXT_ACTIONS.md` (class `INVITER_FINISH_HANDS_OFF_FLOWN_PASS`, finalized by `D-1417`). The filed act -- an A2 consumed from the inviter's own inbox by a shipped trigger -- now happens inside `invite_finish`: the handshake-class frames its scan already pulled are offered to a bounded candidate set within the call that pulled them (`HsPollSource::ProvidedSpeculative`, `handshake/mod.rs:1702`; the offer at `invite/mod.rs:1573`) and acked only on a two-shape witness, measured at `2c3c39b4`. NOT closed by this line: `ENG-0278`, `ENG-0262`, `ENG-0263`, `ENG-0264`; the recv-only bound this entry measured (`status=established_recv_only send_ready=no`) stands as Connected by D5-A and its send half is messaging's; n=1 post-fix flight; the harness cannot reach a completed handshake, so the harness cures are proven by A/B only. ### ENG-0251 — ⚠ P1 — THE SHIPPED TICK LEASES THE INVITER'S A2 AND DECLINES IT, so a handshake poll arriving inside the lease sees an EMPTY MAILBOX and no-ops at rc 0 — **NEW; FILED by NA-0767 (`D-1408`), measured on loopback with a two-arm control. FILING ONLY.**

- Severity: **P1 — it starves the exact act `ENG-0250` shows is missing, and it would defeat the obvious repair for it.** Filed separately from `ENG-0250` on the `R338` identity test: a DIFFERENT mechanism (a lease taken and abandoned, vs an act never performed) and a DIFFERENT repair surface (scan/ack semantics and class ordering, vs a trigger). Buried inside `ENG-0250` it would die on that entry's closure.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/invite/mod.rs::finish_scan_select_invite_resp` (`:1212`); `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/frameclass.rs::classify` (`:61`); desktop `ui/main.js::finishScanClass` (`:2873`) and the beat constants at `:1912`/`:1929`.
- ⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM.** Every tick beat, `finishScanClass` calls `invite_finish` for each contact whose `connect_status.state` reads `inactive` — which the inviter's new contact does. Under `AckMode::Lease` that runs `finish_scan_select_invite_resp`, which PULLS the inviter's inbox (taking a `PULL_LEASE_SECS` lease on what it pulls), classifies each frame, and selects **only** `FrameClass::InviteResp`. The inviter's A2 classifies as `Handshake` (`classify()` returns `FrameClass::Handshake` for any frame whose first four bytes are `HS_MAGIC`, and an A2 is `51 48 53 4D 00 01 03 …`). It is therefore **not selected — and, by that function's own documented contract, "left completely untouched — not acked, not consumed, not decoded."** What the contract does NOT say is that it has already been LEASED by the pull that read it.
- ⛳ **MEASURED, WITH BOTH ARMS OF A CONTROL THAT DIFFER ONLY IN THE PRECEDING TICK.**
  - ARM A (tick beat, then poll): the tick emitted `invite_scan_summary scanned=1 pulls=1 truncated=false selected=none classes=handshake` — it SAW the A2 and declined it — and the store showed the row `LEASED(until=1787858776, +59s)`. The poll that followed emitted `handshake_recv msg=none ok=true`, **rc 0**, and completed nothing; the row was STILL leased to the same instant afterwards, unconsumed.
  - ARM B (no tick, then the identical poll): `handshake_recv msg=A2 ok=true` → `session_store ok=true` → `handshake_complete role=responder peer_confirmed=yes`. The inviter completed on the first attempt.
  - ⇒ the two arms differ ONLY in the preceding tick beat. The lease is the cause, by control rather than by inference.
- ⚠⚠ **THE FIELD CADENCE MAKES THIS THE COMMON CASE, NOT AN EDGE.** `TICK_DEFAULT = "instant"` and `TICK_TEMPO.instant = { b: 20000, j: 5000 }` (`ui/main.js:1912-1929`), so the shipped beat is **15–25 s**; the AWS relay's `PULL_LEASE_SECS` is **60** (proven from the store's own `leased_until` column — `server-info` does not advertise it). A beat therefore recurs roughly three times per lease period. Measured duty cycle over a 150 s window under the shipped cadence: see `NA-0767_as_built.md` §5. The A2 was never consumed and never acked for the whole window.
- ⚠⚠ **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OBVIOUS REPAIR, STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISSED:** `SCAN_CLASSES` is a LIST and `relayScanOnce` runs its members IN ORDER. A handshake-poll class APPENDED to it runs AFTER `finishScanClass` in the same beat — after the lease has just been taken. **The naive repair for `ENG-0250` is defeated by this entry.** Any fix must address ordering, or the finish-scan's treatment of frames it declines, or both.
- ⚠ **RELATIONSHIP TO `ENG-0198`.** `ENG-0198` records that `handshake poll` can return rc 0 while completing nothing. This lane measured that shape with a **new and different cause**: not frames rejected, but **no frames returned at all**, because the shipped tick was holding the lease. `ENG-0198`'s entry should not be closed on the assumption that its one recorded cause is its only one.
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED** — measurement lane; the design is the operator's.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-27 by NA-0767 (`D-1408`).
- Cross-references: `ENG-0250`, `ENG-0198`, `ENG-0196`, `ENG-0142` (the skip-and-leave-leased family), `D-1378` (NA-0742, which introduced the drain-forward scan).
- Source: NA-0767 STOP 001 §4 and §5, two-arm control plus a 150 s duty-cycle window.
- ⚖ **RULED 2026-08-27** (`RULING_NA0767_20260827.md`, sha256 `a1bfa391d9bba36f28ea86e1109bb3756198331f50548c882c8ab0f3cfb75d1c`): kept as its own entry because **it SURVIVES the repair of `ENG-0250`** — which is precisely why the obvious fix would have failed. The design of record is amended for it by `AMENDMENT_1_delivery_ladder_20260827.md`, sha256 `440b101929601704babbe356c5730746a5af2404ce51081e97544dd5f3952feb`, banked 444 at `/srv/qbuild/operator/method/` beside the unedited design doc — **cited, not transcribed or paraphrased; the banked file is the text**, and the successor cites the amended text rather than the superseded sentence. ⚠ NOT CLOSED.
- ⚠ **A SEAT OBSERVATION, REPORTED NOT RULED:** the design doc's sec **1.2 (the lease law)** already stated that a pulled-unacked item is invisible until expiry and ruled that the steady-state tick *"must not undercut the deployed lease WHILE never-ack pull paths exist"*. That antecedent measures TRUE at this base — this entry's own mechanism IS a never-ack pull path (`finish_scan_select_invite_resp`'s contract says the declined frame is *"not acked"*; run C measured **zero** `producer_ack` markers across 8 beats) — while the shipped beat is 15–25 s against the deployed 60 s lease. So the banked design anticipated the lease MECHANISM even though it did not anticipate the DISPATCH shape. `AMENDMENT_1` governs the subject; this entry rules nothing.
- ⚠⚠ **THE SAME TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS BIND HERE — CROSS-REFERENCE ADDED 2026-08-28 BY NA-0769 (`D-1410`); NOTHING CLOSED, NOTHING EDITED ABOVE.** This entry's repair changes what a beat does with a pulled handshake frame, so it inherits both: **`ENG-0253`** (a beat that scans must branch on `AckMode`, or state why Legacy is unreachable) and **`ENG-0252`** (a frame this beat routes to the poll can destroy the addressed pending record before any cryptographic check). ⚠ **The interaction is the sharp one and is stated so it cannot be missed:** this entry records that the tick *leases and declines* the inviter's A2. Under `AckMode::Legacy` there is no lease — the frame is **deleted at pull** — so the symptom this entry measured changes shape entirely and its two-arm control would not reproduce. ⇒ **the deployed `ack_mode` (owed at `ENG-0253`) is load-bearing for this entry's own reproduction, not only for its repair.**
- Status: CLOSED 2026-09-03 by NA-0778 (`D-1421`; `RULING_NA0778_001` R4 on `STOP_NA0778_001` sec 8.2). The mechanism this entry filed -- the finish-scan leases the inviter's A2 and declines it, so nothing consumes it inside the lease -- is cured on the entry's own second surface ("the finish-scan's treatment of frames it declines"): NA-0768 (`D-1409`, #1808, merge `63ece4fe`) made the finish-scan OFFER the handshake-class frames it pulled (`HsPollSource::ProvidedSpeculative`, `invite/mod.rs:1573`) within the call that pulled them, acking only on a two-shape witness; a frame no candidate consumes gets `invite_finish_hs_unconsumed{candidates=N}` (`invite/mod.rs:1661`) and is left to redeliver. Flown X1 HIT (inviter, NO CLICK, within the three-beat window). NOT closed by this line: `ENG-0262` (the lease footprint the scan still takes); the unconsumed-frame redelivery path (`ENG-0198`'s family); and the two owed acts of NA-0768's own objective that `RULING_NA0778_001` R4(i) records beside NA-0768's block in `NEXT_ACTIONS.md` so they do not decay inside a closed entry -- R1(a)'s second half (the handshake-poll class, never shipped) and R1(b) (the lease law, never re-derived; absent at n=2 needles at `2c3c39b4`). The `- Status: open` bullet above is NOT rewritten; this bullet is the entry's current state. Ratified by the operator's merge of NA-0778's promotion PR.

### ENG-0252 — THE UNGATED DESTRUCTIVE CLEAR: A FRAME CARRYING NOTHING BUT A PUBLIC 16-BYTE CORRELATOR AND ARBITRARY BYTES DESTROYS THE ADDRESSED HANDSHAKE PENDING RECORD, BEFORE ANY CRYPTOGRAPHIC OPERATION OF ANY KIND — **NEW; FILED by NA-0769 (`D-1410`) on the SR-15 cold reads of NA-0768, re-measured from the bytes by this seat as a third instrument. FILING ONLY — no repair is performed and none is authorised by this lane.**

⚠⚠ **THIS DEFECT WAS NOT INTRODUCED BY THE PROGRAM'S CURRENT WORK.** It is reachable today, at the bases below, through shipped code. NA-0768 surfaced it; it did not create it. Any record implying otherwise is wrong and must be corrected.

- Severity: **P1** — ⚠⚠ **ASSIGNED 2026-08-28 BY THE OPERATOR, RELAYED THROUGH NA-0770 (`D-1411`) AS A RIDER.** This field read **OWED** from filing until that ruling; the previous wording is preserved immediately below, unedited, because the *reason* it was owed is part of this entry's record and a bare `P1` would erase it.
- ⚠⚠ **THIS ENTRY IS NOT CLOSED, AND NA-0770 DID NOT REPAIR IT.** NA-0770 retired `AckMode::Legacy`; `ENG-0252` is the **ungated destructive clear**, a different defect on a different surface (`handshake/mod.rs`). The retirement changes one thing about it and only one: a hostile frame exploiting it is no longer *destroyed at pull* on a delete-on-pull relay, so the hazard's outcome is now uniformly "leased and redelivered" rather than mode-dependent. That REMOVES A VARIABLE FROM THE SEVERITY ARGUMENT — it does not remove the defect. Repair remains owed and unscheduled.
- *(superseded severity line, kept verbatim)* Severity: **NOT ASSIGNED BY THIS SEAT — OWED.** The Director proposes and the operator rules (brief sec 3(a), verbatim: *"The seat states the measured facts and does NOT assign a severity number"*). ⚠ The field is present rather than omitted **on purpose**: `ENG-0142` records that an entry carrying no `- Severity:` bullet was *"uncountable by the triage instrument for six days"*, so the needle must find a field here even while its value is owed. ⚠⚠ **Severity is bounded below by two UNMEASURED operator figures — see the OWED block.**
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `503dcdadeca2a15aaf3f177913cf26c564461c3e`, qsl-desktop main `11f695dfcb3e6c1f3b3ff78a14eee71e878b0439`, each re-derived bare and unpiped at the NAMED `github` remote, 40/40 digits compared, comparator negative-controlled.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` — the clear at **`:1778`** (initiator branch) and **`:2066`** (responder branch); the matcher `hs_contexts_match` at **`:1272-1281`** with its `_ => false` arm at **`:1279`**; the header decoder `hs_decode_header` at `:456-501`; the admission-false wrappers `hs_decode_resp_pending` at `:650` and `hs_decode_confirm_pending` at `:705`; the reason emitter `hs_reject_context_mismatch` at `:1283-1285`. Reachability today via `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/invite/mod.rs::decode_envelope_resp` at `:769-803`.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE BYTES.** In both role branches the poll compares the frame's 16-byte `session_id` against the addressed pending record's, and then — with **no `is_explicit()` gate and no cryptographic check** — compares suite contexts and destroys the record if they differ. Verbatim, the initiator branch:

```
if resp.session_id != pending.session_id {                        // :1762  the correlator
    emit_marker("handshake_reject", None, &[("reason","session_id_mismatch")]);
    continue;
}
if suite_mode == HandshakeSuiteMode::SuiteRequired                // :1768  a SEPARATE `if`
    && !pending_suite_context.is_explicit()
{ let _ = hs_pending_clear(self_label, peer); ... return Ok(()); } // :1773  its OWN clear
if !hs_contexts_match(&pending_suite_context, &resp.suite_context) {   // :1777
    let _ = hs_pending_clear(self_label, peer);                   // :1778  ⚠ UNGATED
    hs_reject_context_mismatch();
    return Ok(());
}
```

The responder branch at `:2050-2069` is identical in shape, with the clear at **`:2066`** and `continue` in place of `return`. ⚠ **THE `is_explicit()` CHECK ABOVE THE CLEAR DOES NOT GUARD IT.** It is a separate `if` with its own `hs_pending_clear`; nothing conditions `:1778`/`:2066` on the record being explicit, on the suite mode, or on anything the peer had to prove.

⚠⚠ **THE DISTANCE FROM CORRELATOR MATCH TO RECORD DESTRUCTION IS FOUR STATEMENTS, AND THE COUNTING METHOD IS STATED SO THE FIGURE CAN BE CHECKED.** Counting top-level statements of the `Ok(..)` arm of the decode `match`, inclusive of the correlator test and of the clear itself: **(1)** the `session_id` equality `if` (`:1762`), **(2)** the `SuiteRequired && !is_explicit` `if` (`:1768`, evaluated and false on the invite path), **(3)** the `hs_contexts_match` `if` (`:1777`), **(4)** `hs_pending_clear` (`:1778`). ⇒ **four**.

⚠⚠ **AND THE DESTRUCTION PRECEDES EVERY CRYPTOGRAPHIC OPERATION, MEASURED BY LINE ORDER.** On the initiator branch the first cryptographic call after the clear is `c.decap(&pending.kem_sk, &resp.kem_ct)` at **`:1784`** — six lines BELOW the clear at `:1778`. On the responder branch the first is `hs_confirm_mac(...)` at **`:2087`** with its constant-time compare at `:2093` — twenty-one lines BELOW the clear at `:2066`. ⇒ **no decapsulation, no transcript MAC, no signature verification, and no confirm MAC runs before the record is gone.**

⚠⚠ **WHY AN ARBITRARY FRAME REACHES THE `_ => false` ARM.** `hs_decode_header` consults `mode` only in its LEGACY arm (`:467-475`); the V2 arm does not. Under the invite path's hardcoded `LegacyCompat` a wire-version-2 frame is therefore accepted by the header decoder. Both poll decoders pass `admit_context = **false**` (`hs_decode_resp_pending` at `:650`, `hs_decode_confirm_pending` at `:705`), so the parameter-block parser at `:490` is **never reached** and the decoder instead builds, verbatim at `:492-496`:

```
HsSuiteContext::ExplicitV2 { block: block.to_vec(), protocol_version: 0, suite_id: 0 }
```

for **any** block of length `<= HS_PARAM_BLOCK_MAX` (64). The local pending record on the invite path is `LegacyV1`. `hs_contexts_match(LegacyV1, ExplicitV2)` falls to `_ => false` at `:1279` ⇒ **CLEAR.** The frame is well-formed by every length rule the decoder applies: its total length is exactly `9 + block_len + payload_len`.

⚠⚠ **THE ATTACKER'S COMPLETE BILL OF MATERIALS — this is the whole of it:**
  1. **The self-inbox route token**, which is *"the one published in invites"* (the NA-0768 ruling's own H1 statement of reachability).
  2. **The 16-byte `session_id`**, which travels the relay **in the clear** — measured: it is the FIRST payload field of **all three** handshake frame types, read at a fixed offset immediately after the header (`:541` INIT, `:626` RESP, `:685` CONFIRM, each `sid.copy_from_slice(&bytes[off..off + 16])`). The relay operator holds it, a network observer at the relay boundary holds it, and the counterparty holds it.
  3. **Arbitrary bytes** for the remainder of the payload. **No key, no MAC, no signature.**

⚠⚠ **THE VICTIM-VISIBLE SYMPTOM: A CONNECTION THAT NEVER COMPLETES, WITH NOTHING SAYING WHY.** The pending record is the state the whole completion depends on; without it that contact can never complete. `hs_pending_clear` writes `""` rather than deleting (`handshake/mod.rs:1205`, and `ENG-0176` records the same property), so the loader thereafter reports the record as absent. The poll returns **rc 0**. ⇒ the shape is `ENG-0198`'s — *"rc 0 while completing nothing"* — arriving by a **third** cause; see the cross-reference appended to that entry, which is NOT closed.

⚠⚠ **PRE-EXISTING REACHABILITY, STATED FAIRLY AND WITHOUT OVERSTATEMENT.** The clear is reachable **today**, with no change from any current lane, through the shipped `invite_finish` path: `decode_envelope_resp` (`invite/mod.rs:769-803`) is a TLV parse — a version byte, a type byte, a tag/length/value loop and a route-token normalisation — and performs **no cryptographic verification of any kind** (read in full by this seat; there is no signature check, no MAC, no decapsulation). A hostile `01 02` envelope wrapping a crafted frame therefore already reaches the poll. ⚠ **What a future design that routes raw self-inbox frames by class would change is only that the envelope-wrapping step is no longer needed — the widening is modest, and the defect is not created by it.**

- ⚠ **THE FULL SET OF REASONS THAT CAN CLEAR AN ADDRESSED RECORD IS SIX, NOT FOUR** — enumerated and classified in `D-1410`, whose table gives each reason its call sites and its gate. `REJECT_QSC_HS_CONTEXT_MISMATCH` is the **only ungated member**, and it is the subject of this entry.
- ⚠⚠ **OWED OPERATOR MEASUREMENTS, NAMED AND NOT TAKEN — BOTH ARE LOAD-BEARING FOR SEVERITY:** (i) which `ack_mode` the **deployed** configuration actually uses; (ii) the relay's deployed `retention_ttl_secs`. Neither has been measured by any lane. (i) decides whether a hostile push is destroyed at pull or merely leased; (ii) bounds how long a finite flood survives. ⇒ **any severity assigned before these two are measured is assigned on an unmeasured basis.**
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED.** The reads name candidate remedies (a version-agreement check in a resolver; pinning the invite path's suite mode) and this lane **chooses among none of them**. Both are crypto-region work and each carries its own ceremony.
