### ⏹ CLOSED BY RETIREMENT 2026-08-28 (NA-0770 / `D-1411`) — ENG-0253 — UNDER `AckMode::Legacy` THE RELAY DELETES ON PULL, SO ANY BEAT THAT *SCANS* THE SELF INBOX DESTROYS EVERY FRAME IT PULLS: THE SHIPPED `invite_finish` GATE IS THE ONLY THING IN THE INVITE FLOW THAT BRANCHES THE PULL SHAPE ON ACK MODE, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING — **NEW; FILED by NA-0769 (`D-1410`). FILING ONLY — nothing is repaired, and the shipped gate is NOT touched.**

⏹⏹ **CLOSED BY RETIREMENT, NOT BY REPAIR — 2026-08-28, NA-0770 (`D-1411`). NOTHING BELOW IS EDITED.**
> **Severity at close: `P2`, CONDITIONAL.** Conditional because it was never unconditional: this entry's own `DV-8` block records that severity here was bounded below by an **unmeasured** operator figure — which `ack_mode` the deployed configuration actually used. That figure has since been given by the operator (2026-08-28): **neither field machine carries an ack-mode config at all**, so both ran the lease default and the hazard was **latent, never live**, for the whole life of this entry. `P2` is recorded as the severity the hazard **would have carried** had the deployed configuration selected Legacy; it is not a claim that anything was ever destroyed.
>
> **What closes it:** `AckMode::Legacy` is deleted from the client. The two-arm URL quoted below no longer exists — `transport/mod.rs` now builds ONE pull URL and it carries `&ack=lease` unconditionally, pinned by guard **G-A** in `tests/na0770_legacy_retirement_guards.rs` (singleness AND the parameter, red arm proven both ways). There is no longer a mode under which a scanning beat could delete what it fetched, so the forward-looking clause this entry was filed for **cannot be reached**, by any future beat, without first re-introducing the mode — which G-A turns red.
>
> ⚠ **THE CLOSURE IS SCOPED TO THE CLIENT.** The relay still honours a pull without `ack=lease` by deleting (its `None => PullMode::Legacy` default arm is untouched — NA-0770 wrote zero relay bytes). What is gone is any way for **this client** to ask for that. A different client, or a future one, could still ask. If the relay's default arm is ever the subject of a lane, this entry is its precedent, not its closure.

⚠⚠ **THIS ENTRY IS FILED FOR ITS FORWARD-LOOKING CLAUSE.** The hazard is **PREVENTED TODAY** by a gate that is shipped, documented and deliberate. The reason to file it is that the gate is removable, that a design has already been drafted which removes it, and that nothing in the tree would go red if it did.

- Severity: **NOT ASSIGNED BY THIS SEAT — OWED** (brief sec 3, the operator's to rule). Field present so the triage needle finds one; see `ENG-0252`'s note on why omitting it is a measured failure mode.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `503dcdadeca2a15aaf3f177913cf26c564461c3e`, qsl-desktop main `11f695dfcb3e6c1f3b3ff78a14eee71e878b0439`, both re-derived at the NAMED `github` remote.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/transport/mod.rs` — the two-arm URL at **`:3540-3543`**, the wrapper `relay_inbox_pull` at `:3076-3082`. `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/lib.rs` — `resolve_ack_mode` at **`:940-945`** and `stored_ack_mode` at **`:947-955`**. `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/invite/mod.rs` — the gate at **`:1423-1442`**, its comment at `:1416-1422`, the clamp at `:1217`, the constants at `:1155-1156`. Desktop `ui/main.js:2891-2892`.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM.** The pull URL differs between modes in exactly one parameter, verbatim at `transport/mod.rs:3540-3543`:

```
let url = match ack_mode {
    AckMode::Legacy => format!("{}/v1/pull?max={}", base, max),
    AckMode::Lease  => format!("{}/v1/pull?max={}&ack=lease", base, max),
};
```

Under Legacy the relay **deletes on pull**. A fetched-and-unconsumed frame is not leased; it is **gone**. There is no lease to expire and no ack to withhold, so no ack discipline downstream can reach it.

⚠⚠ **LEGACY IS LIVE AND CONFIG-SELECTABLE, AND THIS CORRECTS A CHARACTERISATION ALREADY IN THIS LEDGER.** `resolve_ack_mode(None)` returns `stored_ack_mode().unwrap_or(AckMode::Lease)`, and `stored_ack_mode` reads the string `"legacy"` out of the **config file** (`lib.rs:947-955`, `read_ack_mode(&dir.join(CONFIG_FILE_NAME))`). ⇒ **Legacy is not only an explicit per-invocation flag: it is a persisted operator preference.** Once written, every subsequent command runs Legacy with no flag present. ⚠ `ENG-0142`'s remainder describes Legacy as *"a non-default, explicit-flag lab mode"* — **measured, that is incomplete**, and a correction is appended beside it there rather than rewritten.

⚠⚠ **THE SHIPPED GATE THAT PREVENTS THIS TODAY, AND IT IS EXPLICIT ABOUT WHY.** `invite_finish` branches its **pull shape** on ack mode (`invite/mod.rs:1423-1442`): the Legacy arm takes a head-only `relay_inbox_pull(..., max)` and `.next()`; only the Lease arm calls `finish_scan_select_invite_resp`. The comment above it, verbatim at `:1416-1422`:

> *"⚠⚠ **LEASE-ONLY, END TO END.** Under `AckMode::Legacy` the relay DELETES ON PULL, so a scan there would enlarge this pull from ONE frame to as many as 128 on a delete-on-pull server — converting a one-frame loss into a 16x–128x amplification. The gate is mechanical, not decorative"*

⚠⚠ **THE ARITHMETIC, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** The desktop calls `invite_finish` with **`max: 1`** (`ui/main.js:2892`). The scan path clamps: `let total = max.clamp(FINISH_SCAN_TOTAL_MIN, FINISH_SCAN_TOTAL_MAX)` (`invite/mod.rs:1217`) with `MIN = 16` and `MAX = 128` (`:1155-1156`) ⇒ `1.clamp(16, 128)` = **16**. So a beat that scans costs **16** where the gated beat costs **1**, at the same `max: 1` — the 16x the comment names — and up to **128** if a new verb is given a larger `max`.

⚠⚠ **A CORRECTION TO THE READS' STATED MECHANISM, MEASURED BY THIS SEAT AND CONSEQUENTIAL.** Both cold reads attribute today's destruction-of-one to *"the head-only `.next()`"*. **`.next()` does not bound destruction — `max` does.** The URL at `:3541` carries `max={max}` under **both** arms, and under Legacy every frame the relay returns is already deleted by the time `.next()` runs. The two coincide only because the desktop passes `max: 1`. ⇒ **a future caller that raises `max` while keeping `.next()` would destroy `max` frames with the gate apparently still in place.** The reads' arithmetic for the shipped call is right; the protective mechanism they name is not the one doing the work.

⚠⚠⚠ **THE FORWARD-LOOKING CLAUSE — THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS FILED.** **Any future design that scans this mailbox MUST carry an `AckMode` arm.** Measured: within the invite/handshake flow, `invite_finish:1423` is the **only** site that branches the *pull shape* on ack mode. (`handshake/mod.rs:1718-1719` branches only the **ack** — `acks_own_frames` — and `invite/mod.rs:1384` gates only a `debug_assert`; neither reduces what the pull fetches.) ⇒ **retiring `invite_finish` removes the only pull-shape branch in the flow**, and nothing else would refuse a scan under Legacy.

⚠⚠ **AND A DESIGN THAT DID NOT CARRY ONE HAS ALREADY BEEN DRAFTED.** NA-0768's amended inviter-completion design (`DESIGN_NA0768_amended_20260827.md`, sha256 `b5c49263828d49c11074e37b25b59cb6b1788ed2c729f7d1e1d9c788de3ca117`) replaces the per-contact finish scan with a class-dispatching beat and unregisters `invite_finish`; **no clause of it mentions `AckMode` at any point**, and no instrument in its sealed set inspects one. That design is **not ruled by this entry and is not this lane's subject** — it is named so the next reader inherits the constraint rather than rediscovering it. ⇒ **the next design that touches this mailbox must state its Legacy behaviour explicitly, or state why it cannot be reached.**

- ⚠⚠ **OWED OPERATOR MEASUREMENTS — LOAD-BEARING AND NOT TAKEN:** (i) the **deployed** `ack_mode`; (ii) the relay's deployed `retention_ttl_secs`. If (i) is Lease everywhere, this entry is latent and the gate is insurance; if Legacy is deployed anywhere, it is live. **Neither has been measured by any lane, and the severity of this entry cannot be settled without (i).**
- ⚠ **WHAT THIS SEAT COULD NOT OBSERVE.** No relay was contacted and no rig was run (n=0 network calls for traffic). *Delete-on-pull* is read from the **client's own URL construction** and from the tree's own comment and its `AckFlushOutcome::LegacyComplete` arm — **not** from an observed relay deletion. A relay contract under which `?max=N` without `ack=lease` does not delete on pull would falsify the consequence while leaving the branch asymmetry intact.
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED.** Not repaired here; the gate is not touched.

### ⏹ CLOSED BY RETIREMENT 2026-08-28 (NA-0770 / `D-1411`) — ENG-0254 — A SHIPPED PATH ALREADY SCANS UNDER `AckMode::Legacy`: `handshake poll` PULLS UP TO `--max` FRAMES FROM THE SELF INBOX AND, UNDER LEGACY, THE RELAY DELETES EVERY ONE OF THEM — INCLUDING FRAMES ADDRESSED TO A DIFFERENT PEER, WHICH IT NEVER PROCESSES — **NEW; FILED by NA-0769 (`D-1410`) as the third defect, on the brief's own sec 2(c) instruction to measure whether any other shipped path scans under Legacy. FILING ONLY.**

⏹⏹ **CLOSED BY RETIREMENT, NOT BY REPAIR — 2026-08-28, NA-0770 (`D-1411`). NOTHING BELOW IS EDITED.**
> **Severity at close: `P2`, CONDITIONAL** — on the same measurement, and for the same reason, as `ENG-0253`. The operator's 2026-08-28 figures (neither field machine carries an ack-mode config) make this one latent for its whole life too, notwithstanding that it is the entry filed as *present-tense*: "present-tense" meant **ungated in the code**, not **firing in the field**, and this closure does not let those two be conflated.
>
> **What closes it:** the gate this entry complained about — `handshake/mod.rs`'s `acks_own_frames`, which gated only the ACK on the mode while leaving the PULL ungated — is now `let acks_own_frames = matches!(source, HsPollSource::Relay);`. The mode half of the condition is gone because the mode is gone; the `Relay` half is preserved exactly. With one mode shipped, a poll that pulls and does not ack leaves every unconsumed frame **leased and redelivered** rather than deleted, which is precisely the property this entry said was missing.
>
> ⚠ **WHAT DID NOT GET FIXED, SAID PLAINLY.** This entry also observed that `handshake poll` pulls up to `--max` frames and processes only what it can parse. **That is still true.** The frames it cannot parse are now redelivered instead of destroyed, which is the whole of the improvement. The wedge in which an unparseable frame at the head blocks progress forever is `ENG-0142`/`ENG-0198`, is UNREPAIRED, and NA-0770 made it **more visible, not less** — see loss `L3` in `D-1411`: with delete-on-pull gone, the tree no longer has any verb that can evict such a frame from a relay mailbox.

⚠⚠ **THIS IS THE PRESENT-TENSE SIBLING OF `ENG-0253`.** `ENG-0253` records a hazard a shipped gate prevents. **This one has no gate.** `invite_finish` branches its *pull shape* on ack mode; `handshake poll` branches only its **ack**.

- Severity: **NOT ASSIGNED BY THIS SEAT — OWED** (brief sec 3, the operator's to rule). Field present for the triage needle.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `503dcdadeca2a15aaf3f177913cf26c564461c3e`, qsl-desktop main `11f695dfcb3e6c1f3b3ff78a14eee71e878b0439`, both re-derived at the NAMED `github` remote.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` — the ack-only gate at **`:1718-1719`**, the ungated pull at **`:1722`**, the item loops at `:1759` / `:2047` / `:2267`, the public `HsPollSource::Relay` entry at `:2507`. `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/cmd/mod.rs` — the `Poll` subcommand and its `--max` default at **`:374-392`**. `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/transport/mod.rs:3076-3082` and `:3540-3543`.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE BYTES.** The poll's own code knows Legacy deletes at pull, and gates only the **ack** on it — verbatim at `:1716-1722`:

```
// Lease-only for the same reason the rest of this lane is: under Legacy the relay already
// deleted the frame at pull time, so there is nothing to ack and nothing left leased.
let acks_own_frames = matches!(source, HsPollSource::Relay)
    && crate::resolve_ack_mode(None) == crate::cmd::AckMode::Lease;
let items = match source {
    HsPollSource::Provided(v) => v.to_vec(),
    HsPollSource::Relay => match transport::relay_inbox_pull(relay, inbox_route_token, max) { ...
```

⇒ **the comment states the delete-on-pull fact and the code draws no conclusion from it for the PULL.** `relay_inbox_pull` resolves its own mode internally (`transport/mod.rs:3081`, `crate::resolve_ack_mode(None)`) and the URL carries `max={max}` under **both** arms (`:3540-3543`). There is **no head-only Legacy arm** anywhere on this path, and no clamp: `--max` reaches the relay as written.

⚠⚠ **THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS NOT A WEDGE — IT IS SILENT DESTRUCTION.** The poll is addressed to **one** peer (`--peer`), and it loads exactly that peer's pending record. It then iterates every frame the pull returned. A frame belonging to a **different** peer takes the `session_id_mismatch` arm and `continue`s (`:1762-1767`, `:2050-2055`) — correct behaviour under Lease, where the frame stays leased and redeliverable. **Under Legacy that frame was already destroyed by the pull**, unread and unprocessable, and the poll reports rc 0. ⇒ **polling for peer A destroys peer B's in-flight handshake frames.**

⚠⚠ **THE ARITHMETIC.** `--max` defaults to **4** (`cmd/mod.rs:387`, `#[arg(long, default_value_t = 4)]`) and is **not clamped** on this path. ⇒ under Legacy a single `qsc handshake poll` destroys up to **4** self-inbox frames, of which at most those addressed to the named peer are usable. A larger `--max` destroys proportionally more; the ceiling is whatever the operator types.

⚠ **HONESTY BOUND ON REACHABILITY, STATED PLAINLY.** This path is driven by the **`qsc` CLI**, not by the desktop: measured, the desktop drives **no** handshake poll at all (zero matches for `handshake_poll` in desktop source; the only hit is a comment at `ui/main.js:2857`), which is the same fact `ENG-0250` records from the other direction. `qsc` is nevertheless a shipped client against the same vault and the same mailboxes, and the public entry at `:2507` carries the comment *"The shipped path: pull from the relay"*. ⇒ **shipped and reachable by the CLI; not reachable from the GUI today.**

- ⚠ **WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ENTRY AND NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `ENG-0142`.** `ENG-0142`'s remainder covers Legacy's **wedge** in `receive` (`transport/mod.rs:1147-1211`), where one bad frame ABORTS a batch and the trailing frames are destroyed. This is a different call site with a different shape: no abort, no bad frame required, and the destruction is of frames the caller was never entitled to consume. The duplicate check was run before filing (the `WF-0029` precedent) and is recorded in `D-1410`: the nearest existing entries are `ENG-0142` and `ENG-0196`, and neither describes this site or this shape.
- ⚠⚠ **OWED OPERATOR MEASUREMENT — the same (i) as `ENG-0252` / `ENG-0253`:** the **deployed** `ack_mode`. If Lease is deployed everywhere this is latent; if Legacy is deployed anywhere it is live today.
- ⚠ **WHAT THIS SEAT COULD NOT OBSERVE.** Same bound as `ENG-0253`: no relay was contacted. Delete-on-pull is read from the client's URL construction and the tree's own comments, not observed.
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED.** Filing only.

### ENG-0255 — TWO STORE-LOAD FAILURES ARE FLATTENED TO A SINGLE OPAQUE STRING BY `.map_err(|_| ...)`, SO A PERMISSIONS FAULT, A CORRUPT FILE AND A MISSING FILE ALL REPORT THE SAME CAUSE — **NEW; filed 2026-08-28 by NA-0770 (`D-1411`), NOT REPAIRED**

- Severity: **P3** — assigned by the operator 2026-08-28, relayed through this lane's ruling. P3 and not higher because neither site is on a destructive path and neither can lose data; what is lost is the OPERATOR'S ABILITY TO DIAGNOSE, which costs time rather than bytes.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-28 by NA-0770 (`D-1411`). ⚠⚠ **DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED BY THE FILING LANE.** NA-0770's authorised edit set was ten product files; both sites below are outside it, and the lane's trigger was armed against exactly this kind of momentum repair. Filing is the whole of the action taken.
- Exact surfaces, read from the bytes at qsl-protocol `2557ede2`:
  - `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/attachments/mod.rs:1731` — `let mut store = timeline_store_load().map_err(|_| "timeline_unavailable")?;`
  - `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/contacts/mod.rs:312` — `let mut rec = contacts_entry_read(peer_alias).map_err(|_| "contacts_store_invalid")?;`
- Estimated repair cost: **~2 seat-hours**, and stated so the entry can be scheduled rather than admired. The work is mechanical (widen the two error types, or map distinct causes to distinct strings) but it touches shared store-loading paths, so it needs the full suite rather than a targeted run — which is where the two hours go, not the edit.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM IS THE DISCARD, NOT THE STRING.** `|_|` throws the underlying error away before anything can read it. Every distinguishable cause the loader can return — the file is absent, the file is present and unparseable, the process lacks permission, the disk failed mid-read — arrives at the operator as one flat token. The token is not even wrong; it is unfalsifiable, which is worse, because an operator who reads `timeline_unavailable` has no way to learn whether to check a path, a mode bit, or a backup.

⚠ **WHY THIS IS FILED BY A LANE ABOUT ACK MODES AT ALL.** NA-0770 spent this lane's attention on the difference between a defect and its *diagnosis*, and both sites were met while measuring whether a retired-key read could report a third state distinguishably. The program's own words, which this entry adopts as its standard: **distinct errors for distinct causes; false diagnosis is the enemy.** A single opaque string is a false diagnosis whenever more than one cause can produce it — which here is always.

⚠ **NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS PROGRAM'S RECENT WORK.** Both lines predate NA-0770 and neither was touched by it. This entry records where they are, not who wrote them.

### WF-0090 — ⚠⚠ THE QUEUE'S STATUS VOCABULARY AND THE TOOL THAT READS IT HAVE DIVERGED: `qsl_evidence_helper.py queue` REQUIRES EXACTLY ONE BARE `READY` TOKEN, THE RECORDS WRITE `PROMOTED for **D-####**` AND `**DONE**`, AND `qwork` HAS THEREFORE BEEN FAILING CLOSED SINCE 2026-08-18 — **NEW; FILED 2026-08-29 by NA-0771 (`D-1412`) on the Director's ruling, after the operator hit it live. FILING ONLY — the tool is NOT changed and the vocabulary is NOT swept.**

- Severity: **NOT ASSIGNED BY THIS SEAT — OWED.** The Director proposes and the operator rules. Field present rather than omitted on purpose: `ENG-0142` records that an entry with no `- Severity:` bullet was *"uncountable by the triage instrument for six days"*.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-29. ⚠ **NOT A LATENT FINDING: it fired in production.** `qwork NA-0771 qsl-protocol` returned `startup_result=FAIL / reason=queue-helper-failed / qshell_qwork_status=2`.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `375668397f77efe7f94ca0c1533735bfefefdfac`, re-derived bare and unpiped at the NAMED `github` remote.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, READ FROM THE TOOL'S OWN BYTES.** `scripts/ci/qsl_evidence_helper.py` extracts a lane's status with

```
status_match = re.search(r"(?m)^\s*-?\s*Status:\s*([A-Z_]+)\b", body)
```

and its `queue` subcommand then does `ready = [... if item.status == "READY"]` followed by `if len(ready) != 1 and not args.allow_nonready_count: return 2`. Two properties follow and both are load-bearing: the token must be **BARE** (`[A-Z_]+` cannot pass a `*`, so `Status: **DONE**` yields **no match at all**), and the count must be **EXACTLY ONE** — zero fails as surely as two. `tools/qwork.sh:248` calls it **without** `--allow-nonready-count`, so the seat has no way to proceed past it.

⚠⚠ **THE CENSUS, MEASURED AT THE BASE — AND IT CORRECTS A FIGURE THIS SEAT ITSELF SUPPLIED.** Of **755** `### NA-` blocks: **744 DONE** (read correctly), **3 PROMOTED**, **3 BLOCKED**, **1 BACKLOG**, **4 status-empty to the tool**, and **0 READY**. The four status-empty divide into two causes: `NA-0706` and `NA-0707` carry **no `Status:` line at all**, while `NA-0770` and `NA-0769` carry `Status: **DONE**` — **bolded, and therefore unreadable by the regex**.

⚠⚠ **THE `~60` FIGURE IN THE ORDERING RULING IS WRONG, AND THE ERROR ORIGINATED IN THIS SEAT'S OWN INSTRUMENT.** The seat's first census sliced a **fixed 1500-character window** from each `### NA-` heading rather than delimiting each block at the NEXT heading, so every block longer than that window appeared to have no `Status:` line. That produced *"~60 recent blocks are status-empty"*, which the seat reported and the ruling then carried in good faith. **MEASURED WITH BLOCK BOUNDARIES: 4.** ⇒ the drift is real but **an order of magnitude smaller** than filed. `SR-09` governs: a measured census supersedes any prose count, **including our own**, and the superseding record says so explicitly. ⚠ The corrected instrument was **validated against a known answer before being believed** — it reproduces the helper's own `READY_COUNT 0` and the anchored grep's `PROMOTED 3` at the same base (`NA-0758`'s rule).

⚠⚠ **TWO CONSUMERS OF ONE NEEDLE THAT DISAGREE ABOUT ZERO — THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT.** `scripts/ci/preflight_governance.sh:39-47` reads `^Status: READY\b` and fails **only when the count is `> 1`**; the `qwork` helper fails on **anything `!= 1`**. ⇒ **a count of 0 is simultaneously VALID to the governance preflight and FATAL to `qwork`**, and merged main has sat at 0 continuously. A repo state that satisfies one gate and blocks the other is not a bug in either gate; it is an unstated contract between them.

⚠⚠ **THE CONDITION WAS ALREADY IN REPO TRUTH AND WAS READ AS A NOTE RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** `NA-0746`'s own queue block records, verbatim, that *"the anchored needle `^Status: READY` counts **0** on merged main"* — and that lane's declared class is `QUEUE_NEEDLE_ANCHORED_FIVE_STATE_PASS`. The sentence was true, was written down, and **named a state nothing could act on**, because at that moment nobody was running `qwork`. ⇒ **a recorded observation with no consumer decays into background text.** That is `D-2`/`R305`'s rule about rules, applying to a *measurement*.

⚠ **THE LATENCY, AND WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE.** `qwork` last succeeded **2026-08-18** (newest proof: `/srv/qbuild/tmp/qwork.NA-0744.qsl-protocol.905390.proof`). Every lane since has been opened by pasting a kickoff into a seat, so nothing exercised the queue gate for **eleven days** while the records vocabulary moved from `READY` to `PROMOTED for **D-####**`. **The tool did not break; it stopped being run, and the records drifted underneath it.**

- **CURE CANDIDATES — NAMED, NOT BUILT, AND NEITHER IS CHOSEN HERE.**
  **(a) THE RECORDS MOVE TO THE FORM THE TOOL READS** — `Status: READY (D-####)` at promotion, `Status: MERGING (PR #N)` at the PR, `Status: DONE (class)` at close: bare, unbolded, one token the regex can pass. Cost: a sweep of every block whose form is wrong, and a rule that keeps it. Benefit: the tool needs no change and the preflight keeps working.
  **(b) THE TOOL MOVES TO THE FORM THE RECORDS WRITE** — the helper accepts `PROMOTED` as a distinct state and strips bold before matching. Cost: a change to a gate, which needs its own red arm; and it does not settle the 0-vs-1 disagreement with the preflight, which would still need ruling.
  **(c) DO NOTHING** — named so the option set is not narrower than its claim (`D-1371`). It is the status quo, and its cost is exactly what the operator just paid: `qwork` fails closed with a reason that names the helper rather than the vocabulary.
- ⚠ **WHAT THIS PR DOES AND DOES NOT DO.** It applies **(a)** to the **three blocks it already touches for other reasons** — `NA-0771` to `READY (D-1412)`, `NA-0766` and `NA-0767` to `DONE (<class>)` — **and nothing else.** The other 752 blocks are untouched, the helper is untouched, `preflight_governance.sh` is untouched, and the 0-vs-1 disagreement is **filed, not settled**. `NA-0706`/`NA-0707`'s missing `Status:` lines and `NA-0769`/`NA-0770`'s bolded ones are named here and left alone.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0201` (the same needle counting **mentions** at both sites, wrong in both directions for three weeks — the previous defect in this exact instrument), `ENG-0230` (the `STATE:` header must be gated on NAMING the newest block, not counting `READY` lines — open, and the sibling of this entry), `WF-0087` (recording a sweep plants the swept ids), `D-1412` (the lane that filed this), `D-1407` / `D-1408` (the two classes declared in the same act, which is why those two blocks were in reach).

### ENG-0257 — ⚠ P3 (DESIGN FINDING) — RELAY-SIDE CONTACT-GRAPH LINKABILITY: ONE self-inbox route token per account is handed to EVERY contact, so a relay that sees pushes can link an account's contacts BY ADDRESS — **NEW; FILED by NA-0768 (`D-1409`) as the records disposition ordered at `ORDER_contact_graph_linkability_20260829.md` R4. FILING ONLY — nothing is built, and R1 of that order forbids building on it until a threat-model ruling lands.**

- Severity: **P3 — a metadata/linkability property, not a confidentiality or integrity defect.** No message content, key or ratchet state is exposed. ⚠ **Severity is deliberately not raised on a guess:** what it costs depends on WHICH relay the account uses, and that is exactly what R3's threat-model lane is commissioned to settle.
- Exact surfaces (Director-measured from the bytes at qsl-protocol `4a4dfdc9`, carried here with the sites named): `vault/mod.rs:568`/`:573` and `generate_default_route_token` `:726`/`:737` (the token is generated ONCE at vault creation); `contacts/mod.rs::relay_self_inbox_route_token` `:60-69` (read back from the single vault secret `TUI_RELAY_INBOX_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY`); and the three sites that hand that one token to every contact — `invite/mod.rs:1120 -> :1129` (invite create), `:1354 -> :1372` (invite accept), `:1416` (invite finish).
- ⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM.** There is **ONE** self-inbox route token per account, and it is published to every peer the account ever invites or accepts. The other direction is already per-contact (the peer's token is stored per contact); the per-contact LOCAL mint was REMOVED at NA-0681 (`D616` sec 2m) because it minted a token the peer had never seen. ⇒ **two contacts of one account push to the SAME mailbox address**, and a relay that observes pushes can link them by that address.
- ⚠⚠ **THE DIRECTOR'S OWN CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN IN THE FILING, AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** The statement that prompted the operator's *"I agree, lets add that feature"* was: *"Per-contact route tokens would close it."* **That is an OVERCLAIM and is withdrawn at sec 2 of the order.** Measured: per-contact tokens close the **SEND** side (no linking by destination address) and do **NOT** close the **PULL** side — the account pulls its N mailboxes from one client session, and the relay serving those pulls links them by session, IP and timing regardless of address. Under the delivery ladder's rungs 2–3 (one held connection per client) that pull-side linkage is **STRUCTURAL**. ⇒ against the account's OWN relay (the self-hosted story) per-contact tokens buy little; against a SHARED or a SENDER'S relay they buy the send side. SimpleX's unlinkability comes from per-contact queues **PLUS** multiple servers **PLUS** private routing, not from per-contact addresses alone. ⇒ recorded as an `SR-16` row against the Director's chair: **the PREMISE was measured (one token) and the CONSEQUENCE was not (that the named fix closes the gap)** — the family is *"a remedy named from its mechanism, not from a threat table"*.
- **What is ordered, carried verbatim in substance from R1–R3:**
  - **R1 — NOTHING IS BUILT ON THE WITHDRAWN CLAIM.** No lane mints per-contact tokens until a threat-model ruling says what they buy, against which relay, and whether the pull side needs its own answer (separate sessions, Tor, relay-side batching that hides membership, multiple relays) for the benefit to exist at all.
  - **R2 — `N` INBOXES PER ACCOUNT IS A DESIGN INPUT TO THE INVITER REPAIR'S MENU (`NA-0768`, `D-1409`).** Whatever fetch/dispatch architecture is chosen **must not ASSUME one mailbox per account**; the menu prices, for each entry, what changes at `N > 1`. Amendment `A1` (*"one pull per beat per mailbox"*) is read as **per mailbox**, which already admits `N` — so the menu must say whether an entry means **`N` fetchers or one fetcher over `N` addresses**, and what each costs at rung 2/3, ⚠ **where a beat that scales with contact count LEAKS THE CONTACT COUNT.**
  - **R3 — A THREAT-MODEL LANE RULES THE QUESTION BEFORE THE MESSAGING EPIC.** Seat-authored and measured: a table of what each relay learns — own relay, shared relay, sender's relay, network observer — at each ladder rung, for one-token and per-contact-token designs, for the pull side with and without session unlinkability. **The DOCUMENT is the deliverable** (the funding plan's readiness list names a threat model as a gap; this is it). Per-contact tokens become a RULED mechanism with a measured benefit, or are DECLINED with the measurement.
- ⚠⚠ **THE THREAT-MODEL LANE'S INPUTS, FILED HERE BY NAME SO THEY ARE INHERITED RATHER THAN REDISCOVERED.** Both are findings of NA-0771's `STOP_NA0771_005` sec 14, neither repaired by that lane and neither in this one's scope:
  - **`F-B` — A1 CARRIES NO AUTHENTICATOR.** `HsInit` has no `mac` and no `sig`, so **any sender can cause a responder pending record to be created**. NA-0771's own words: *"The successor lane, and bigger than this one."*
  - **`F-C` — `--suite-mode` IS A CLI-ONLY PROTOCOL MODE, WHICH `P-FACADE` (`D-1413`) FORBIDS.** It is also load-bearing rather than cosmetic: it is what makes two of NA-0771's reachability rows reachable at all.
- **Sequence:** the threat-model lane is inserted into `ORDER_ladder_climb`'s R3 between the inviter repair (step 3) and the messaging epic (step 6). ⚠ **It runs IN PARALLEL with the inviter repair**, per the operator's ruling of 2026-08-29 (*"lets get to work"*) refining `CLOSEOUT_NA0771_20260829.md` sec 9 — it does not gate this lane, and this lane does not gate it.

### ENG-0259 — ⚠ P2 — DELETED MESSAGES PERSIST ON DISK: the relay's SQL view reports a fully-delivered conversation gone while the message body, its id and both mailbox pseudonyms remain recoverable from `relay.db-wal` and freelist pages — **NEW; FILED by NA-0772 (`D-1415`) on the SR-15 cold read of STOP 002, re-measured from a RUN at the deployed relay's bracket. FILING ONLY — no repair is performed and none is authorised by this lane.**

- Severity: **P2** — privacy at rest. The organization's disk encryption is the outer control, and nothing here is a confidentiality defect in the cryptographic sense: bodies remain E2EE ciphertext. What is exposed is that a conversation *existed*, its size, its timing and its mailbox pseudonyms, after the product's own store reports them deleted.
- Bases measured at: qsl-server **`37ec82072cbbd68e4eaba83e192282fbcb96e5b4`** (the deployed relay's bracket, built locally), qsl-protocol `25e6f14961d6da6188924c891cd1f459b8c507da`.
- Exact surfaces: `src/store.rs:208-212` — the complete pragma set is `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `foreign_keys=ON`. Needle count across all of `src/` for `secure_delete`, `wal_checkpoint`, `VACUUM`, `auto_vacuum`, `journal_size_limit`: **ZERO**.
- ⚠⚠ **MEASURED BY A RUN, IN TWO ARMS THAT DIFFER.** A mailbox pushed to, pulled and acked — fully drained:
  - **ARM A, the SQL view:** `routes` **0 rows**, `messages` **0 rows**.
  - **ARM B, the raw files:** the message body **×3**, its `msg_id` **×3**, the `route_key` pseudonym **×9**, the `log_id` pseudonym **×2**. `sqlite_sequence` additionally retains a **lifetime message count**.
  - ⛳ The raw route **token** appears **0 times** — the at-rest token-protection property is real and is not affected by this entry.
- ⚠⚠ **WHY IT IS FILED AS A DEFECT AND NOT AS A NOTE.** The product's buyer-facing answer to "what does a subpoena yield" is an at-rest claim, and **an at-rest claim measured through the store's own query interface cannot see this**. A subpoena or a seizure takes the **directory** — `relay.db`, `relay.db-wal`, `relay.db-shm` — not a SQL connection. The recovery above needs no forensic tooling: ordinary SQLite reads it.
- Recommended change: **NONE CHOSEN.** Candidates NAMED only: `PRAGMA secure_delete=ON` (a write-amplification cost); a periodic `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`; and the honest limit that **filesystem-level residue remains regardless** — page reuse is not erasure. A qsl-server lane; the relay-redeploy decision (`ORDER_ladder_climb` R3.7) rides with it.
- ⚠ **NOT MEASURED:** how long a page survives before reuse. That depends on traffic volume; **n=0 field measurements**. The finding does not depend on it — the claim under test was that the data is GONE, and it is not.

### ENG-0260 — THE CLEARTEXT HANDSHAKE CORRELATOR: the 16-byte `session_id` sits at a fixed offset in all three handshake frame types and the SAME value lands in BOTH peers' mailboxes, so the relay pairs handshake counterparts by byte equality with no cryptography — **NEW; FILED by NA-0772 (`D-1415`) as a DESIGN finding. FILING ONLY — the cure is a protocol change and belongs to the messaging epic's design pass, not to this lane.**

- Severity: **P3 (DESIGN FINDING)** — a metadata/linkability property, not a confidentiality or integrity defect. No content, key or ratchet state is exposed.
- Exact surfaces: `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/src/handshake/mod.rs` — `HS_MAGIC = b"QHSM"` at **`:22`**, the magic check at **`:459`**, and the 16-byte `session_id` copies at **`:541`** (A1/`HsInit`), **`:626`** (B1/`HsResp`) and **`:685`** (A2/`HsConfirm`).
- ⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM.** A1 and A2 are delivered to the **responder's** mailbox; B1 is delivered to the **initiator's**. All three carry the same 16-byte `session_id` in the clear at a fixed offset. ⇒ **the relay holds frames in two different mailboxes bearing an identical correlator**, and can pair those mailboxes — hence those two accounts — by exact byte comparison, performing no cryptographic operation of any kind.
- ⚠⚠ **WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE RULING IT WAS FOUND IN.** `D-1415` declines per-contact route tokens for the primary deployment, and this is one of its four grounds: **per-contact addressing changes the ADDRESS and leaves the CORRELATOR.** Any future design that offers per-contact or rotating mailboxes as an unlinkability measure must answer this entry or it will not deliver what it claims.
- Recommended change: **NONE PROPOSED.** The cure is a protocol change — a per-mailbox or encrypted correlator — with its own ceremony. Named so the obligation is inherited rather than rediscovered.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-30 by NA-0772 (`D-1415`).
- Cross-references: `ENG-0257` (the contact-graph linkability filing this lane was commissioned to rule on); `ENG-0252` (which measured the same `session_id` travelling in the clear, for a different purpose).
- Source: NA-0772 STOP 003; every one of the five line cites was verified line-exact by an independent SR-15 cold read.

### ENG-0261 — ⚠ P3 — THE RELAY'S EMPTY DEFAULT LOG IS AN ACCIDENT OF `EnvFilter`'s DEFAULT LEVEL, NOT A STATED CONTRACT, AND REQUEST LOGGING IS ONE LINE AWAY — **NEW; FILED by NA-0772 (`D-1415`). FILING ONLY.**

- Severity: **P3** — a hardening and durability-of-guarantee item, not a live defect. The shipped behaviour is currently *good*; nothing protects it.
- Bases measured at: qsl-server **`37ec8207`**, built and run locally.
- ⛳ **THE PROPERTY WORTH PROTECTING, MEASURED.** At the shipped default the relay installs **no request-logging middleware of any kind** — no `TraceLayer`, no `.layer()` call anywhere in `src/`, and no `ConnectInfo`, `peer_addr`, `remote_addr` or `X-Forwarded-For` — and emits nothing per push, pull or ack. A scripted exchange with `RUST_LOG` unset produced a log of **0 bytes**.
- ⚠ **BUT IT FOLLOWS FROM A DEFAULT, NOT FROM A DECISION.** `main.rs:231-233` installs `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())`. With the variable unset that admits **ERROR**, not OFF. There are **nine** `tracing::error!` sites — `main.rs:239`, `:246`, `:258`, `:265`, `:272`, `:287`, `:304` and `lib.rs:480`, `:1019` — of which **one (`lib.rs:1019`, inside `run_store`) sits on a live request path**; a second (`lib.rs:480`) is the background retention sweeper, and the remaining seven are startup and configuration. Three arms with `RUST_LOG` unset produced timestamped ERROR lines of **95, 109 and 117 bytes**.
- ⚠⚠ **AND REQUEST LOGGING IS ONE LINE AWAY.** `Cargo.toml` at this base already declares `tower-http = { version = "0.5", features = ["trace"] }` — **the crate is linked and the `trace` feature is ON**, with zero uses in `src/`. The absence of request logging is a line that was never written, not a dependency that was never taken.
- Recommended change: **NONE CHOSEN.** Candidates named: **state the contract** ("no request logging by default") and **test it** with an assertion that the log is empty after a scripted exchange, so the guarantee cannot regress silently; consider what the two `store_error` sites should carry, since both interpolate the store's own error string (`store.rs:185` `format!("ERR_STORE {e}")`) and **neither was observed firing — n=0**; and, if any deployment ever raises the level, key or drop `channel_log_id`, whose unkeyed FNV-1a a token-holder inverts at will.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-30 by NA-0772 (`D-1415`).
- Source: NA-0772 STOP 003 sec 4.2 and its carried run `RUN_B2_logarms_at_37ec8207.txt`, with the instrument carried beside it.


### ENG-0262 — ⚠ P3 — `invite_scan_summary`'s `scanned=` UNDERSTATES THE LEASE FOOTPRINT ACROSS BATCHES AND AT BUDGET EXHAUSTION — **NEW; FILED by NA-0768 (`D-1409`). FILING ONLY.**

### ENG-0264 — ⚠ P3 — AN INPUT TO THE E3 / MESSAGING DISPATCH DESIGN: ADDRESSING RESTORES THE ALARM THAT THE FAN-OUT CANNOT SOUND — **NEW; FILED by NA-0768 (`D-1409`). FILING ONLY.**

- ⚠⚠ **THE ALARM IS RESTORED BY ADDRESSING, AND THAT IS THIS FILING.** When frames are matched to a mailbox or a session BEFORE they are offered — which is the dispatch table's job — a mismatch is once again a statement about a NAMED peer, and the security marker becomes sound again. **Whoever designs E3 / messaging dispatch should take this as an input rather than rediscover it.**
- ⚠ The mitigation this lane DID build is `invite_finish_hs_unconsumed{candidates=N}` (`invite/mod.rs`), which makes the CONDITION visible — a frame nobody took, redelivered every lease until the 7-day TTL — without claiming to know why. It carries no fingerprint, no identity, no alias and **no session id**: the ruling permitted at most a hash8 of the session id, and this lane declined it, because obtaining one means reading the frame's session id outside the crypto module, which `RULING_005` sec 2 refuses. **A permission is not an instruction.**

### WF-0091 — ⚠⚠ A SUITE RUNNER KEYED ITS RESULTS BY TARGET **NAME** WHILE TWO TARGETS SHARE ONE NAME, SO ONE SILENTLY OVERWROTE THE OTHER AND **THE RUN REPORTED GREEN WHILE INCOMPLETE** — **NEW; FILED by NA-0768 (`D-1409`) from `STOP_NA0771_006` sec 8.3, carrying property `PR-7`. FILING ONLY — the runner is seat tooling, not a repository artifact, and nothing is repaired here.**

- Severity: **⚠⚠ workflow defect, and it is the dangerous class: a FALSE GREEN on the gate a seat runs before opening a PR.** It did not reach CI and it did not reach a merged claim — but only because an arithmetic check caught it.
- ⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, MEASURED.** The build produced **148 test executables** but only **147 distinct target NAMES**: the `lib` target and the `bin:qsc` target are **BOTH named `qsc`**. The runner keyed its log and exit files by NAME, so both wrote to the same `qsc.log` / `qsc.exit` and one **OVERWROTE** the other. Both executed — the scheduler logged 148 launches, two of them named `qsc` — but **only one result survived to be counted.**
- ⛳⛳ **HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THE ENTRY: NOT BY ANY FAILURE.** The run was GREEN. It was found by **RECONCILING THE EXECUTED COUNT AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT CENSUS** — the shard manifest's **149** — and getting **148**. ⇒ **`PR-7`: A GREEN RUN IS NOT A COMPLETE RUN.** An instrument that loses a result silently reports success, and the only thing standing between that and a false *"the full suite passed"* was the arithmetic.
- **The cure applied in-lane (recorded, not landed as tooling):** both executables re-run separately under distinct tags — `qsc_lib` exit 0 with **141 passed**, `qsc_bin` exit 0 with 0 passed. ⚠ **The lib target's 141 unit tests are the bulk of what the overwrite had masked** — the loss was not marginal.
- **Remedy (proposed, not built):** key run artifacts by the **unique target PATH or kind+name**, never by name alone; and make the runner **PRINT ITS OWN CARDINALITY** beside its verdict, reconciled against the manifest, so a dropped result is an error rather than a silence. ⚠ The general form is already law in spirit at `SR-26` (a''): *"AN INSTRUMENT THAT REPORTS A VERDICT WITHOUT ITS COUNT CANNOT REPORT THAT IT LOOKED AT THE WRONG NUMBER OF THINGS."*
- ⓘ **WHY THIS IS FILED BY A LATER LANE RATHER THAN BY THE LANE THAT FOUND IT.** `STOP_NA0771_006` sec 8.3 records the finding and states its own reason for not landing it: adding the row would have edited `PREDICTION_LEDGER.md`, **changing the tree and INVALIDATING the very suite run that section reports.** The Director's close-out sec 8 assigns it to this promotion instead. ⇒ the finding travelled in the artifact, not in the commit, exactly as intended.
- **NAMED FOR THE CI-MIGRATION LANE, NOT ORDERED HERE** (`CLOSEOUT_NA0771` sec 8, and the separately-banked `FINDING_parallel_suite_durability_20260829T221244Z.md`):
  - **THE LOAD-GOVERNED RUNNER** with per-kind keys — the durable form of the cure above.
  - **THE SHARD-DURATION DATA, because shards balanced by COUNT are lopsided:** **49 targets (33%) carry 89% OF ALL RUNTIME**; median **28.4 s**, mean **97.7 s**, max **1836.4 s** (`aws_file_medium_boundary_na0192a`, **65x the median**). Per-target durations are carried in that finding as the rebalancing input.
  - **THE MEASURED ECONOMICS:** parallel wall clock (cap 6, load-governed) **48.0 min** against a true serial equivalent of **~3.2 h** — **~4.0x**, calibrated: 16 targets ran BOTH ways and aggregate inflation under parallel load is **x1.25**, so the summed per-target duration OVERSTATES serial cost and the honest figure is ~4x, not the ~5x the raw sum implies. Load over 202 samples at 10 s: min 2.99, mean 7.46, max 12.16.
  - ⚠⚠ **WHY CI HAS NEVER SEEN ANY OF THIS:** CI shards across **ELEVEN RUNNERS, one shard per machine** — and a separate machine **IS** the isolation that a shared test root and 38 process-global mutexes silently assume. **The defect class is invisible in CI by construction** and appears only when the suite runs concurrently on one box, which is the gate a seat actually runs before a PR.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-29 by NA-0768 (`D-1409`).
- Cross-references: `D-1412` (`PR-7`, appended beside it by this promotion); `SR-26` (a'') (an instrument reports its count, not only its verdict); `SR-05` (the suite policy, whose wording this promotion clarifies beside it); `SR-21` (an instrument's scope must equal its claim's scope).
- Source: `STOP_NA0771_006_20260829T221326Z.md` sec 8.3 and the lane's separately-banked `FINDING_parallel_suite_durability_20260829T221244Z.md` (whole-file sha256 `231afd747c4d578a014ffcb8a9e3019a738d5fbb9ced5831efad8d21eb8f3bf9`).
- ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY.** Every figure above is from **one Linux box** and is carried, not re-measured by this seat: `n=0` suite runs, `n=0` builds, no macOS instrument was available to anyone in the source lane, and **no claim is made about CI wall clock**. ⚠ The durability finding explicitly does NOT establish that the proposed per-target isolation CURES the contention — mechanism measured, **cure UNTESTED** — and this entry does not upgrade that.


### WF-0092 — ⚠⚠ ONE SELF-DIGEST CONSTRUCTION HOUSE-WIDE, AND THE STAMP PASS MUST NOT RESOLVE THE PLACEHOLDER INSIDE QUOTED TEXT — **NEW; FILED by NA-0772 (`D-1415`), RULED by the Director at `RULING_NA0772_002_20260830.md` sec 3 `F4`. The construction is RULED; the placeholder rule is filed with it because `F4` now owns it.**

- Title: one self-digest construction house-wide, and a stamp pass that cannot corrupt a quotation.
- Problem, in two halves:
  - **(1) THE CONSTRUCTIONS HAD DIVERGED.** Measured across seats: NA-0768, NA-0771 and NA-0770 all masked `64-hex → @@SELFDIGEST@@`; NA-0772 masked `64-hex → 64 'x'`. On one file the two produce **different digests**, so a reader running one lane's stated one-liner against another lane's stop reads MISMATCH on a sound file. A seal is only worth having if a reader can reproduce it **without asking the author which variant was used**.
  - **(2) THE HOUSE TOKEN COLLIDED WITH THE STAMP PLACEHOLDER.** `@@SELFDIGEST@@` was simultaneously the mask target and the literal a stamper substitutes. Measured consequences, both in this lane: a stamper corrupted a carried copy of `docs/ops/STANDING_RULES.md` by exactly **64 − 14 = 50 bytes**, at the very line where `SR-26 (a'')` describes that defect; and, one level up, a stop's own self-audit **quoted** a record line containing the token, had it replaced by that stop's digest, and then **scored the corrupted line `[OK]`** — the quoted sentence asserting that three other lanes use that stop's digest as their construction, which is false.
- Recommended change (the first half is RULED, the second is filed with it):
  - **RULED: the 64-'x' mask becomes the house construction**, because its token cannot collide with a stamp placeholder. The kickoff template states the exact one-liner so no seat invents a variant.
  - **THE PLACEHOLDER RULE: the stamp pass must not resolve the token inside quoted text.** The invariant "no unresolved identity field outside any carry" is **over-broad by exactly one case** — a legitimate quotation of carried text, printed in the file's own prose. The pass must skip quoted regions as well as carried ones, or the excerpt printer must escape the token before emitting it.
- ⚠ **WHY IT IS A WORKFLOW ITEM AND NOT AN ENGINEERING FINDING:** no repository artifact is defective. This is method machinery — the stamper and the kickoff template — and it will recur on the next assembly that prints a quotation containing the house placeholder, **whichever lane cuts it**. Before this filing, nobody owned it.
- Status: open — the construction RULED 2026-08-30; the template edit lands in the next records act that touches the template.
- Originating / last lane: NA-0772 (`D-1415`).
- Last-updated: 2026-08-30.
### ENG-0265 — ⚠⚠ THE RNG-FAILURE SEAM SIMULATES A FAULT THE PRODUCT CANNOT ACTUALLY HAVE: EVERY DRAW PANICS ON FAILURE, THE SEAM RETURNS `Err` INSTEAD OF DRAWING, AND TEN OF THE TESTS ASSERT THAT `"panicked"` IS ABSENT — SO A GREEN RUN DOES NOT ESTABLISH FAIL-SAFE BEHAVIOUR UNDER A REAL RANDOMNESS FAILURE — **NEW; FILED by NA-0773 (`D-1416`) on the SR-15 cold read's `F-1` (STOP-class). FILING ONLY — no repair is authorised by this lane and none was attempted.**

- Severity: **OF THE PRODUCT: UNGRADED, DELIBERATELY.** No defect was observed at any draw site; what is filed is the **absence of an instrument that could find one**. **OF THE ASSURANCE CLAIM IN OUR OWN RECORDS: `P2`** — a load-bearing statement on a security property is false as written. The distinction is the entry's point and must not be collapsed.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `c6687bbdd19927e3f3ed3e0f63f8c1672b804730`, re-derived bare and unpiped at the named `github` remote.

⚠⚠ **THE MECHANISM, FROM THREE MEASUREMENTS AND ONE CRATE SOURCE.** (1) `try_fill_bytes` — the only form of the call that can *return* an error — occurs **0 times** across `qsl/**` and `tools/refimpl/**`. (2) Every draw therefore goes through `rand_core 0.6.4`'s `OsRng::fill_bytes`, whose entire body is `if let Err(e) = self.try_fill_bytes(dest) { panic!("Error: {}", e); }`. ⇒ **a real randomness failure in this product is a PANIC, not an error return.** (3) The seam does something different in kind: at each wrapped site it reads an environment variable and returns `Err("rng_failure_forced")` **instead of** calling `fill_bytes`. It is faithful about **where** the failure happens and unfaithful about **what happens next** — an `Err` return runs the site's cleanup (`fail_core_buffers` zeroizes the passphrase and key buffers; the temp file is removed; `keychain_remove_key` is called), whereas a panic unwinds **past** all of it, and neither buffer is `Zeroizing`-wrapped.

⚠⚠ **THE SHARPEST TELL IS IN THE CORPUS ITSELF.** `assert_no_secret_output`, defined in **six of the nine** seam files and reached by **10 of the 19** asserting tests, asserts that `"panicked"`, `"stack backtrace"` and `"thread '"` do **NOT** appear in the output. **The suite asserts the absence of exactly the signature a real RNG failure produces.**

- ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY, STATED BECAUSE IT BOUNDS THE FILING: THE PANIC PATH IS REASONED, NOT OBSERVED.** The read did **not** induce a `getrandom` failure and watch the product. The three measurements above are measurements; the *consequences* of a panic — what residue it leaves, whether cleanup is skipped — are **inference**. This entry files the inference as an inference.
- **WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO KNOW — three options, so the set is not narrower than the problem, none chosen here:** **(i)** route every draw through **one fallible RNG helper** the seam can fail — a design change, a crypto region, its own lane, and it would **also close `ENG-0266`**; **(ii)** an **OS-level fault harness** (a `getrandom` shim or seccomp injection) that makes the real call fail, leaving the product unchanged — an audit instrument; **(iii)** accept the bound and **restate the finish line**, which is what the Director ruled (see `ENG-0197`).

- Severity: **THE COVERAGE GAP: `MAJOR`. THE PRODUCT: UNGRADED** — no defect was found at these sites; what was found is the absence of any test that could find one. **Not knowable by this mechanism** whether any of the 13 misbehaves on failure.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `c6687bbdd19927e3f3ed3e0f63f8c1672b804730`.

**THE NEEDLE, STATED SO IT CAN BE RE-RUN.** A randomness-consumption site = `OsRng.fill_bytes` · `rand_core::OsRng.fill_bytes` · `generate_nonce(&mut OsRng)` · `let mut rng = OsRng` · `<primitive>::generate(&mut OsRng)` · `.encapsulate(&mut OsRng)`. Instrument: **`git grep` throughout** — never a gitignore-honouring recursive search (`WF-0087`: `.gitignore`'s `**/evidence/` rule hides ~514 tracked files from other tools). **CONTROL, so the needle is not narrower than its claim:** `thread_rng` **0** · `rand::random` **0** · direct `getrandom` **0** · `from_entropy` **0** · `SmallRng` **0** · `StdRng` **0** ⇒ **`OsRng` is the only randomness source in the tree.**

⚠⚠ **EIGHT DRAWS IN `qsc` WITH NO SEAM WRAPPER, AND THE FIRST IS THE WORST.**
  1. **`vault/mod.rs:1476`, `derive_key`, the `KeySource::Keychain` arm — THE VAULT MASTER KEY ITSELF.** Ungated; **and no seam test uses `--key-source keychain`** (every vault seam test runs `--key-source passphrase` with `QSC_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1`). **The most security-critical draw in the client has zero coverage on two independent grounds.** ⚠ Compounding: `keychain_store_key` runs **before** the vault file write, so a failure between them leaves a key in the OS keychain with no vault referencing it — a residue class no test looks for.
  2. `msgqueue/mod.rs:332` `store_key` — the message-queue **store key**, persisted to the vault.
  3. `quarantine/mod.rs:234` `store_key` — the quarantine **store key**, persisted to the vault.
  4-6. `msgqueue/mod.rs:389`, `msgqueue/mod.rs:749`, `quarantine/mod.rs:287` — ChaCha20Poly1305 nonces.
  7. `invite/mod.rs:815` `csprng_16` — invite identifiers.
  8. `msgqueue/mod.rs:287` `mint_msg_id` — message ids, the correlation surface `DESIGN §4` governs.
**CONTROL:** the five files that DO carry the seam are `attachments`, `handshake`, `identity`, `protocol_state`, `vault`. **`invite`, `msgqueue` and `quarantine` carry the seam token 0 times each** — three whole modules outside the seam, two of which mint and persist long-lived symmetric keys.

⚠⚠ **AND THE REFERENCE-CRYPTO CRATE HAS NO SEAM AT ALL.** `git grep 'qsc_rng_failure_test_seam' -- tools/refimpl/**` returns **zero hits (exit 1)**; **POSITIVE CONTROL: `OsRng` occurs in 6 files there**, so the zero is real. `quantumshield_refimpl` is where `StdCrypto` lives — the actual primitives the client calls — and its **five product-code draws** are all in `crypto/stdcrypto.rs`: `:87` `ml_kem::MlKem768::generate(&mut OsRng)` (**ML-KEM-768 keypair**) · `:115` `OsRng.fill_bytes(seed)` (**ML-DSA-65 signing-key seed**) · `:171` `OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut sk_bytes)` (**the X25519 static secret**) · `:192` `.encapsulate(&mut OsRng)` (**KEM encapsulation**) · `:273` `random_nonce12`. The client's seam intercepts the **caller** of several of these by label and **never exercises a failure inside the primitive**.

⚠ **FIVE WRAPPED LABELS ARE NEVER FORCED BY ANY TEST, ALL AEAD NONCE DRAWS — THEY STAY DARK AFTER A GREEN RUN, AND THEY ARE CHEAP TO CLOSE** (five tests on a mechanism that already exists): `QSC.VAULT.INIT.NONCE` (⚠ the **vault envelope nonce** — the vault test forces `...INIT.SALT`, not this) · `QSC.VAULT.SECRET_SET.NONCE` · `QSC.VAULT.SECRET_SET_WITH_PASSPHRASE.NONCE` · `QSC.VAULT.SESSION_PERSIST.NONCE` · `QSC.QSP.SESSION_BLOB_NONCE`. **Product labels at which a failure can be injected: 22. Forced by at least one test: 17.**

### ENG-0267 — ⚠⚠ THE INITIATOR COMMITS THE SESSION **BEFORE** IT PUSHES THE SIGNED A2, SO ANY FAILURE IN THAT WINDOW — SIGNING, OR THE RELAY MERELY BEING UNREACHABLE — LEAVES HER WITH A STORED SESSION THE RESPONDER NEVER LEARNED OF — **NEW; FILED by NA-0773 (`D-1416`) as a DESIGN finding on the Director's `E-4`, from the SR-15 cold read's `F-2`. FILING ONLY — the cure is a protocol question and belongs to the messaging epic's design pass, not to this lane.**

- Severity: **UNKNOWN, and deliberately not graded.** Whether an initiator holding a session the responder never learned of is **accepted design or a defect** is an open PROTOCOL question this lane did not open. What is NOT unknown is that the window is **reachable in ordinary operation** — the relay being unreachable between the commit and the push needs no fault injection at all.
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `c6687bbdd19927e3f3ed3e0f63f8c1672b804730`.

**THE WINDOW, FROM THE TREE'S OWN WORDS.** The product commits the session **before** it signs and pushes A2. Test 19's source comment names it exactly: *"the initiator branch takes its early `Ok(())` AFTER the session commit and BEFORE the push."* When signing fails, **the session blob is written and pending is cleared while the peer has received nothing.**

⚠⚠ **AND THE TREE ALREADY PINS IT — HONESTLY, AND IN THE ONE PLACE NOBODY WAS LOOKING.** `a2_signature_provider_rng_failure.rs`'s test does **not forbid** the surviving partial write; it **pins** it, and its markers say so aloud: `NA0463_..._NO_FALSE_NO_MUTATION_CLAIM_OK` and `NA0463_..._POST_MUTATION_TIMING_ACKNOWLEDGED_OK`. ⛳ **The authors were honest**: they measured the mutation, refused to claim otherwise, and wrote a test that goes red if it silently changes. **That is good engineering and it is why this entry can be written at all.**

⚠⚠ **WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN A NOTE: THE CONSEQUENCE CHAIN.** The initiator's GUI reads the stored session as **"active"** (the `F10` chain); the responder stays **pending**; and **no frame exists for the delivery ladder to deliver**, because the A2 that would have carried it never left. ⇒ **the two peers disagree about whether they are connected, and nothing in the shipped system reconciles them.**

- ⚠ **THIS ENTRY IS AN INPUT TO THE MESSAGING EPIC, NOT A REPAIR ORDER.** It is filed **beside `ENG-0260`** (the cleartext handshake correlator, likewise a design finding for that epic) and is cross-referenced from `ENG-0250` / `ENG-0251`, the inviter-completion entries whose lane (`NA-0768`) owns the surrounding code.
- ⚠ **AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: A LIVE FAILURE ON THIS EXACT WINDOW IS FILED AT `ENG-0269`**, measured by NA-0773's own run of the repaired seam.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-30 by NA-0773 (`D-1416`).

### ENG-0269 — ⚠⚠⚠ **MEASURED, NOT REASONED: WHEN THE A2 SIGNATURE FAILS, THE INITIATOR COMMITS THE SESSION, EMITS `handshake_reject`, AND THEN ACKS THE FRAME ANYWAY — RETIRING FROM THE RELAY A FRAME WHOSE EFFECT NEVER HAPPENED** — **NEW; FILED by NA-0773 (`D-1416`) from ITS OWN RUN of the repaired seam. FILED, NOT REPAIRED — the Director's ruling is explicit that a failing assertion is filed with its severity argued from what it asserts.**

- Severity: **`P2`, ARGUED FROM WHAT THE ASSERTION ASSERTS AND OFFERED FOR RULING, NOT DECLARED.** The argument: a frame is **destroyed** (acked ⇒ retired from the relay) while the effect it was acked for **did not occur**; the two peers are left permanently disagreeing, and **no frame remains to retry from**. Against `P1`: it requires a failure inside a narrow window and no confidentiality is lost. Against `P3`: it is not cosmetic and it is **reachable without fault injection** — see `ENG-0267`, where the same window opens if the relay is merely unreachable. ⚠ **The severity is the Director's to set; this entry argues it and does not rule it.**
- Bases measured at: qsl-protocol main `c6687bbdd19927e3f3ed3e0f63f8c1672b804730`; the failure measured on NA-0773's impl commit `1fe8ac2ec95557e47596a03378f2f3c7805f0057`, which changes **one line inside the seam arm** and no product behaviour in any build.

⚠⚠ **THIS IS THE ONE OUTCOME NOBODY COULD PRICE IN ADVANCE, AND IT IS THE GOOD ONE.** The originating report named three ways turning the seam on could end: **(i)** all pass, **(ii)** tests drifted, **(iii)** *"the PRODUCT does not in fact fail safe under RNG failure — a real defect in fail-safe behaviour, found by the arms built to find it."* **The result is (iii), on exactly one of the 27.** The arm was written for this in NA-0742, was never able to run, and found it the first time it ran.

**THE MEASUREMENT.** `t8_the_a2_sig_failure_exit_emits_no_producer_ack`, in `qsl/qsl-client/qsc/tests/na0742_invite_finish_scan_producer_acks.rs`, forces `QSC_RNG_FAILURE_TEST_SEAM=QSC.SIG.A2` through `qsc invite finish`. **Both of its antecedent assertions PASSED**, so the exit under test was genuinely taken and the arm proves what it claims:
  · `handshake_reject reason=sig_sign_failed` **present** — the A2-signing exit was reached;
  · `handshake_complete` **absent** — the early exit was taken.
**THE ASSERTION THEN FAILED**, at `na0742_invite_finish_scan_producer_acks.rs:1462`:
```
assertion `left == right` failed: A FRAME WHOSE A2 NEVER LEFT MUST NOT BE ACKED. The session was
committed, but the peer received nothing; acking here would retire a frame whose effect never happened.
  left: 1
 right: 0
```
**The product's own markers, in the order it emitted them, are the whole case:**
```
QSC_MARK/1 event=session_store ok=true format=v3 enc=aead
QSC_MARK/1 event=handshake_reject reason=sig_sign_failed
QSC_MARK/1 event=relay_pull_diagnostic ... api=relay_pull_ack_v1 op=ack ack_mode=lease max=1 status_code=200 acked_count=1
QSC_MARK/1 event=producer_ack caller=finish sent=1 acked=1
```
⇒ **the session IS stored · the A2 signature FAILED · and the frame is ACKED regardless**, `acked_count=1` confirming the ack reached the relay.

⚠⚠ **CONTENTION RULED OUT UNDER A RULE WRITTEN BEFORE THE RE-RUN.** The rule, written first: *passes alone = contention; fails alone = real.* Re-run **alone and single-threaded** (`--exact --test-threads=1`, 11 filtered out): **FAILED again, exit 101, in 51.57s.** ⇒ **REAL.**

- ⚠ **IT CANNOT REDDEN ANY REQUIRED CHECK, AND THAT IS THE PROBLEM RESTATED, NOT A MITIGATION.** No CI job compiles `--cfg qsc_rng_failure_test_seam`, so the default build runs this file's `#[cfg(not(...))]` companion (`t8_the_rng_seam_is_absent_from_the_default_build`) instead. **The defect is invisible to every gate the project runs** — which is `ENG-0197`'s thesis, now demonstrated on a live defect rather than argued.
- ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY.** What is measured is that the frame **is acked** on this path. Whether the acked frame is thereby **unrecoverable** in the deployed relay is **not measured here** and is not claimed; the relay's retention and lease semantics bound it. The test's own words are the claim this entry rests on.
- Status: open — filed 2026-08-30 by NA-0773 (`D-1416`). **NOT REPAIRED IN THIS LANE**, per the Director's ruling, and no repair is proposed.

### WF-0093 — ⚠⚠ A cfg-GATED TEST SURFACE IS COMPILED BY NO CI JOB, AND A TEST WITH ZERO ASSERTIONS IS NOT A LINT FAILURE — THE TWO GAPS THAT LET 27 TESTS ROT FOR 46 DAYS AND 13 ASSERTION-FREE TESTS PASS INDEFINITELY — **NEW; FILED by NA-0773 (`D-1416`) as the CI-migration input the Director's ruling sec 4 orders. FILED, NOT BUILT — `.github/**` is outside this seat's authority and the committed `.claude/settings.json` denies writes there.**

- Type: workflow; Status: open — filed 2026-08-30 by NA-0773 (`D-1416`).
- **THE GROUND, ON THE CORRECTED FIGURES.** **27** gated tests (not 28 — the 28th gate covers a *helper*), of which **19 assert** and **8 are no-op marker fixtures**; of the 19, **16** pin the fail-safe property (`ENG-0197`). **None had ever executed.** The defect was **rediscovered and re-filed twice in twelve days** (`ENG-0197` 2026-08-17, `ENG-0256` 2026-08-29) and had existed for **46 days** at repair. ⇒ **a configuration no gate builds can rot unobserved, and this one did.**
- **THE TWO PROPOSALS, NEITHER BUILT HERE.** **(1) COMPILE THE CFG IN CI** — at minimum a job running `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg qsc_rng_failure_test_seam" cargo check -p qsc --tests`. ⚠ **Measured, so the proposal is priced rather than guessed:** at `1fe8ac2e` that command exits **0** in **20.85s** on a 6-core box. A *check* job, not a test job, is enough to stop the rot and costs almost nothing. **(2) A ZERO-ASSERTION TEST IS A LINT FAILURE** — the census at `ENG-0268` found **13** such tests across 939, **five of them green in every run today**. ⚠ The needle is the maintenance surface: it must resolve through the call graph and must know `prop_assert!`, `cmd.assert()` and turbofished `assert_*::<T>()`, all three of which produced false positives when this census was first run.
- ⚠ **AND A THIRD, SMALLER ONE, NAMED SO THE SET IS NOT NARROWER THAN THE PROBLEM:** running the seam suite in CI would ALSO have caught `ENG-0269` — the live defect this lane found — **on the day it was introduced**, instead of never.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0197` / `ENG-0256` (the rot); `ENG-0268` (the assertion-free species); `ENG-0269` (what the gate would have caught); `ENG-0230` (another gate that cannot see what it is supposed to gate); `D-0883` (the seam's authorising record, which requires the cfg be non-default — the gate must therefore be additive, never a default-build change).

### ENG-0270 — the contacts list could not scroll: `#contacts-rows` carried no CSS rule at all and `.list-pane` no `min-height`, so 30 contacts made the pane 1496px tall inside a 673px window and every row below the fold was unreachable with no scrollbar to reach it — **NEW; FILED AND CLOSED by NA-0774 (`D-1417`, desktop `D-0045`).**

- Severity: **`P3`** — no data is lost or exposed and nothing fails unsafely; the defect is that a shipped surface becomes unusable past the fold. Argued, not declared.
- ⚠ **IT EXISTED ONLY IN AN OPERATOR PACKET UNTIL THIS LANE** (the `D-1` / `R331.1` shape): a defect the operator had reported and no ledger row carried. Filing it is half the point of the lane.
- **MEASURED IN THE RUNNING APP BEFORE ANY CHANGE**, 30 injected rows at desktop main `0a908099`: `#contacts-rows` `scrollHeight` 1410 == `clientHeight` 1410 (no clipping — it simply grew), `.list-pane` `clientHeight` 1496 against `window.innerHeight` 673, computed `overflow-y: visible`, computed `min-height: auto`.
- ⚠⚠ **THE CURE IS TWO RULES AND THE SECOND IS NOT OPTIONAL — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** The brief asked for one rule. `overflow-y` on the rows container ALONE was driven and measured: the declaration **applied** (computed `overflow-y` went `visible` → `auto`) and the defect was **unchanged** (rows 1410, pane 1496, `scrollHeight == clientHeight` still). `.list-pane` is a GRID ITEM of `.main-layout`, and a grid item's default `min-height: auto` refuses to shrink below its content, so the pane grew and handed the rows container a 1410px box to "scroll" in. With `min-height: 0` on the pane as well: rows client 556, pane 642 ≤ 673, `scrollHeight > clientHeight`.
- Red arm printed: reverting both rules fails `na0774_gui_o_contacts_scroll` at `expected "scrolls" / measured "NO-SCROLL scroll=1410 client=1410"`, rc=101.
- ⚠ **CLAIM BOUNDARY.** Two of the brief's three assertions do **not** discriminate at the harness window size and are kept as no-regression guards, not as proof: the heading was already in view in the red state (the pane grows downward, the header sits above it), and the window is not resized on `scr-main`. The arm that carries the red is `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, joined by this lane's added assertion that the pane fits the window.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0271` (the other packet-only defect this lane filed); desktop `D-0045`.
- Source: NA-0774 `D-1417`; measured at desktop main `0a908099`.

### ENG-0271 — the "Working…" busy indicator flashed on every liveness beat forever: the tick's scan makes **four** IPC calls per beat with nothing to do, and `invoke()` showed the indicator on every one — **NEW; FILED AND CLOSED by NA-0774 (`D-1417`, desktop `D-0045`).**

- Severity: **`P3`** — cosmetic in effect, but continuous and unavoidable on an idle unlocked screen, and it trains a user to ignore the one signal the app has for "a human is waiting".
- ⚠ **ALSO PACKET-ONLY UNTIL THIS LANE**, the same `D-1` / `R331.1` shape as `ENG-0270`.
- **THE ENUMERATION, WHICH THE CURE HAD TO COVER ALL OF.** Reachable from `relayScan` when `ev.source === "tick"`, traced from bytes: `setInterval` (`ui/main.js:1995`) → `relayScan` → `relayScanOnce` (`:3406`) → `SCAN_CLASSES` (`:3385`) = `[finishScanClass, autoConnectClass]`. Six commands: `relay_config_get` (both classes, once each per beat), `contact_list` (once), `invite_list` (once), `connect_status` (per contact row), `invite_finish` (per eligible row), `invite_accept` (per due invite).
- ⚠⚠ **THE PER-BEAT FLOOR IS FOUR CALLS AND IT IS UNCONDITIONAL**: each class opens with an unguarded `relay_config_get`, then — the relay being configured, which the tick gate already requires — an unguarded `contact_list` / `invite_list`. Four IPC calls every beat with zero contacts, zero invites and nothing whatever to do.
- **THE CURE AND WHY IT SITS WHERE IT DOES.** A depth-counted flag raised around `relayScanOnce` when `ev.source === "tick"`. **Scoped to the PASS, not to `relayScan`**: a scan's rerun can carry a **different source** than the pass that started it (`relayScan` stores the pending event and replays it through a second `relayScanOnce(next)`), so a flag scoped to `relayScan` would silence a **user-sourced rerun**. Scoped to the pass, quietness follows `ev.source`, which is the thing that actually decides it.
- **OPERATOR-RULED AND UNCHANGED:** suppression is for tick-sourced calls ONLY. "Suppress always" was refused — the indicator earns its keep where a human is waiting.
- Red arm printed: reverting the guard fails `na0774_gui_p_tick_quiet_busy` at `expected "quiet" / measured "UNHID 2 time(s) under a tick"`, rc=101, **with the positive control still PASSING in that same red run** — so the observer is known to work and the green arm's silence means something.
- ⚠ **STATED BOUND, NOT DESIGNED AROUND.** `await` yields, so a **user-sourced call made during one of the pass's awaits is also suppressed**. The window is one scan pass. Eliminating it needs per-call context the platform does not provide without threading the source through both scan-class signatures and all six call sites, where **missing one is silent**. Recorded as a known bound.
- ⚠ **COUPLED CONSEQUENCE, ALREADY RULED:** once the tick is silent, the footer's declined-frame notice is the only visible evidence of background activity — see `ENG-0274`, which is not built in this lane.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0270`; `ENG-0274` (the footer notice); desktop `D-0045`.
- Source: NA-0774 `D-1417`; measured at desktop main `0a908099`.

### ENG-0272 — the Settings ▸ Identity pane told a user who HAS an identity that they have none, and invited them to "finish setup", whenever `identity_show` merely threw — **NEW; FILED AND CLOSED by NA-0774 (`D-1417`, desktop `D-0045`). Raised as escalation `E5` at NA-0768 and accepted by ruling.**

- Severity: **`P2`, argued.** It is a **false statement about identity state on the identity surface**, and it invites an action that is wrong for the user's actual state. Against `P1`: nothing is destroyed and no secret is exposed. Against `P3`: it is not cosmetic — a user acting on it would attempt to create an identity they already have.
- **THE MEASUREMENT**, `ui/main.js:930-941` at desktop main `0a908099` before the fix: `refreshIdentityPane` wrapped `await invoke("identity_show")` in `try { … } catch (_) { /* treated as absent below */ }` and then branched on `if (!rec)`. **A thrown error and a genuinely absent identity reached that branch identically.** The branch reveals `#identity-empty`, whose text is, verbatim from `ui/index.html:232`: *"No identity exists yet — finish setup to create one."* `#identity-empty` had **exactly one** reference in `ui/main.js`, so that branch was its only writer.
- **THE CURE:** two distinct states. `readFailed` separates the causes; a new `#identity-read-error` element carries *"Couldn't read your identity. Try again."*, naming **retry** and never setup; both states are driven from the same condition so they can neither both show nor both hide, and the success path clears both.
- ⚠⚠ **THE ERROR PATH IS NOT DRIVEN END-TO-END ANYWHERE, AND THAT IS A REAL LIMIT, NOT A FORMALITY.** Making `identity_show` throw needs the IPC layer, and NA-0768 measured that `window.__TAURI__.core` is **FROZEN** — `invoke` is non-writable and non-configurable, so a scenario cannot patch it **at any delay** (driven at 1500 ms and at 10 s; both left the flow green). The three unit seals in `src-tauri/tests/na0774_identity_error_state.rs` prove **both branches exist and are distinct in the shipped bytes**. What no test in this repository proves is the rendered result of a real `identity_show` rejection.
- Red arm printed: reverting the branch and the element fails all three seals, rc=101.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0273` (the same display-honesty class, one surface over); desktop `D-0045`.
- Source: NA-0774 `D-1417`; escalated at NA-0768 STOP 016.

### ENG-0279 — the gui-driver harness reddened **three** times in one arc on non-attributable, wall-clock-shaped failures, all of one class — a scenario asserting on an element written behind an `await` with no precondition — and only the `#settings-code` instance of that class has been swept — **NEW; FILED by NA-0774 (`D-1417`); the two known instances are CLOSED, the CLASS is not.**

- Severity: **`P2`, argued.** A gate that reddens for reasons unrelated to the change under test teaches its readers to re-run rather than investigate, and this arc paid roughly three review cycles to it. It also **hid a real question for a full act**: whether main's red was a race or a genuine empty is still not settled.
- **THE THREE REDS:** desktop `#46` (flow `k`), `#47` (flow `g`), and main's push run `33364026983` at `ac03da05` (flow `i`) — different flows, different PRs, none attributable to the change it reddened.
- **THE CURE THAT SHIPPED, AND ITS EVIDENCE:** a `poll_exec` precondition that waits on the **element's state**, never on wall-clock, added to flow `g` and `k` by `#48` and to flow `i` by `#49`. It cannot mask a product defect: on budget exhaustion `op_poll_exec` calls `self.step(…, False)` (`src-tauri/tests/harness/runner.py:311-313`), so a never-populating element still goes RED, at a **labelled** step carrying the last value seen. Proven by injected A/B on each flow: uncured `rc=101` → cured `rc=0`.
- ⛳ **AND THE RACE THEN FIRED ON ITS OWN, UNSIMULATED, ON `#49`'s OWN CI RUN**: `STEP poll_exec settings_code_populated PASS measured='true after 2 poll(s)'` — the first read returned not-30-digits, the loop waited, the second returned 30. That is the production mechanism absorbed by the cure, and it is the evidence the PR greens alone could not supply.
- ⚠⚠ **THE CLASS IS NOT SWEPT AND THAT IS THIS ENTRY'S POINT.** Only `#settings-code` has been enumerated and guarded (a census over all 14 scenarios found exactly two readers, both now cured). **Every other element written behind an `await` and asserted without a precondition is the same defect unfound.** A class-shaped sweep is owed and is not this lane's.
- ⚠ **AND THE DESKTOP REPOSITORY HAS NO RED-MAIN ISSUE AUTOMATION.** Measured by the operator: zero open issues after a red push run on `main`. The protocol repository has it. So a red main on the desktop side is noticed only if a human happens to look — which is how `ENG-0270`'s and `ENG-0271`'s originating packet sat unfiled, and how this arc's third red was found by a Director census rather than by a gate.
- ⚠ **THE HARNESS CANNOT SIMULATE THIS FAULT AT ITS OWN MECHANISM.** `window.__TAURI__.core` is FROZEN (`invoke` non-writable, non-configurable), so an IPC-timing fault cannot be injected from a scenario at any delay; the delayed-repopulate injection is the only instrument available for the class, and it is a **different mechanism** than the real fault. Stated as a standing limit under `PR-18`.
- Cross-references: `ENG-0272` (the frozen-IPC limit again, from the other side); `ENG-0280`.
- Source: NA-0774 `D-1417`; measured across NA-0768 and this lane.

### ENG-0280 — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` documents the required-context set **inverted**: it calls the required leak-scanning gate "advisory" and lists a non-required job among the required three — **NEW; FILED by NA-0774 (`D-1417`); the repair is drafted and is the OPERATOR's to apply.**

- Severity: **`P2`, argued, and the argument is the whole entry.** `infra-literal-scan` is the gate that scans the tracked tree and a PR's added lines for **leaked private keys, cloud tokens and operator infrastructure literals** — the gate that exists because earlier PRs published a private LAN address. **It IS required.** The file tells every reader the opposite, in bold: *"⚠ WHAT IS ACTUALLY ADVISORY IS THE NEW `infra-literal-scan` CONTEXT ABOVE: it runs and reports on every PR, but it is NOT in the required set yet"*. Someone who sees that context red, opens the workflow to learn what it is, and reads "advisory", may **merge past a red leak scan**. That reaches privacy and secrets.
- **MEASURED AT THE LIVE GATE** (desktop `main`, `0a908099`): `required_status_checks.contexts = ["rust", "advisories", "infra-literal-scan"]`, `strict = true`. Required: `rust`, `advisories`, `infra-literal-scan`. **NOT** required, though both run and report: `public-safety`, `gui-driver`.
- ⚠ **IT IS THE COMMENT'S OWN STATED FAILURE MODE, INVERTED.** Twenty lines above, the same block says: *"A comment that understates a gate is worse than none, because it invites someone to merge past a red they were told was advisory."* That sentence now describes itself. And the block misdescribes the **other** gate in the opposite direction, listing `public-safety` among the required three when it is not required — so a reader is told a non-blocking gate blocks, and a blocking gate does not.
- ⚠ **THE CAUSE IS NOT BAD AUTHORSHIP, AND NAMING IT MATTERS.** The block documents a three-step sequence: *"1. this PR merges; 2. the OPERATOR adds `infra-literal-scan` to the required set and removes `public-safety` from it; 3. a later lane deletes this now-redundant job."* **Step 2 has since happened.** The comment was true when written and was invalidated by the operator act it itself prescribed. **Step 3 is ripe and unclaimed.**
- ⚠⚠ **A FILE CANNOT STATE ITS OWN BRANCH PROTECTION.** This lane's own seat took the required set from that comment and published it wrongly in NA-0768 STOP 016 §3f before catching it by re-measurement. The standing correction: read the gate, never the description of the gate — `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --jq .required_status_checks` — and note the set is **base-scoped**.
- ⚠ **NOT REPAIRED HERE.** `.github/**` is operator-only. Two comment replacements are drafted in this lane's stop, both proven **comment-only** by comparing the **parsed** YAML documents with a positive control; the deletion of the redundant `public-safety` job is batched with them by amendment. ⚠ **Before that deletion, re-measure the required set at that commit's base**: deleting a job whose name IS in the required set leaves a required context that never reports and blocks every pull request indefinitely (the NA-0653 failure).
- Cross-references: `ENG-0279` (the other CI-truth defect this lane filed); `D-1417`.
- Source: NA-0774 `D-1417`; escalated as `E6` at NA-0768 STOP 017 and accepted by ruling.
- Status: CLOSED 2026-09-03 by NA-0778 (`D-1421`; `RULING_NA0778_001` R4(iii)) -- closed by desktop PR #51 ("ENG-0280: ci.yml comment truth + public-safety job deletion"), merge `83019356` (base `b6d9237a`, head `e591cce4`), merged_at 2026-09-02T02:50:11Z read at the edit; the landed cure is `.github/workflows/ci.yml` at desktop main `2411bf9f`, sha256 `8d89373e6de596c200233448e9ada23676af42bc084f273f06702f81e9e62ecc` (161 lines), byte-identical to the candidate NA-0776 banked.
